label: Volume & Vibrations
statement: Demonstrate the “Volume & Vibrations” objective: Find patterns between the volume of a sound and the strength of the vibrations that produced it.
subject: Science

label: Motors & the Motor Effect
statement: Demonstrate the “Motors & the Motor Effect” objective: Explain the motor effect as the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field, and describe how this principle is used in electric motors and loudspeakers.
subject: Science

label: How minibeasts move
statement: Demonstrate the “How minibeasts move” objective: How minibeasts move: crawling (ants, beetles), flying (butterflies, bees), slithering (worms, slugs), jumping (grasshoppers, fleas), burrowing (earthworms). Counting legs as a first step toward grouping creatures.
subject: Science

label: Needs & Wants
statement: Demonstrate the “Needs & Wants” objective: The difference between things we need (food, shelter, clothing) and things we want (toys, treats); that we sometimes have to choose because money is limited.
subject: Life Skills

label: Classifying Ocean Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Classifying Ocean Animals” objective: Classify ocean animals into major groups: fish (breathe through gills, have scales), marine mammals (breathe air, warm-blooded, feed milk), and invertebrates (no backbone — jellyfish, octopuses, crabs, starfish).
subject: Science

label: AI and the Future of Work
statement: Demonstrate the “AI and the Future of Work” objective: How AI is changing the world of work: some jobs disappear, new ones are created, many change; jobs AI can't do (yet); what skills matter in an AI world.
subject: Computing

label: Bias in AI Systems
statement: Demonstrate the “Bias in AI Systems” objective: If training data is biased, AI will be biased; examples: facial recognition working better for some skin tones, translation assuming gender; where bias comes from and whether we can fix it.
subject: Computing

label: Sorting and Identifying Minibeasts
statement: Demonstrate the “Sorting and Identifying Minibeasts” objective: Using classification keys to identify minibeasts. Branching yes/no questions: 'Does it have legs?' → 'How many legs?' → 'Does it have wings?' Dichotomous keys as a systematic tool for sorting and identifying creatures.
subject: Science

label: Decimal place value
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimal place value” objective: Round decimals to any place using place-value understanding; round any whole number to a required degree of accuracy.
subject: Mathematics

label: Reading Inflectional Endings
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading Inflectional Endings” objective: Read words containing taught GPCs with common inflectional endings (-s, -es, -ing, -ed, -er, -est) and the prefix un-; read multi-syllable words with taught patterns.
subject: English

label: Threats to insects and conservation
statement: Demonstrate the “Threats to insects and conservation” objective: Threats to insects and conservation: insect populations are declining worldwide. Causes include habitat loss, pesticide use, light pollution disrupting nocturnal insects, and climate change. Pollinator decline threatens food production. What children can do: plant pollinator-friendly gardens, reduce pesticide use, participate in citizen science like the Big Butterfly Count.
subject: Science

label: Comparing groups: more or fewer
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing groups: more or fewer” objective: Compare two groups of objects to determine which has more, fewer, or whether they are equal, using matching and counting strategies.
subject: Mathematics

label: Using Mathematical Structure
statement: Demonstrate the “Using Mathematical Structure” objective: Look for and use mathematical structure: exploit place-value patterns for ×10/×100, use the distributive property to break apart multiplications, apply fraction equivalence to compare and compute, use shape properties to classify quadrilaterals.
subject: Mathematics

label: Growth Through Adversity
statement: Demonstrate the “Growth Through Adversity” objective: Understand that facing serious challenges can lead to genuine growth in three domains: new perspectives on life, improved relationships, and a strengthened sense of personal capability (post-traumatic growth); distinguish genuine growth from toxic positivity ('everything happens for a reason') and from denial; understand that resilience does not mean being unaffected by adversity but recovering and growing through it; develop a personal philosophy for handling setbacks based on meaning-making; explore how to support others going through serious difficulty without minimising their experience.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Seismic Waves & Earth's Interior
statement: Demonstrate the “Seismic Waves & Earth's Interior” objective: Distinguish between P-waves (compression, travel through solids and liquids) and S-waves (shear, cannot pass through liquids); explain why a seismic shadow zone exists on the far side of an earthquake; describe how seismologists use wave refraction and reflection to infer that Earth has a solid inner core, liquid outer core, mantle, and crust.
subject: Science

label: Blending Sounds to Read Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Blending Sounds to Read Words” objective: Apply phonic knowledge to blend sounds in unfamiliar words containing taught grapheme-phoneme correspondences; respond speedily to graphemes for all 40+ phonemes.
subject: English

label: The Future of AI
statement: Demonstrate the “The Future of AI” objective: What AI might do in 10 years; what we want it to do and what we're worried about; children as future designers and decision-makers about AI; hopeful, empowered framing.
subject: Computing

label: Writing to inform
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing to inform” objective: Compose informative or explanatory texts using drawing, dictating, or writing that name a topic and supply some information about it.
subject: English

label: Telling time to the minute
statement: Demonstrate the “Telling time to the minute” objective: Measure and begin to record time in hours, minutes, and seconds.
subject: Mathematics

label: Fall of the Roman Republic
statement: Demonstrate the “Fall of the Roman Republic” objective: Trace how Roman political violence — the murder of the Gracchi brothers, civil wars between Marius and Sulla, Caesar's crossing of the Rubicon and assassination on the Ides of March, and the final war between Octavian and Antony — destroyed the Republic and led to one-man rule under Augustus, and debate whether the fall of the Republic was inevitable or a series of choices.
subject: History

label: Step-by-Step Instructions
statement: Demonstrate the “Step-by-Step Instructions” objective: Step-by-step instructions for everyday tasks (making a sandwich, brushing teeth); that if instructions are wrong or missing, things go wrong; computers follow instructions exactly.
subject: Computing

label: Earthquake Safety
statement: Demonstrate the “Earthquake Safety” objective: Know basic earthquake safety: drop, cover, and hold on; move away from windows; tell a trusted adult.
subject: Science

label: Egyptian Art and Architecture
statement: Demonstrate the “Egyptian Art and Architecture” objective: Analyse Egyptian art and architecture: understand that Egyptian paintings followed strict conventions (people shown from the side with eyes from the front, size indicating importance), that tomb and temple design evolved from mastabas to step pyramids to smooth pyramids to rock-cut temples like Abu Simbel, and that obelisks, colossal statues, and temples like Karnak demonstrated the pharaoh's power and devotion to the gods.
subject: History

label: Place Value Problem-Solving
statement: Demonstrate the “Place Value Problem-Solving” objective: Solve number and practical problems involving place value with increasingly large positive numbers.
subject: Mathematics

label: Fluent adding and subtracting within 20
statement: Demonstrate the “Fluent adding and subtracting within 20” objective: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies; know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.
subject: Mathematics

label: Fluent adding and subtracting within 10
statement: Demonstrate the “Fluent adding and subtracting within 10” objective: Fluently add and subtract within 10.
subject: Mathematics

label: Hurricanes, Tornadoes & Monsoons
statement: Demonstrate the “Hurricanes, Tornadoes & Monsoons” objective: Explain how hurricanes form and intensify over warm ocean water (latent heat release, low-pressure spiral); describe tornado formation within supercell thunderstorms; explain monsoon mechanics driven by temperature differences between land and sea; introduce attribution science — how scientists use climate models to calculate whether and by how much climate change increased the probability or intensity of a specific extreme weather event.
subject: Science

label: Two written numerals between 1 and 10
statement: Demonstrate the “Two written numerals between 1 and 10” objective: Compare two written numerals between 1 and 10 to determine which is greater or less.
subject: Mathematics

label: Rainforest Layers
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Layers” objective: Know that a rainforest has four layers from ground to sky — the forest floor (dark, damp, full of decomposing leaves), the understory (small trees and shrubs in the shade), the canopy (a thick roof of treetops where most animals live), and the emergent layer (the tallest trees poking above the canopy into bright sunlight).
subject: Science

label: Comparing Structure in Information Texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing Structure in Information Texts” objective: Compare and contrast the overall structure of events, ideas, concepts, or information in two or more informational texts, identifying patterns such as chronology, comparison, cause/effect, or problem/solution.
subject: English

label: Drawing Ray Diagrams
statement: Demonstrate the “Drawing Ray Diagrams” objective: Draw ray diagrams to show reflection at a plane mirror (angle of incidence = angle of reflection) and refraction at a boundary between media; use ray diagrams to locate images and explain how lenses and mirrors work.
subject: Science

label: Plotting Linear Graphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Plotting Linear Graphs” objective: Plot linear graphs by generating a table of values, reduce a two-variable linear equation to the form y = mx + c, and calculate gradients from two points on a line.
subject: Mathematics

label: Measuring Liquids & Masses
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring Liquids & Masses” objective: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using grams, kilograms, and litres; solve one-step word problems involving mass or volume.
subject: Mathematics

label: Experimental vs Theoretical
statement: Demonstrate the “Experimental vs Theoretical” objective: Run repeated probability experiments and compare experimental (relative frequency) results with theoretical predictions; understand and demonstrate that as the number of trials increases, the experimental probability tends towards the theoretical probability — and that short runs can give very different results.
subject: Mathematics

label: Probability as a Fraction
statement: Demonstrate the “Probability as a Fraction” objective: Describe the probability of simple equally-likely outcomes using unit fractions: the probability of rolling a 6 on a fair die is 1/6, flipping heads is 1/2, picking one specific colour from three equally represented colours is 1/3; place these fractional probabilities on a 0-to-1 probability scale.
subject: Mathematics

label: Paraphrasing What You Hear
statement: Demonstrate the “Paraphrasing What You Hear” objective: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats, capturing the key ideas accurately in one's own words.
subject: English

label: Adding and subtracting (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding and subtracting (age 9+)” objective: Solve addition and subtraction multi-step problems in contexts, deciding which operations and methods to use and why.
subject: Mathematics

label: Finding patterns in data
statement: Demonstrate the “Finding patterns in data” objective: Analyse and interpret data from maps to describe patterns of Earth's features, recognising that many features result from processes that occur over long periods.
subject: Science

label: How the Eye Works
statement: Demonstrate the “How the Eye Works” objective: Describe how the eye works: light enters through the pupil, the lens focuses it onto the retina at the back of the eye, and the retina sends signals along the optic nerve to the brain, which interprets the image.
subject: Science

label: What Is a Half?
statement: Demonstrate the “What Is a Half?” objective: Recognise, find, and name a half as one of two equal parts of an object, shape, or quantity.
subject: Mathematics

label: Plate Boundaries
statement: Demonstrate the “Plate Boundaries” objective: Explain how plate boundaries cause earthquakes and volcanoes: plates pushing together, pulling apart, or sliding past each other create the forces that trigger these events, and mountains form where plates collide.
subject: Science

label: Punctuating Direct Speech
statement: Demonstrate the “Punctuating Direct Speech” objective: Punctuate direct speech using inverted commas (speech marks), understanding that direct speech records the exact words spoken and must be enclosed in punctuation marks.
subject: English

label: Relative Motion
statement: Demonstrate the “Relative Motion” objective: Explain relative motion — how the apparent speed and direction of an object depends on the observer's own motion — using everyday examples such as trains and cars passing.
subject: Science

label: Friction & Surfaces
statement: Demonstrate the “Friction & Surfaces” objective: Compare how things move on different surfaces, noticing that some surfaces create more friction than others.
subject: Science

label: Measuring mass and weight (age 4+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring mass and weight (age 4+)” objective: Compare two objects directly by mass or weight and describe the difference using language such as heavy, light, heavier than, lighter than.
subject: Mathematics

label: Why circuit components behave differently
statement: Demonstrate the “Why circuit components behave differently” objective: Compare and give reasons for variations in how circuit components function, including brightness of bulbs, loudness of buzzers, and switch positions.
subject: Science

label: Extinction & Rapid Change
statement: Demonstrate the “Extinction & Rapid Change” objective: Explain how environmental change can outpace a species' ability to adapt through natural selection, leading to extinction, using historical and contemporary examples.
subject: Science

label: How Telescopes Work
statement: Demonstrate the “How Telescopes Work” objective: Know that telescopes are instruments that help us see distant objects in space, and that space telescopes like Hubble and James Webb orbit above Earth’s atmosphere to get clearer views of the universe.
subject: Science

label: Grammar Terms: Modal Verbs and Clauses
statement: Demonstrate the “Grammar Terms: Modal Verbs and Clauses” objective: Know and use Year 5 grammar terminology accurately when discussing reading and writing: modal verb, relative pronoun, relative clause, parenthesis, bracket, dash, cohesion, ambiguity.
subject: English

label: What Causes Wind
statement: Demonstrate the “What Causes Wind” objective: Understand what causes wind: the Sun heats the Earth's surface unevenly, warm air rises because it is lighter, and cooler air rushes in to take its place — this movement of air is wind.
subject: Science

label: Adding fractions (different denominators)
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding fractions (different denominators)” objective: Add and subtract fractions with denominators that are multiples of the same number by finding a common denominator.
subject: Mathematics

label: How Animals Have Babies
statement: Demonstrate the “How Animals Have Babies” objective: Know that different animals have their babies in different ways — some lay eggs (birds, reptiles, fish, insects), some give birth to live young (most mammals) — and that babies may look like miniature adults or look very different from their parents.
subject: Science

label: Ordering Events in Time
statement: Demonstrate the “Ordering Events in Time” objective: Sequence events in chronological order using language such as before, after, next, first, today, yesterday, tomorrow, morning, afternoon, evening.
subject: Mathematics

label: Sun-Driven Weather Systems
statement: Demonstrate the “Sun-Driven Weather Systems” objective: Understand how the Sun drives weather: the Sun heats Earth's surface unevenly (land heats faster than water, equator gets more heat than poles), creating differences in air pressure that cause wind patterns, ocean currents, and large-scale weather systems.
subject: Science

label: Rock layers and Earth's history
statement: Demonstrate the “Rock layers and Earth's history” objective: Interpret cross-section diagrams of the Earth's interior, geological strata, and rock cycle; read and label layers (crust, mantle, outer core, inner core); understand that deeper layers in sedimentary sequences are older.
subject: Science

label: Joining Letters
statement: Demonstrate the “Joining Letters” objective: Begin to join letters using diagonal and horizontal strokes, understanding which letter pairs are best left unjoined, forming letters of correct size relative to one another.
subject: English

label: Camouflage, warning colours, and mimicry
statement: Demonstrate the “Camouflage, warning colours, and mimicry” objective: Camouflage, warning colours, and mimicry: how insects survive by hiding or sending visual signals. Stick insects look like twigs, leaf insects look like leaves. Wasps have warning stripes; hoverflies mimic wasps but are harmless. The 'can you spot it?' challenge.
subject: Science

label: Understanding fractions (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding fractions (age 9+)” objective: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b (e.g. 3/5 = 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5).
subject: Mathematics

label: Matter Cycling in Ecosystems
statement: Demonstrate the “Matter Cycling in Ecosystems” objective: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment in an ecosystem.
subject: Science

label: Seeds & Plant Growth
statement: Demonstrate the “Seeds & Plant Growth” objective: Observe and describe how seeds and bulbs grow into mature plants through stages of germination and growth.
subject: Science

label: Finite Resources & Recycling
statement: Demonstrate the “Finite Resources & Recycling” objective: Explain that many raw materials (metals, fossil fuels, minerals) are finite resources, describe the environmental costs of extraction, and evaluate the benefits of recycling and the circular economy.
subject: Science

label: Habits and Motivation
statement: Demonstrate the “Habits and Motivation” objective: Understand habit formation through the cue-routine-reward loop and how to design new habits intentionally; distinguish intrinsic motivation (doing something for its own value) from extrinsic motivation (rewards/punishments) and understand when each is more effective; understand procrastination as primarily an emotion regulation problem (avoiding discomfort) rather than a time management failure; apply self-determination theory (autonomy, competence, relatedness) to boost intrinsic motivation; design environments that reduce friction for desired behaviours.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Robin Hood & King Arthur
statement: Demonstrate the “Robin Hood & King Arthur” objective: The legends of Robin Hood (Sherwood Forest, stealing from the rich, Merry Men) and King Arthur (Round Table, Excalibur, Camelot); that these are stories, not proven history, but reflect medieval values.
subject: History

label: Recommending Books
statement: Demonstrate the “Recommending Books” objective: Recommend books to peers, giving reasons for choices based on knowledge of a wide range of genres, authors, and themes, and making comparisons within and across books.
subject: English

label: Digestion & Enzymes
statement: Demonstrate the “Digestion & Enzymes” objective: Describe the organs of the human digestive system and how food is physically and chemically digested, including the role of enzymes as biological catalysts.
subject: Science

label: Fronted Adverbials and Commas
statement: Demonstrate the “Fronted Adverbials and Commas” objective: Use fronted adverbials to vary sentence openings and punctuate them with commas.
subject: English

label: Global Trade
statement: Demonstrate the “Global Trade” objective: Why countries trade with each other; imports and exports; how goods travel around the world; that different countries use different currencies.
subject: Life Skills

label: DNA & Genes
statement: Demonstrate the “DNA & Genes” objective: Describe the double helix structure of DNA (base pairs, complementarity), explain how genes are sections of DNA that code for proteins, introduce the central dogma (DNA → mRNA → protein) conceptually, and discuss the ethical implications of CRISPR gene editing — including potential benefits (genetic disease treatment) and concerns (germline editing, 'designer babies').
subject: Science

label: Changing Scientific Knowledge
statement: Demonstrate the “Changing Scientific Knowledge” objective: Evaluate competing scientific explanations about dinosaurs by weighing fossil evidence — understanding that scientific knowledge changes as new fossils are discovered and new methods of analysis are developed.
subject: Science

label: Where Rainforests Are
statement: Demonstrate the “Where Rainforests Are” objective: Know that rainforests are found in a belt around the middle of the Earth — in South America (the Amazon), Central Africa (the Congo), and Southeast Asia — and that they appear on every continent except Antarctica and Europe.
subject: Science

label: Odd and even numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Odd and even numbers” objective: Recognise odd and even numbers.
subject: Mathematics

label: Good Stress and Bad Stress
statement: Demonstrate the “Good Stress and Bad Stress” objective: Distinguish between eustress (the productive, motivating kind of stress) and distress (harmful, overwhelming stress); explain the physiological stress response (fight-flight-freeze, HPA axis) and how chronic stress affects the body and mind; identify common adolescent stressors (academic pressure, social comparison, physical change, uncertainty about the future); evaluate evidence-based coping strategies (exercise, sleep, mindfulness, social support, expressive writing); recognise warning signs that stress has crossed into anxiety or depression and know where to get help.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Factors, multiples, and primes (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Factors, multiples, and primes (age 9+)” objective: Solve problems involving multiplication and division using knowledge of factors, multiples, squares, and cubes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Commas After Introductory Elements
statement: Demonstrate the “Commas After Introductory Elements” objective: Use a comma to separate an introductory element from the rest of the sentence, including introductory words, phrases, and clauses.
subject: English

label: Telling Time: Hours and Half Hours
statement: Demonstrate the “Telling Time: Hours and Half Hours” objective: Tell the time to the hour and half past the hour, and draw clock hands to show these times.
subject: Mathematics

label: Desert Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Desert Animals” objective: Explore animals of the desert — camels, fennec foxes, scorpions, rattlesnakes, meerkats — and understand how desert animals survive extreme heat and lack of water through being active at night, storing water or fat, burrowing underground during the day, and having large ears to lose heat.
subject: Science

label: Herbivores, Carnivores & Omnivores
statement: Demonstrate the “Herbivores, Carnivores & Omnivores” objective: Classify common animals as carnivores (eat meat), herbivores (eat plants), or omnivores (eat both).
subject: Science

label: Marathon and Thermopylae
statement: Demonstrate the “Marathon and Thermopylae” objective: Describe the battles of Marathon and Thermopylae as moments when Greek city-states united against the invading Persian Empire — the runner Pheidippides bringing news of victory at Marathon (origin of the marathon race), and the heroic stand of 300 Spartans at Thermopylae — and understand these wars were fought to defend Greek independence.
subject: History

label: Decoding unfamiliar words
statement: Demonstrate the “Decoding unfamiliar words” objective: Read Y3-4 exception words with unusual spelling-sound correspondences, applying growing knowledge of morphology and etymology to decode unfamiliar exception words.
subject: English

label: Adding Fractions (Unlike Denominators)
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding Fractions (Unlike Denominators)” objective: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions to produce a common denominator.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Moon's Orbit
statement: Demonstrate the “The Moon's Orbit” objective: Know that the Moon orbits Earth approximately once a month, that it does not make its own light but reflects sunlight, and that its changing appearance (phases) is caused by how much of the sunlit side we can see from Earth.
subject: Science

label: Angles in triangles (age 12+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Angles in triangles (age 12+)” objective: Know and use the criteria for triangle congruence (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS), use standard labelling conventions for sides and angles of triangle ABC, and determine whether two triangles are congruent.
subject: Mathematics

label: Written Multiplication
statement: Demonstrate the “Written Multiplication” objective: Multiply two-digit and three-digit numbers by a one-digit number using formal written layout.
subject: Mathematics

label: Regular Plural Nouns
statement: Demonstrate the “Regular Plural Nouns” objective: Form and use regular plural nouns orally and in writing by adding -s or -es; understand that plural means more than one.
subject: English

label: Numbers on a number line
statement: Demonstrate the “Numbers on a number line” objective: Represent whole numbers as lengths on a number line and represent sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.
subject: Mathematics

label: Ancient life vs today
statement: Demonstrate the “Ancient life vs today” objective: Compare how children in ancient Greece or Rome lived with how children live today — including differences in school (writing on wax tablets, learning to fight in Sparta), food (olives, bread, grapes), games, and clothing (tunics and sandals) — and understand these civilisations existed thousands of years ago.
subject: History

label: Scale and similar shapes (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Scale and similar shapes (age 11+)” objective: Use scale factors to interpret and create scale diagrams and maps, calculating real-life distances from map measurements and vice versa.
subject: Mathematics

label: Fossilised Dinosaur Dung
statement: Demonstrate the “Fossilised Dinosaur Dung” objective: Describe what coprolites are (fossilised dinosaur dung) and how palaeontologists analyse them to discover what dinosaurs ate, including plant fragments, bones, and seeds.
subject: Science

label: Critical comparison across texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Critical comparison across texts” objective: Make critical comparisons across texts — comparing themes, characters, settings, styles, or arguments in two or more works, including texts from different periods, genres, or cultures.
subject: English

label: Science Can Be Revised
statement: Demonstrate the “Science Can Be Revised” objective: Scientific knowledge is provisional — it is the best current explanation based on available evidence, and it can and should be revised when better evidence arrives.
subject: Science

label: Physical vs Chemical Changes
statement: Demonstrate the “Physical vs Chemical Changes” objective: Distinguish between physical changes (reversible, no new substances formed) and chemical changes (new substances formed, often irreversible), using conservation of mass to understand both types.
subject: Science

label: Animal Classification Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Animal Classification Vocabulary” objective: Use vocabulary for classifying animals and describing life cycles — vertebrate, invertebrate, mammal, bird, reptile, amphibian, fish, insect, arachnid, larva, pupa, metamorphosis, gestation, offspring, complete metamorphosis, incomplete metamorphosis — and apply these correctly when sorting and comparing organisms.
subject: Science

label: States of Matter Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “States of Matter Vocabulary” objective: Name and distinguish the three states of matter — solid, liquid, and gas — using properties vocabulary: hard, rigid, runny, flows, keeps its shape, fills its container; use 'change of state' to describe what happens when materials are heated or cooled.
subject: Science

label: Understanding print
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding print” objective: Demonstrate understanding that print carries meaning, follows left-to-right top-to-bottom directionality, and is organised page by page in books.
subject: English

label: Negative numbers in context
statement: Demonstrate the “Negative numbers in context” objective: Interpret negative numbers in context (temperature, sea level, bank balance); count forwards and backwards with positive and negative whole numbers, including through zero.
subject: Mathematics

label: Rainforest Food Webs
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Food Webs” objective: Understand how energy and nutrients flow through a rainforest food web — from plants (producers) to herbivores (primary consumers) to predators (secondary consumers) — and that decomposers like fungi and insects break down dead material on the forest floor, recycling nutrients back into the soil for plants to use again.
subject: Science

label: Exploring the Ocean
statement: Demonstrate the “Exploring the Ocean” objective: Know that oceanographers and marine biologists study the ocean using submarines, remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), satellites, and diving, and that much of the ocean remains unexplored — we know more about the Moon's surface than the deep ocean floor.
subject: Science

label: What happens when things collide
statement: Demonstrate the “What happens when things collide” objective: Ask questions and predict outcomes about the changes in energy that occur when objects collide.
subject: Science

label: Orbital Mechanics
statement: Demonstrate the “Orbital Mechanics” objective: Apply Newton's laws to explain orbital motion: why orbit is continuously falling sideways rather than floating; how a gravity assist (slingshot manoeuvre) transfers momentum from a planet to a spacecraft; and why rockets need to reach a specific speed to enter orbit — with a conceptual (not algebraic) treatment of the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation.
subject: Science

label: Dividing by Fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Dividing by Fractions” objective: Interpret and compute division of a whole number by a unit fraction (e.g. 4 ÷ 1/5 = 20); use visual models and the relationship between multiplication and division to explain why the quotient is larger than the dividend.
subject: Mathematics

label: Dialects & Registers
statement: Demonstrate the “Dialects & Registers” objective: Compare and contrast the varieties of English used in stories, dramas, or poems, including dialects and registers, understanding how language varies by region, context, and purpose.
subject: English

label: Pathogens & the Immune System
statement: Demonstrate the “Pathogens & the Immune System” objective: Explain how pathogens (bacteria, viruses, and fungi) cause disease and describe how the immune system responds, including the roles of white blood cells (phagocytosis, antibody production) and the concept of immunity.
subject: Science

label: Types of angles (age 13+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of angles (age 13+)” objective: Apply Pythagoras’ Theorem (a² + b² = c²) to calculate unknown side lengths in right-angled triangles, including in real-world and coordinate-geometry contexts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Sorting into categories (age 6+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Sorting into categories (age 6+)” objective: Interpret categorical data by asking and answering questions about totals, how many in each category, and how many more or less one category has than another.
subject: Mathematics

label: Types of Fossils
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of Fossils” objective: Distinguish body fossils (preserved bones, teeth, shells) from trace fossils (footprints, trackways, eggs, burrows, coprolites) and explain what each type can tell scientists.
subject: Science

label: Inherited characteristics
statement: Demonstrate the “Inherited characteristics” objective: Analyse and interpret data to provide evidence that plants and animals have traits inherited from parents and that variation of these traits exists in a group of similar organisms.
subject: Science

label: Sets & Venn Diagrams
statement: Demonstrate the “Sets & Venn Diagrams” objective: Enumerate sets and their unions and intersections systematically using tables, grids, and Venn diagrams to organise and count outcomes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Designing Fair AI Rules
statement: Demonstrate the “Designing Fair AI Rules” objective: Design thinking applied to AI ethics: if you were designing an AI system, what rules would you give it? Who should it help? What should it not be allowed to do?
subject: Computing

label: Static electricity and sparks
statement: Demonstrate the “Static electricity and sparks” objective: Explain static electricity as the build-up of electric charge through friction, describe how charged objects attract or repel each other, and relate static discharge to everyday phenomena such as lightning.
subject: Science

label: Hands-On Problem Solving
statement: Demonstrate the “Hands-On Problem Solving” objective: Select and use familiar tools (concrete objects, fingers, ten frames) to help solve a mathematical problem.
subject: Mathematics

label: Brave Polar Explorers
statement: Demonstrate the “Brave Polar Explorers” objective: Know simple stories of brave polar explorers — Robert Falcon Scott and Roald Amundsen who raced to the South Pole, and Ernest Shackleton whose ship Endurance was crushed by ice but who brought all his men home safely — and understand that polar exploration required incredible courage and endurance.
subject: Science

label: Anglo-Saxon Britain
statement: Demonstrate the “Anglo-Saxon Britain” objective: Who the Anglo-Saxons were: Germanic peoples who settled in Britain after the Romans left; their kingdoms, villages, place names, art, and eventual conversion to Christianity.
subject: History

label: Building shade from the sun
statement: Demonstrate the “Building shade from the sun” objective: Use tools and materials to design and build a structure that will reduce the warming effect of sunlight on an area, such as a shade or shelter.
subject: Science

label: Separating Mixtures
statement: Demonstrate the “Separating Mixtures” objective: Use knowledge of solids, liquids, and gases to decide how mixtures might be separated through filtering, sieving, and evaporating.
subject: Science

label: Current, voltage, and what they measure
statement: Demonstrate the “Current, voltage, and what they measure” objective: Understand that electric current is the rate of flow of charge (measured in amperes using an ammeter), and that potential difference (voltage) is the energy transferred per unit charge (measured in volts using a voltmeter).
subject: Science

label: Kings & Queens
statement: Demonstrate the “Kings & Queens” objective: What medieval kings and queens did: ruling the land, making laws, collecting taxes; the crown and throne as symbols of power; the Tower of London.
subject: History

label: Understanding fractions (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding fractions (age 9+)” objective: Construct and present logical mathematical arguments involving multiple steps; critique others' reasoning about fractions, angles, or calculations and clearly explain errors or alternative methods.
subject: Mathematics

label: Different Accounts of the Same Event
statement: Demonstrate the “Different Accounts of the Same Event” objective: Recognise that different people can give different accounts of the same event — and that both can be genuine while still disagreeing.
subject: History

label: Extending Table Patterns
statement: Demonstrate the “Extending Table Patterns” objective: Recognise and use repeated reasoning to generalise: extend multiplication table patterns, derive unknown facts from known ones, and describe rules for sequences.
subject: Mathematics

label: Choosing A or An
statement: Demonstrate the “Choosing A or An” objective: Use the correct form of the indefinite article — 'a' before words beginning with a consonant sound and 'an' before words beginning with a vowel sound (e.g., a rock, an open box, an hour, a unicorn).
subject: English

label: Agreement in sentences
statement: Demonstrate the “Agreement in sentences” objective: Ensure subject-verb agreement and pronoun-antecedent agreement within and across sentences.
subject: English

label: Medieval Food & Feasts
statement: Demonstrate the “Medieval Food & Feasts” objective: What people ate in medieval times: bread and pottage for ordinary people, grand feasts for the rich; no forks, eating with hands; the great hall as the centre of castle life.
subject: History

label: Deforestation Causes & Scale
statement: Demonstrate the “Deforestation Causes & Scale” objective: Understand the causes and scale of rainforest deforestation — cattle ranching (largest driver in the Amazon), soy and palm oil plantations, logging for timber, and mining — and know that approximately 10 million hectares of forest are lost globally each year, with devastating consequences for biodiversity, climate, and indigenous communities.
subject: Science

label: Stereotypes and Individual Differences
statement: Demonstrate the “Stereotypes and Individual Differences” objective: Recognise stereotypes — oversimplified beliefs about groups of people based on gender, race, age, or other characteristics — and understand that stereotypes are unfair because they ignore individual differences.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Scale and similar shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Scale and similar shapes” objective: Solve problems involving similar shapes where the scale factor is known or can be found.
subject: Mathematics

label: Electromagnets
statement: Demonstrate the “Electromagnets” objective: Describe the magnetic effect of an electric current (a current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field), and investigate how the strength of an electromagnet depends on current, number of coil turns, and core material.
subject: Science

label: Effects of Drugs & Alcohol
statement: Demonstrate the “Effects of Drugs & Alcohol” objective: Explain the effects of recreational drugs including alcohol, tobacco, and illegal substances on behaviour, health, and body systems, and distinguish between depressants, stimulants, and hallucinogens.
subject: Science

label: Finding Knowledge Gaps
statement: Demonstrate the “Finding Knowledge Gaps” objective: Survey your own understanding of a whole topic — identify where your knowledge is solid, where it is shaky, and what still needs work.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Speed and energy
statement: Demonstrate the “Speed and energy” objective: Use evidence to construct an explanation relating the speed of an object to the energy of that object.
subject: Science

label: Decimal place value
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimal place value” objective: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given system (e.g. 5 cm to 0.05 m) using decimal notation to up to three decimal places; convert between smaller and larger units of length, mass, volume, and time.
subject: Mathematics

label: Building & Drawing Shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Building & Drawing Shapes” objective: Model shapes by building from components (e.g. sticks and clay balls) and by drawing.
subject: Mathematics

label: Diet, Exercise & Lifestyle
statement: Demonstrate the “Diet, Exercise & Lifestyle” objective: Recognise the impact of diet, exercise, drugs, and lifestyle on the way human bodies function.
subject: Science

label: Suffixes (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Suffixes (age 9+)” objective: Spell words with Latin and French suffix patterns: endings sounding like /ʃəs/ spelt -cious or -tious (e.g., precious, cautious), /ʃəl/ spelt -cial or -tial (e.g., official, essential), and words ending in -ant/-ance/-ancy vs -ent/-ence/-ency (e.g., observant/observance, confident/confidence).
subject: English

label: Number of minutes in an hour
statement: Demonstrate the “Number of minutes in an hour” objective: Know the number of minutes in an hour and the number of hours in a day.
subject: Mathematics

label: Telling time to the minute (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Telling time to the minute (age 9+)” objective: Solve problems involving converting between units of time (hours↔minutes, minutes↔seconds, years↔months, weeks↔days).
subject: Mathematics

label: Indigenous Rainforest Peoples
statement: Demonstrate the “Indigenous Rainforest Peoples” objective: Know that indigenous peoples such as the Yanomami have lived in rainforests for thousands of years, building homes from forest materials, finding food by hunting, fishing, and gathering, and knowing the forest and its plants and animals deeply.
subject: Science

label: Plants Grow from Air & Water
statement: Demonstrate the “Plants Grow from Air & Water” objective: Support an argument that plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air and water, not from the soil.
subject: Science

label: Connecting New & Old Ideas
statement: Demonstrate the “Connecting New & Old Ideas” objective: Look for connections between new ideas and things you already know — how does this fit with what I've learned before?
subject: Learning to Learn

label: The solar system (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “The solar system (age 11+)” objective: Describe the detailed structure of the solar system, including moons, asteroids, and comets, compare orbital periods and distances of the planets, and distinguish between planets, dwarf planets, and other bodies.
subject: Science

label: Giving and Receiving Feedback
statement: Demonstrate the “Giving and Receiving Feedback” objective: Give and receive constructive feedback — telling someone what they did well and what could be improved in a way that is helpful rather than hurtful, and receiving feedback about their own work without becoming defensive.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Positive Self-Talk
statement: Demonstrate the “Positive Self-Talk” objective: Use positive self-talk to manage difficult situations — replacing unhelpful thoughts like 'I'm stupid' or 'I'll never be able to do this' with encouraging ones like 'This is hard but I can keep trying' or 'I've done hard things before'.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Homophones
statement: Demonstrate the “Homophones” objective: Distinguish and correctly spell common homophones and near-homophones encountered at Y3-4 level (e.g., accept/except, affect/effect, brake/break, grate/great), including using the /eɪ/ sound spelt ei, eigh, or ey.
subject: English

label: The Amazon Rainforest
statement: Demonstrate the “The Amazon Rainforest” objective: Know that the Amazon is Earth's greatest rainforest — spanning nine countries across South America, containing the world's largest river by water volume, and home to an estimated 10% of all species on Earth including 40,000 plant species, 1,300 bird species, and 3,000 types of fish.
subject: Science

label: Midnight Sun & Polar Night
statement: Demonstrate the “Midnight Sun & Polar Night” objective: Know that at the poles, daylight and darkness are extreme — in summer the Sun never fully sets (midnight sun) and in winter the Sun never rises (polar night lasting months) — and that this is very different from what we experience at home, where every day has both daylight and darkness.
subject: Science

label: Fluent addition and subtraction
statement: Demonstrate the “Fluent addition and subtraction” objective: Recall and use addition and subtraction facts to 20 fluently, and derive and use related facts up to 100.
subject: Mathematics

label: Probabilities Sum to One
statement: Demonstrate the “Probabilities Sum to One” objective: Understand that when all possible outcomes of a trial are listed, their probabilities must add up to 1; use this to find the probability of an event NOT happening: P(not A) = 1 − P(A); apply this shortcut to avoid counting all unfavourable outcomes directly.
subject: Mathematics

label: Unknown in Addition & Subtraction
statement: Demonstrate the “Unknown in Addition & Subtraction” objective: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.
subject: Mathematics

label: Drawing conclusions from evidence (age 12+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Drawing conclusions from evidence (age 12+)” objective: Identify patterns and trends in data, draw conclusions that directly address the hypothesis with quantitative reference to evidence, and evaluate the investigation by distinguishing between systematic and random errors and proposing targeted improvements.
subject: Science

label: Reading Weather Maps
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading Weather Maps” objective: Read and interpret weather maps, data tables, and graphs — identifying symbols for sun, rain, wind, and temperature; spotting trends and patterns in weather data over weeks, months, or seasons; and using data to make simple predictions.
subject: Science

label: Simple formulae
statement: Demonstrate the “Simple formulae” objective: Understand and use standard mathematical formulae; rearrange formulae to change the subject, performing inverse operations to isolate a different variable.
subject: Mathematics

label: Advanced Maths Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Advanced Maths Vocabulary” objective: Communicate with mathematical precision: use correct vocabulary for ratio, proportion, algebra, volume, coordinate geometry, and circle parts; specify units including cm³, m³, and miles/km; use notation for algebraic expressions and order of operations accurately.
subject: Mathematics

label: What Is an Angle?
statement: Demonstrate the “What Is an Angle?” objective: Understand that an angle is a geometric shape formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint (vertex); recognise angles in real-life contexts and 2-D shapes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Miles & Kilometres
statement: Demonstrate the “Miles & Kilometres” objective: Convert between miles and kilometres using the approximate relationship (5 miles ≈ 8 km).
subject: Mathematics

label: Crime & Punishment
statement: Demonstrate the “Crime & Punishment” objective: How justice worked in medieval times: trial by ordeal, trial by combat, the role of the sheriff; punishments including stocks, pillory, and dungeons; how different it was from modern justice.
subject: History

label: Halves and quarters (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Halves and quarters (age 7+)” objective: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.
subject: Mathematics

label: What Plants Need to Grow
statement: Demonstrate the “What Plants Need to Grow” objective: Understand that plants need water, light, and a suitable temperature to grow and stay healthy.
subject: Science

label: Fractions on a number line
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions on a number line” objective: Move fluently between real-world situations, diagrams, number lines, and symbolic equations involving multiplication, fractions, and decimals, explaining what each representation shows.
subject: Mathematics

label: Balanced & Unbalanced Forces
statement: Demonstrate the “Balanced & Unbalanced Forces” objective: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence of the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the motion of an object.
subject: Science

label: Estimating answers (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Estimating answers (age 7+)” objective: Estimate and read time with increasing accuracy to the nearest minute; record and compare time in terms of seconds, minutes, and hours.
subject: Mathematics

label: Fractions of amounts (harder)
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions of amounts (harder)” objective: Solve problems involving increasingly harder fractions to calculate quantities, including non-unit fractions where the answer is a whole number.
subject: Mathematics

label: Protecting Eyes from Sunlight
statement: Demonstrate the “Protecting Eyes from Sunlight” objective: Recognise that light from the sun can be dangerous and that there are ways to protect eyes.
subject: Science

label: Cohesion within paragraphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Cohesion within paragraphs” objective: Use cohesive devices within a paragraph — including pronouns, adverbials (then, after that, firstly), and synonyms — to link sentences and build a coherent flow of ideas.
subject: English

label: Measurement Line Plots
statement: Demonstrate the “Measurement Line Plots” objective: Make a line plot to display measurement data in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8); solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions using line plot data.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Biodiversity Crisis
statement: Demonstrate the “The Biodiversity Crisis” objective: Quantify the current biodiversity crisis: extinction rates 100-1000x the background rate; explain methods for measuring biodiversity loss (species-area relationship, population viability analysis, IUCN Red List categories); evaluate rewilding case studies — Yellowstone wolf reintroduction triggering a trophic cascade that changed river courses; Iberian lynx recovery; describe minimum viable population theory and conservation triage; examine ethical debates in deciding which species to prioritise.
subject: Science

label: Shared Research Projects
statement: Demonstrate the “Shared Research Projects” objective: Participate in shared research and writing projects; recall information from experiences or gather information from sources to answer a question.
subject: English

label: Describing Aloud
statement: Demonstrate the “Describing Aloud” objective: Describe familiar people, places, things, and events with detail; speak audibly and express thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly; give well-structured descriptions and explanations.
subject: English

label: Coasts & Beaches
statement: Demonstrate the “Coasts & Beaches” objective: Know what a coast or beach is — the place where land meets the ocean — and that different coasts can be sandy, rocky, or muddy, each with different plants and animals.
subject: Science

label: Comparing Time Durations
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing Time Durations” objective: Compare durations of events and calculate the time taken by particular events or tasks.
subject: Mathematics

label: Rhyming words
statement: Demonstrate the “Rhyming words” objective: Recognise and produce rhyming words; join in with predictable phrases and rhymes in stories and poems; learn to appreciate and recite poems by heart.
subject: English

label: Light & Seeing in the Dark
statement: Demonstrate the “Light & Seeing in the Dark” objective: Observe that objects in darkness can be seen only when illuminated by a light source.
subject: Science

label: Life Cycles of Organisms
statement: Demonstrate the “Life Cycles of Organisms” objective: Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles but all share the common stages of birth, growth, reproduction, and death.
subject: Science

label: Poems, Drama & Prose
statement: Demonstrate the “Poems, Drama & Prose” objective: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, identifying structural elements unique to each form: verse, rhythm, and meter in poetry; cast of characters, dialogue, and stage directions in drama; chapters and paragraphs in prose.
subject: English

label: The Immune System
statement: Demonstrate the “The Immune System” objective: Know that the body has an immune system that protects against illness: the skin acts as a barrier, white blood cells identify and destroy germs (bacteria and viruses), and vaccines train the immune system to recognise specific diseases before they cause illness.
subject: Science

label: Decimals and fractions (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimals and fractions (age 10+)” objective: Associate a fraction with division and calculate decimal fraction equivalents for simple fractions (e.g. 3/8 = 0.375); recall and use equivalences between simple fractions, decimals, and percentages in different contexts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Healthy Lifestyle Choices
statement: Demonstrate the “Healthy Lifestyle Choices” objective: Understand how lifestyle choices affect the body’s health: a balanced diet, regular exercise, adequate sleep, and avoiding harmful substances (tobacco, alcohol, drugs) help body systems function well, while poor choices increase the risk of disease.
subject: Science

label: Fractions of a whole (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions of a whole (age 10+)” objective: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b); solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to fractional or mixed-number answers.
subject: Mathematics

label: Capacity and volume
statement: Demonstrate the “Capacity and volume” objective: Measure and begin to record capacity and volume using non-standard and standard units.
subject: Mathematics

label: Telling time to the minute (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Telling time to the minute (age 7+)” objective: Tell and write time from analogue and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m., p.m., and 12-hour and 24-hour notation.
subject: Mathematics

label: Measuring angles
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring angles” objective: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor; draw given angles and sketch angles of specified measure.
subject: Mathematics

label: Applying Spelling Rules to Complex Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Applying Spelling Rules to Complex Words” objective: Spell correctly and consistently, applying the spelling patterns and rules from KS1-2 to increasingly complex vocabulary encountered in KS3 reading and subject-specific study.
subject: English

label: Storm Safety
statement: Demonstrate the “Storm Safety” objective: Know basic storm safety: during thunder and lightning, go indoors or into a car, stay away from trees and water; understand that storms can be frightening but there are ways to stay safe.
subject: Science

label: Percentage and decimal equivalents
statement: Demonstrate the “Percentage and decimal equivalents” objective: Solve problems requiring knowledge of percentage and decimal equivalents of 1/2, 1/4, 1/5, 2/5, 4/5 and fractions with denominators that are multiples of 10 or 25.
subject: Mathematics

label: Where Are the Poles?
statement: Demonstrate the “Where Are the Poles?” objective: Know that Earth has a North Pole and a South Pole — the two coldest places on the planet — and be able to find them on a globe, understanding that they are at the very top and very bottom of the Earth, as far from the Equator as possible.
subject: Science

label: Phases of the Moon
statement: Demonstrate the “Phases of the Moon” objective: Explain the phases of the Moon as the changing angle of sunlight on the lunar surface as seen from Earth, and describe how solar and lunar eclipses occur.
subject: Science

label: Not all minibeasts are insects
statement: Demonstrate the “Not all minibeasts are insects” objective: Not all minibeasts are insects: distinguishing insects from other minibeasts. Spiders have 8 legs and 2 body parts (arachnids), woodlice have 14 legs (crustaceans), worms have no legs, snails have a shell and one foot. The 'Is it an insect?' sorting game.
subject: Science

label: Writing Number Sentences
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing Number Sentences” objective: Write simple numerical expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them (e.g. recognise that 3 × (18932 + 921) is three times as large as 18932 + 921).
subject: Mathematics

label: Glaciers & Ice Sheets
statement: Demonstrate the “Glaciers & Ice Sheets” objective: Understand how glaciers and ice sheets form and behave — snow accumulates over centuries and compresses into dense ice, glaciers flow slowly downhill under their own weight carving U-shaped valleys and depositing moraines; the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets together hold enough ice to raise sea levels by over 65 metres; and ice cores drilled from these sheets contain trapped air bubbles that reveal Earth's climate history going back 800,000 years.
subject: Science

label: The most successful animals on Earth
statement: Demonstrate the “The most successful animals on Earth” objective: The most successful animals on Earth: there are roughly one million described insect species, and scientists estimate 5–10 million may exist. More insect species than all other animal groups combined. Why so many? Small body size means less food needed, fast reproduction with many offspring, flight allows reaching new habitats, and the exoskeleton is incredibly versatile.
subject: Science

label: Protecting the Ocean
statement: Demonstrate the “Protecting the Ocean” objective: Understand how people protect the ocean: marine protected areas limit fishing and pollution, sustainable fishing prevents overharvesting, beach clean-ups reduce plastic, and international agreements aim to reduce carbon emissions that cause ocean acidification.
subject: Science

label: Magnetic Fields
statement: Demonstrate the “Magnetic Fields” objective: Describe magnetic poles (north and south), explain attraction and repulsion between poles, describe magnetic field lines plotted using a compass, and explain the Earth's magnetic field and its practical uses.
subject: Science

label: Multiple Accounts of Events
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiple Accounts of Events” objective: Analyse multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences in the point of view they represent.
subject: English

label: Fractions on a number line
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions on a number line” objective: Solve word problems involving distances, time intervals, liquid volumes, masses, and money using the four operations with fractions or decimals; represent with diagrams including number lines.
subject: Mathematics

label: The solar system
statement: Demonstrate the “The solar system” objective: Describe the sun, Earth, and moon as approximately spherical bodies, and describe the movement of the Earth and other planets orbiting the sun in the solar system.
subject: Science

label: Proportion
statement: Demonstrate the “Proportion” objective: Recognise and solve problems involving direct proportion (as one quantity increases, the other increases at a constant rate) and inverse proportion (as one increases, the other decreases), including graphical and algebraic representations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Connecting reading to experience
statement: Demonstrate the “Connecting reading to experience” objective: Link what is read or heard to own experiences; draw on background knowledge and vocabulary to support understanding of texts.
subject: English

label: Rounding Large Numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Rounding Large Numbers” objective: Round any whole number up to 1,000,000 to the nearest 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000, or 100,000 using place-value understanding.
subject: Mathematics

label: Egyptian Trade and Economy
statement: Demonstrate the “Egyptian Trade and Economy” objective: Understand that ancient Egypt had a thriving economy based on farming surplus, trade, and specialised labour: the Nile's fertile soil produced enough food to support craftworkers, priests, and officials, and Egypt traded along the Nile and across the Mediterranean — exchanging gold, papyrus, and grain for cedarwood from Lebanon, lapis lazuli from Afghanistan, and incense from Punt.
subject: History

label: Fair testing (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Fair testing (age 9+)” objective: Use test results to make predictions and set up further comparative and fair tests to investigate new questions.
subject: Science

label: Fall of Ancient Egyptian Civilisation
statement: Demonstrate the “Fall of Ancient Egyptian Civilisation” objective: Trace the end of ancient Egyptian civilisation through its successive conquests — Assyrian, Persian, Macedonian (Alexander the Great), and finally Roman — and explain how each conqueror was simultaneously shaped by Egyptian culture; examine Cleopatra VII as the last pharaoh and as a multilingual political strategist; and consider what survives of ancient Egypt in modern culture, religion, and language.
subject: History

label: Objects vs Materials
statement: Demonstrate the “Objects vs Materials” objective: Distinguish between an object and the material from which it is made, understanding that objects can be made from different materials.
subject: Science

label: Endangered & Extinct Species
statement: Demonstrate the “Endangered & Extinct Species” objective: Understand why some animal species become endangered or go extinct — habitat destruction, hunting/poaching, pollution, climate change, and invasive species — and know examples like the giant panda, mountain gorilla, Amur leopard, and the now-extinct dodo and thylacine, using the IUCN Red List as the system scientists use to track threatened species.
subject: Science

label: Volume as additive
statement: Demonstrate the “Volume as additive” objective: Recognise volume as additive; find volumes of composite solid figures made of two or more non-overlapping right rectangular prisms.
subject: Mathematics

label: Global Citizenship
statement: Demonstrate the “Global Citizenship” objective: Understand what it means to be a citizen in an interconnected world where decisions in one place affect people elsewhere; explore global issues (climate justice, forced migration, global health, poverty) through an empathy lens, distinguishing facts from value judgements; engage with the ethical tension between obligations to those close to us and obligations to distant strangers; introduce evidence-based giving and effective altruism as one framework for thinking about global responsibility; develop a personal, reasoned stance on global citizenship that acknowledges complexity.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Giving Change
statement: Demonstrate the “Giving Change” objective: Add and subtract amounts of money to give change, using both £ and p in practical contexts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Multiplicative Comparison
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiplicative Comparison” objective: Solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number.
subject: Mathematics

label: Discussing and Questioning New Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Discussing and Questioning New Words” objective: Ask and answer questions about unknown words in texts; discuss word meanings and link new vocabulary to words already known.
subject: English

label: Energy can't be created or destroyed
statement: Demonstrate the “Energy can't be created or destroyed” objective: Explain the principle of conservation of energy (energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred between stores), and describe how energy is dissipated as thermal energy to the surroundings in all real processes.
subject: Science

label: Naming Your Feelings
statement: Demonstrate the “Naming Your Feelings” objective: Notice what you are feeling and put a name to it — being able to label an emotion is the first step to understanding and managing it.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Chromosomes, Genes & DNA
statement: Demonstrate the “Chromosomes, Genes & DNA” objective: Describe the relationship between chromosomes, genes, and DNA in heredity, including the double helix structure of DNA and the historical roles of Watson, Crick, Franklin, and Wilkins.
subject: Science

label: Extreme Weather Events
statement: Demonstrate the “Extreme Weather Events” objective: Know about extreme weather events — hurricanes (spinning storms over warm ocean), tornadoes (violent rotating columns of air), floods, droughts, and blizzards — how they form, where they typically occur, and their effects on people and the environment.
subject: Science

label: Teaching It Back
statement: Demonstrate the “Teaching It Back” objective: After learning something new, explain it in your own words — to yourself, a family member, or even a toy.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Money Addition & Subtraction
statement: Demonstrate the “Money Addition & Subtraction” objective: Solve simple money problems involving addition and subtraction, including giving change.
subject: Mathematics

label: Question Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Question Words” objective: Understand and use question words (who, what, where, when, why, how) to form and answer questions.
subject: English

label: How Muscles Move Bones
statement: Demonstrate the “How Muscles Move Bones” objective: Understand that muscles work in pairs to move bones: when one muscle contracts (gets shorter and pulls), the opposite muscle relaxes, and that some muscles are voluntary (we choose to use them) while others like the heart are involuntary (they work automatically).
subject: Science

label: Daily Life in a Roman Town
statement: Demonstrate the “Daily Life in a Roman Town” objective: Describe daily life in a Roman town — the forum (marketplace and meeting place), public baths, amphitheatre, and villas — and explain that the Romans were brilliant engineers who built straight roads, aqueducts to carry water, underfloor heating (hypocaust), and Hadrian's Wall to mark the empire's northern frontier in Britain.
subject: History

label: Calculating with measurements
statement: Demonstrate the “Calculating with measurements” objective: Measure, compare, add, and subtract lengths (m/cm/mm), mass (kg/g), and volume/capacity (l/ml) using standard units.
subject: Mathematics

label: How We See Objects
statement: Demonstrate the “How We See Objects” objective: Develop a model to describe that light reflecting from objects and entering the eye allows objects to be seen.
subject: Science

label: Using a Dictionary to Check Spellings
statement: Demonstrate the “Using a Dictionary to Check Spellings” objective: Use the first two or three letters of a word to check its spelling in a dictionary; consult reference materials including beginning dictionaries to verify and correct spellings.
subject: English

label: Deep-Sea Life Without Sunlight
statement: Demonstrate the “Deep-Sea Life Without Sunlight” objective: Contrast photosynthesis (energy from sunlight) with chemosynthesis (energy from oxidising chemicals like hydrogen sulphide); describe hydrothermal vent communities: chemoautotrophic bacteria form the base of a food web supporting tube worms, giant clams, and vent crabs with no sunlight; explore what deep-sea life tells us about the origin of life on Earth; explain why NASA studies ocean vents as analogues for potential life around hydrothermal activity on Europa and Enceladus.
subject: Science

label: Sequence intervals of time
statement: Demonstrate the “Sequence intervals of time” objective: Compare and sequence intervals of time.
subject: Mathematics

label: Difficult Ethical Choices
statement: Demonstrate the “Difficult Ethical Choices” objective: Understand that ethical decisions are not always black and white — that sometimes there is no perfect answer and reasonable people can disagree — and practise weighing up competing values when making difficult choices.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Vikings vs Anglo-Saxons
statement: Demonstrate the “Vikings vs Anglo-Saxons” objective: The conflict between Vikings and Anglo-Saxons for control of England: Viking raids, Alfred the Great's resistance, the Danelaw, Athelstan as first king of all England, Edward the Confessor.
subject: History

label: Understanding Area
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding Area” objective: Understand that a unit square has one square unit of area and that the area of a plane figure is the number of unit squares that cover it without gaps or overlaps.
subject: Mathematics

label: How Plant Parts Work
statement: Demonstrate the “How Plant Parts Work” objective: Identify and describe the functions of different parts of flowering plants: roots absorb water and nutrients, stems transport materials, leaves make food, flowers enable reproduction.
subject: Science

label: Fossils as Evidence
statement: Demonstrate the “Fossils as Evidence” objective: Analyse and interpret data from fossils to provide evidence of organisms and environments that existed long ago.
subject: Science

label: Insect Adaptations
statement: Demonstrate the “Insect Adaptations” objective: Adaptation and evolution in insects: peppered moths as a famous example of natural selection (dark moths survived better on soot-covered trees during the Industrial Revolution). Stick insects evolved to look like twigs. Ant-mimicking spiders evolved to fool predators. How small changes over many generations lead to remarkable disguises.
subject: Science

label: Adding and subtracting mixed numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding and subtracting mixed numbers” objective: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, including by converting to improper fractions or using properties of operations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Compound Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Compound Words” objective: Recognise and spell compound words by identifying the two component words that combine to form a single word.
subject: English

label: Number Words to 100
statement: Demonstrate the “Number Words to 100” objective: Read and write numbers to at least 100 in words.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Present Perfect Tense
statement: Demonstrate the “The Present Perfect Tense” objective: Use the present perfect form of verbs in contrast to the simple past tense, understanding how the present perfect indicates an action completed at an unspecified time or with ongoing relevance (e.g., 'He has gone out' vs 'He went out').
subject: English

label: Communities Protecting Resources
statement: Demonstrate the “Communities Protecting Resources” objective: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect the Earth's resources and environment.
subject: Science

label: Drawing Life Cycle Diagrams
statement: Demonstrate the “Drawing Life Cycle Diagrams” objective: Draw and interpret life cycle diagrams for flowering plants, insects (complete and incomplete metamorphosis), birds, and mammals — labelling stages, describing transitions, and comparing cycles across species.
subject: Science

label: Space Robots & Rovers
statement: Demonstrate the “Space Robots & Rovers” objective: Describe how robots and rovers have explored places humans cannot easily go — Mars rovers like Curiosity and Perseverance drive across Mars taking photos, collecting rock samples, and searching for signs of past water.
subject: Science

label: Cells to Organ Systems
statement: Demonstrate the “Cells to Organ Systems” objective: Describe the hierarchical organisation of multicellular organisms: cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organism.
subject: Science

label: Classifying living things
statement: Demonstrate the “Classifying living things” objective: Gather, record, classify, and present data in a variety of ways including tables, bar charts, labelled diagrams, and keys.
subject: Science

label: Polar Food Chains
statement: Demonstrate the “Polar Food Chains” objective: Understand polar food chains — in the Antarctic, phytoplankton are eaten by krill, krill are eaten by fish and penguins, and penguins are eaten by leopard seals and orcas; in the Arctic, algae under ice feeds zooplankton, which feeds fish, which feeds seals, which feeds polar bears — and that tiny organisms like krill and plankton are the foundation of all polar life.
subject: Science

label: Polar Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Polar Animals” objective: Know about other polar animals besides penguins and polar bears — seals that swim under ice, walruses with long tusks, Arctic foxes that turn white in winter, snowy owls, narwhals with their unicorn-like tusk, and whales that migrate to polar waters to feed — and that all these animals have special features to survive extreme cold.
subject: Science

label: Fixing Fragments & Run-Ons
statement: Demonstrate the “Fixing Fragments & Run-Ons” objective: Recognise and correct sentence fragments (incomplete sentences lacking a subject or predicate) and run-on sentences (two or more independent clauses joined without proper punctuation or conjunctions).
subject: English

label: Polar Conservation & Future
statement: Demonstrate the “Polar Conservation & Future” objective: Understand the conservation challenges facing polar regions — marine protected areas in the Southern Ocean aim to preserve Antarctic ecosystems, Arctic nations dispute sovereignty over northern sea routes and resources as ice retreats, indigenous peoples fight for land rights and voice in environmental decisions, and international cooperation (Paris Agreement, Antarctic Treaty) is essential but difficult to maintain as economic pressures grow.
subject: Science

label: Counting in 6s
statement: Demonstrate the “Counting in 6s” objective: Count in multiples of 6, 7, 9, 25, and 1000.
subject: Mathematics

label: Expanded noun phrases (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Expanded noun phrases (age 9+)” objective: Form and use prepositional phrases (preposition + noun phrase) to add detail about time, location, or direction within sentences, recognising how they function as adjective or adverb phrases.
subject: English

label: Scaling Up
statement: Demonstrate the “Scaling Up” objective: What happens when a small business grows; making more products, hiring people, reaching more customers; the challenges and opportunities of scaling.
subject: Life Skills

label: Drawing conclusions from evidence
statement: Demonstrate the “Drawing conclusions from evidence” objective: Report on findings from enquiries using oral and written explanations, draw simple conclusions, make predictions, and suggest improvements.
subject: Science

label: Numbers up to 10 into pairs
statement: Demonstrate the “Numbers up to 10 into pairs” objective: Decompose numbers up to 10 into pairs in more than one way (part-part-whole).
subject: Mathematics

label: Reconstructing Ancient Ecosystems
statement: Demonstrate the “Reconstructing Ancient Ecosystems” objective: Reconstruct an ancient ecosystem using multiple independent lines of evidence: isotope analysis of teeth to infer diet and migration, bone histology (growth rings) to estimate age and growth rate, coprolite chemistry for diet, and palaeobotany for habitat — understanding that palaeontology is an evidence-synthesis discipline.
subject: Science

label: Predicting what happens next
statement: Demonstrate the “Predicting what happens next” objective: Predict what might happen next in a story based on what has been read so far; discuss the significance of titles and events.
subject: English

label: Writing Craft Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing Craft Vocabulary” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of writing craft and effect — form, structure, register, tone, voice, coherence, cohesion, argument, evidence, perspective, rhetoric, technique, formal, informal, and style — and understand that these words describe choices writers make intentionally to achieve a particular effect on the reader.
subject: English

label: Body Parts & Senses
statement: Demonstrate the “Body Parts & Senses” objective: Identify, name, and locate basic parts of the human body and associate each body part with its sense.
subject: Science

label: Calculating Dietary Energy
statement: Demonstrate the “Calculating Dietary Energy” objective: Calculate and evaluate energy intake and requirements in a healthy daily diet, interpreting food labels and nutritional data.
subject: Science

label: Formal and Informal English
statement: Demonstrate the “Formal and Informal English” objective: Recognise and compare formal and informal uses of English, understanding that language choices vary based on audience, purpose and context.
subject: English

label: Measuring angles (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring angles (age 9+)” objective: Recognise angle measure as additive; find unknown angles by adding or subtracting on a diagram using equations with a symbol for the unknown.
subject: Mathematics

label: Mental multiplication and division (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Mental multiplication and division (age 9+)” objective: Multiply and divide numbers mentally drawing upon known facts, including related facts and place-value adjustments.
subject: Mathematics

label: Athenian Democracy
statement: Demonstrate the “Athenian Democracy” objective: Understand that Athens invented democracy — a system where free male citizens gathered in an Assembly to debate and vote on important decisions for the city — but that women, enslaved people, and foreigners were not allowed to vote.
subject: History

label: Scatter Graphs & Correlation
statement: Demonstrate the “Scatter Graphs & Correlation” objective: Describe simple mathematical relationships between two variables using scatter graphs, identify positive, negative, or no correlation, and use a line of best fit to make predictions.
subject: Mathematics

label: Abstract nouns
statement: Demonstrate the “Abstract nouns” objective: Understand and use abstract nouns to name ideas, qualities, and states that cannot be perceived by the senses.
subject: English

label: Checking Your Own Work
statement: Demonstrate the “Checking Your Own Work” objective: After finishing a task, look back at what you did and ask yourself: does this seem right?
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Combining information from texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Combining information from texts” objective: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably, combining and comparing what each source contributes.
subject: English

label: A Hundred Is Ten Tens
