statement: Demonstrate the “A Hundred Is Ten Tens” objective: Understand that 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens — called a 'hundred'.
subject: Mathematics

label: Regular and irregular polygons
statement: Demonstrate the “Regular and irregular polygons” objective: Distinguish between regular and irregular polygons based on reasoning about equal sides and equal angles.
subject: Mathematics

label: Brackets in Expressions
statement: Demonstrate the “Brackets in Expressions” objective: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions and evaluate expressions containing these grouping symbols.
subject: Mathematics

label: Understanding angles
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding angles” objective: Recognise angles as a property of shape or a description of a turn.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Black Death
statement: Demonstrate the “The Black Death” objective: The Black Death of 1348-49: what the plague was, how it spread, its devastating death toll; how it changed society by giving surviving workers more power and higher wages.
subject: History

label: The Five Oceans
statement: Demonstrate the “The Five Oceans” objective: Name and locate the five oceans — Pacific (largest), Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic (smallest and coldest) — on a world map, and understand that they are all connected as one global ocean.
subject: Science

label: Judgement of the Dead
statement: Demonstrate the “Judgement of the Dead” objective: Describe the Egyptian belief in the judgement of the dead: after death, the heart was weighed against the feather of Ma'at in the Hall of Judgement, with Anubis overseeing the scales and Thoth recording the result — a pure heart meant entry to the Field of Reeds (paradise), while a heavy heart was devoured by the monster Ammit, and know that the Book of the Dead contained spells to help the deceased pass this test.
subject: History

label: Reading +, −, and = symbols
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading +, −, and = symbols” objective: Read, write, and interpret the symbols +, −, and = in number sentences.
subject: Mathematics

label: Magna Carta and Limiting Royal Power
statement: Demonstrate the “Magna Carta and Limiting Royal Power” objective: King John, the barons' revolt, and the sealing of the Magna Carta in 1215; what the Magna Carta said about limiting the king's power; its lasting importance for democracy and rights.
subject: History

label: Leadership Styles and Influence
statement: Demonstrate the “Leadership Styles and Influence” objective: Distinguish different leadership styles (directive, democratic, servant, transformational) and understand when each is appropriate; understand that influence in a group comes with responsibility, and explore the difference between leading through inspiration versus coercion; practise inclusive leadership: actively creating space for quieter voices and diverse perspectives; understand the ethics of influence and the boundary between persuasion and manipulation; explore concepts of consent and coercion in peer relationships; reflect on what kind of influence they want to have in their communities.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Egypt, the Nile, and the Desert
statement: Demonstrate the “Egypt, the Nile, and the Desert” objective: Locate Egypt on a map of Africa and understand that it is a country in a very hot, dry desert, but the River Nile — the longest river in the world — flows through it, bringing water and rich soil that allowed people to grow food and build one of the earliest great civilisations.
subject: History

label: Structures for Survival
statement: Demonstrate the “Structures for Survival” objective: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that function to support survival, growth, behaviour, and reproduction.
subject: Science

label: Real-World Maths Modelling
statement: Demonstrate the “Real-World Maths Modelling” objective: Model real-world problems involving scaling, unit conversion, area/perimeter, and percentage by selecting appropriate mathematical representations and interpreting results in context.
subject: Mathematics

label: Consonant Digraphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Consonant Digraphs” objective: Read and spell words containing consonant digraphs and less common consonant spellings (ch, sh, th, ck, tch, ng, ph, wh, k for /k/).
subject: English

label: Writing opinions
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing opinions” objective: Compose opinion pieces using drawing, dictating, or writing that name a topic or book and state a preference or opinion about it.
subject: English

label: Comparing Decimals
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing Decimals” objective: Compare two decimals to hundredths (or up to three decimal places) by reasoning about size using place-value understanding; record with >, =, <.
subject: Mathematics

label: Trying a New Approach
statement: Demonstrate the “Trying a New Approach” objective: When your first approach isn't working, try a different one — being flexible about strategies is part of being a good learner.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Place Value to 1000
statement: Demonstrate the “Place Value to 1000” objective: Solve number problems and practical problems involving place value of numbers up to 1000.
subject: Mathematics

label: Transferring Skills
statement: Demonstrate the “Transferring Skills” objective: Recognise when a skill or strategy learned in one subject or situation can be applied in a completely different one.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Ocean Animal Adaptations
statement: Demonstrate the “Ocean Animal Adaptations” objective: Understand that ocean animals have special adaptations for their environment: streamlined bodies for fast swimming, camouflage to hide from predators, blubber to keep warm in cold seas, and tentacles or suckers to catch prey.
subject: Science

label: Costs & Revenue
statement: Demonstrate the “Costs & Revenue” objective: It costs money to make things (costs/expenses); you earn money by selling them (revenue); if revenue is more than costs, that's profit; if costs are more, that's a loss.
subject: Life Skills

label: Spelling -able & -ible
statement: Demonstrate the “Spelling -able & -ible” objective: Spell words ending in -able/-ible and the corresponding adverb forms -ably/-ibly, applying patterns to determine which suffix to use based on the root word.
subject: English

label: Number Words to Twenty
statement: Demonstrate the “Number Words to Twenty” objective: Read and write number words from one to twenty.
subject: Mathematics

label: Wide Independent Reading Across Genres
statement: Demonstrate the “Wide Independent Reading Across Genres” objective: Read widely and independently across fiction and non-fiction — including whole novels, short stories, plays, poetry, and non-fiction from different genres, periods, and cultures — building stamina, breadth, and personal taste as a reader.
subject: English

label: Understanding fractions (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding fractions (age 10+)” objective: Move fluently between real-world situations, diagrams, coordinate grids, algebraic expressions, tables, and symbolic equations involving fractions, ratio, and algebra, explaining connections between representations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Representing Numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Representing Numbers” objective: Identify, represent, and estimate numbers using different representations including the number line.
subject: Mathematics

label: Writing Across Genres
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing Across Genres” objective: Write for a range of purposes and audiences beyond narrative — including scripts, poetry, personal and formal letters, notes for talks, and other forms — selecting the appropriate form, register, and conventions for each.
subject: English

label: Seeing Someone Else's Point of View
statement: Demonstrate the “Seeing Someone Else's Point of View” objective: Practise perspective-taking by imagining how someone else might feel in a given situation — using prompts like 'How would you feel if that happened to you?' and applying this when reading stories or during real interactions.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Magnetic Materials
statement: Demonstrate the “Magnetic Materials” objective: Observe how magnets attract or repel each other and attract some materials and not others.
subject: Science

label: What uses electricity at home
statement: Demonstrate the “What uses electricity at home” objective: Identify common appliances that run on electricity and understand that electricity is a form of energy that powers devices in everyday life.
subject: Science

label: Planning Ideas Before Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Planning Ideas Before Writing” objective: Plan before writing by saying aloud or noting down what will be written, writing down ideas and key words, and encapsulating ideas sentence by sentence before composing.
subject: English

label: Positive and Negative Numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Positive and Negative Numbers” objective: Understand positive and negative numbers as describing quantities with opposite directions or values; use them in context such as temperature, floors in a building, and bank balances.
subject: Mathematics

label: Evidence from the Past
statement: Demonstrate the “Evidence from the Past” objective: Understand that everything we know about the past comes from evidence — objects, buildings, pictures, documents, and stories that have survived.
subject: History

label: Seasonal Constellations
statement: Demonstrate the “Seasonal Constellations” objective: Recognise named constellations visible in different seasons and understand why we see different constellations at different times of year — because Earth’s orbit around the Sun changes which part of the sky we face at night.
subject: Science

label: 1000 More or Less
statement: Demonstrate the “1000 More or Less” objective: Find 1000 more or less than a given number.
subject: Mathematics

label: Triggers and Causes of Feelings
statement: Demonstrate the “Triggers and Causes of Feelings” objective: Understand that feelings have causes — something happens (a trigger) and that makes us feel a certain way — and begin to identify what triggers their own emotions.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Dividing fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Dividing fractions” objective: Divide a fraction by a fraction using the 'keep-change-flip' method and visual models; interpret and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions.
subject: Mathematics

label: Pronouns for clarity
statement: Demonstrate the “Pronouns for clarity” objective: Choose pronouns for clarity and cohesion, avoiding ambiguity and repetition; use reflexive pronouns correctly (e.g., myself, ourselves, himself).
subject: English

label: Shape patterns
statement: Demonstrate the “Shape patterns” objective: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule; identify apparent features of the pattern not explicit in the rule and explain informally why they occur.
subject: Mathematics

label: Finding Theme and Summarising
statement: Demonstrate the “Finding Theme and Summarising” objective: Determine the theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text, and provide an objective summary that captures the key events without personal opinions.
subject: English

label: Simple Fraction Sums
statement: Demonstrate the “Simple Fraction Sums” objective: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator within one whole (e.g. 5/7 + 1/7 = 6/7).
subject: Mathematics

label: Animal Life Cycles
statement: Demonstrate the “Animal Life Cycles” objective: Describe differences in the life cycles of mammals, amphibians, insects, and birds, comparing metamorphosis with direct development.
subject: Science

label: Justifying mathematical reasoning (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Justifying mathematical reasoning (age 8+)” objective: Construct and present multi-step mathematical arguments; critique the reasoning of others and explain clearly why a method works or fails.
subject: Mathematics

label: Summarising Spoken and Media Presentations
statement: Demonstrate the “Summarising Spoken and Media Presentations” objective: Summarise a written text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats including visually, quantitatively, and orally.
subject: English

label: Vocabulary: social awareness
statement: Demonstrate the “Vocabulary: social awareness” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of social awareness — including stereotype, prejudice, discrimination, equality, equity, bias, compassion, and fairness — and understand what distinguishes these closely related concepts.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: R-Controlled Vowel Sounds
statement: Demonstrate the “R-Controlled Vowel Sounds” objective: Read and spell words containing r-controlled vowels (ar, er, ir, ur, or, ore) and vowel-r patterns where 'r' modifies the vowel sound.
subject: English

label: Insect communication and behaviour
statement: Demonstrate the “Insect communication and behaviour” objective: Insect communication and behaviour: bees perform a waggle dance to tell hive-mates where flowers are. Ants lay pheromone trails for others to follow. Fireflies flash light patterns to find mates. Crickets chirp by rubbing their wings. Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles across continents. How insects 'talk' without words.
subject: Science

label: Multiplying fractions (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiplying fractions (age 10+)” objective: Multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction, including proper fractions by proper fractions; interpret (a/b) × q as a parts of q partitioned into b equal parts; write answers in simplest form.
subject: Mathematics

label: Weather vs Climate
statement: Demonstrate the “Weather vs Climate” objective: Distinguish between weather and climate: weather is what the atmosphere is doing right now or today (it can change hour to hour), while climate is the typical pattern of weather in a place over many years.
subject: Science

label: Helping Others Resolve Conflicts
statement: Demonstrate the “Helping Others Resolve Conflicts” objective: Mediate conflicts between others — helping two friends who are arguing by listening to both sides, helping them see each other's perspective, and guiding them toward a fair resolution.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Reading and writing numbers (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading and writing numbers (age 10+)” objective: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form; compare using >, =, < based on place-value meaning.
subject: Mathematics

label: Poetic forms and conventions
statement: Demonstrate the “Poetic forms and conventions” objective: Recognise and understand poetic conventions — including form (sonnet, ballad, free verse), metre, rhyme scheme, stanza structure, imagery, and sound devices (alliteration, assonance, onomatopoeia) — and analyse how poets use them for effect.
subject: English

label: Fast & Slow Earth Changes
statement: Demonstrate the “Fast & Slow Earth Changes” objective: Understand that Earth's surface changes: some changes are quick (eruptions, earthquakes) and some are slow (wind, water wearing away rock).
subject: Science

label: Why the Sun Looks Brightest
statement: Demonstrate the “Why the Sun Looks Brightest” objective: Explain why the Sun appears much brighter than other stars: it is the nearest star to Earth, not the biggest or brightest star in the universe — understanding the difference between apparent brightness (how bright something looks) and actual brightness.
subject: Science

label: Controlling variables (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Controlling variables (age 11+)” objective: Form a testable scientific hypothesis linking an independent variable to a predicted outcome, plan a full investigation identifying independent, dependent, and control variables, sample size, and risk assessment.
subject: Science

label: Adding money and giving change
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding money and giving change” objective: Find different combinations of coins that equal the same amount of money.
subject: Mathematics

label: Commas with yes, no, and names
statement: Demonstrate the “Commas with yes, no, and names” objective: Use commas to set off the words yes and no, to set off tag questions, and to indicate direct address in sentences.
subject: English

label: Main Topic of Informational Texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Main Topic of Informational Texts” objective: Identify the main topic and retell key details of informational texts; describe connections between individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information.
subject: English

label: Communication Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Communication Vocabulary” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of healthy communication and conflict — assertive, passive, aggressive, compromise, conflict, resolution, mediate, bystander, upstander, and peer pressure — and understand the difference between these contrasting approaches.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Weather Forecasting
statement: Demonstrate the “Weather Forecasting” objective: Know that meteorologists are scientists who study and forecast the weather using satellites, radar, weather balloons, and computer models, and that weather forecasts help people plan their activities and prepare for dangerous weather.
subject: Science

label: Layout and Formatting in Informational Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Layout and Formatting in Informational Writing” objective: Use layout devices including headings, sub-headings, columns, bullets, and tables to structure text and guide the reader through informational and explanatory writing.
subject: English

label: Counting forwards and backwards
statement: Demonstrate the “Counting forwards and backwards” objective: Count forwards and backwards in steps of 3 from 0.
subject: Mathematics

label: Spelling from Dictation
statement: Demonstrate the “Spelling from Dictation” objective: Write simple sentences from memory when dictated by the teacher, applying taught GPCs, spelling rules, and common exception words.
subject: English

label: Mentally adding tens to 3-digit numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Mentally adding tens to 3-digit numbers” objective: Mentally add and subtract a three-digit number and tens.
subject: Mathematics

label: Changes & Separation Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Changes & Separation Vocabulary” objective: Use process vocabulary for changes of state and material separation — dissolve, solution, soluble, insoluble, evaporate, condense, melt, freeze, filter, sieve, mixture, separate — and understand precisely what each term describes, including the important distinction between dissolving and melting.
subject: Science

label: Times tables (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Times tables (age 8+)” objective: Recognise and use repeated reasoning to generalise: extend patterns in times tables and equivalent fractions, derive unknown facts from known facts efficiently, describe general rules.
subject: Mathematics

label: Resultant Forces
statement: Demonstrate the “Resultant Forces” objective: Describe forces as vector quantities with both magnitude and direction, distinguish between balanced forces (zero resultant, no change in motion) and unbalanced forces (non-zero resultant, causes acceleration or deceleration).
subject: Science

label: Quoting Accurately from Texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Quoting Accurately from Texts” objective: Quote accurately from literary and informational texts when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences, using quotation marks and citations correctly.
subject: English

label: Mental addition and subtraction (age 6+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Mental addition and subtraction (age 6+)” objective: Add and subtract a two-digit number and ones mentally and using concrete/pictorial representations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Naming types of energy
statement: Demonstrate the “Naming types of energy” objective: Name and use vocabulary for types of energy and energy transfer — kinetic energy, potential energy, heat energy, light energy, sound energy, electrical energy, chemical energy, stored energy, energy transfer, energy transformation — and describe energy changes in familiar situations using these terms.
subject: Science

label: Predicting Motion Patterns
statement: Demonstrate the “Predicting Motion Patterns” objective: Make observations and measurements of an object's motion to provide evidence that a pattern can be used to predict future motion.
subject: Science

label: Percentages as Fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Percentages as Fractions” objective: Define percentage as 'number of parts per hundred'; interpret percentages and percentage changes as a fraction or a decimal; express one quantity as a percentage of another; compare quantities using percentages; work with percentages greater than 100%.
subject: Mathematics

label: Supervolcanoes & Volcanic Winter
statement: Demonstrate the “Supervolcanoes & Volcanic Winter” objective: Describe calderas such as Yellowstone and Toba as supervolcanoes capable of erupting thousands of cubic kilometres of ash; explain how sulphur dioxide aerosols in the stratosphere scatter sunlight and cause volcanic winter; discuss the Toba catastrophe theory and how giant eruptions have interacted with ice ages; contrast supervolcano eruptions with ordinary eruptions in scale and climate impact.
subject: Science

label: Resilience and Bouncing Back
statement: Demonstrate the “Resilience and Bouncing Back” objective: Understand resilience as the ability to recover from setbacks, adapt to difficult circumstances, and keep going — recognising that resilience is a skill that develops through experience, not a trait you either have or don't.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Acids, Alkalis & pH
statement: Demonstrate the “Acids, Alkalis & pH” objective: Define acids and alkalis in terms of hydrogen ion concentration, describe the pH scale (0–14), and explain how indicators are used to identify and measure acidity or alkalinity.
subject: Science

label: Two-Step Equations
statement: Demonstrate the “Two-Step Equations” objective: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations; represent problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity.
subject: Mathematics

label: Arctic vs Antarctic
statement: Demonstrate the “Arctic vs Antarctic” objective: Know that the Arctic (North Pole) and Antarctic (South Pole) are very different — the Arctic is a frozen ocean surrounded by land where people and polar bears live, while the Antarctic is a huge ice-covered continent surrounded by ocean where penguins live but no people live permanently.
subject: Science

label: The three digits of a three-digit number
statement: Demonstrate the “The three digits of a three-digit number” objective: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones.
subject: Mathematics

label: Ordering Numbers to 1000
statement: Demonstrate the “Ordering Numbers to 1000” objective: Compare and order numbers up to 1000 using >, =, and < symbols, based on place-value understanding.
subject: Mathematics

label: Area and the distributive property
statement: Demonstrate the “Area and the distributive property” objective: Use tiling to demonstrate the distributive property: the area of a rectangle with sides a and (b+c) equals a×b + a×c; use area models to represent the distributive property.
subject: Mathematics

label: Multiply & Add Problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiply & Add Problems” objective: Solve problems involving multiplying and adding, including using the distributive law, integer scaling problems, and harder correspondence problems.
subject: Mathematics

label: Controlling variables
statement: Demonstrate the “Controlling variables” objective: Plan different types of scientific enquiries to answer questions, recognising and controlling variables where necessary.
subject: Science

label: Coping with Life Changes
statement: Demonstrate the “Coping with Life Changes” objective: Understand that change is a normal part of life — such as starting school, getting a new teacher, a new baby arriving, or moving house — and identify simple strategies that help them cope with changes.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Jobs People Do
statement: Demonstrate the “Jobs People Do” objective: Different kinds of work people do; that people earn money by working; how jobs help the community; linking personal interests to possible jobs.
subject: Life Skills

label: Evidence Supporting Ideas
statement: Demonstrate the “Evidence Supporting Ideas” objective: Identify scientific evidence that has been used to support or refute ideas or arguments, evaluating the strength of evidence.
subject: Science

label: Proportional Reasoning Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Proportional Reasoning Vocabulary” objective: Know and use advanced vocabulary of multiplicative reasoning — direct proportion, inverse proportion, ratio, rate, unit rate, compound unit, scale factor — accurately in problem-solving contexts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Repeated tests for reliability
statement: Demonstrate the “Repeated tests for reliability” objective: Distinguish between precision (consistency of repeated readings) and accuracy (closeness to true value), use significant figures and standard form correctly, and choose and use appropriate measuring instruments to minimise uncertainty.
subject: Science

label: The Vast Scale of Space
statement: Demonstrate the “The Vast Scale of Space” objective: Describe the scale of the universe in nested layers: Earth is one planet in our solar system, the Sun is one star among billions in the Milky Way galaxy, and the Milky Way is one galaxy among billions in the universe.
subject: Science

label: Describing Material Properties
statement: Demonstrate the “Describing Material Properties” objective: Describe simple physical properties of everyday materials such as hard/soft, stretchy/stiff, shiny/dull, rough/smooth, waterproof/absorbent, transparent/opaque.
subject: Science

label: Planning, Revising and Editing Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Planning, Revising and Editing Writing” objective: Plan, revise, and edit writing to improve coherence and effectiveness — considering how the writing reflects its intended audience and purpose, amending vocabulary, grammar, and structure, and proofreading for accurate spelling, punctuation, and grammar.
subject: English

label: Organising Writing into Paragraphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Organising Writing into Paragraphs” objective: Organise writing into paragraphs, grouping related material around a theme, and use simple organisational devices such as headings and sub-headings in non-narrative writing.
subject: English

label: The Eight Planets
statement: Demonstrate the “The Eight Planets” objective: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune), know that Pluto is a dwarf planet, and distinguish rocky inner planets from gas giant outer planets.
subject: Science

label: Gravity & Falling Objects
statement: Demonstrate the “Gravity & Falling Objects” objective: Explain that unsupported objects fall towards the Earth because of the force of gravity acting between the Earth and the falling object.
subject: Science

label: Text Features & Presentation
statement: Demonstrate the “Text Features & Presentation” objective: Identify how language choices, text structure and presentational features (illustrations, diagrams, bold print, layout) contribute to the overall meaning and effect of a text.
subject: English

label: Word Parts as Clues
statement: Demonstrate the “Word Parts as Clues” objective: Use knowledge of common inflections and affixes (-ed, -s, un-, -er) as clues to the meaning of unknown words; understand how the prefix un- changes meaning.
subject: English

label: Making Change
statement: Demonstrate the “Making Change” objective: Calculating change from a purchase; working confidently with pounds and pence together; solving practical money problems involving addition and subtraction.
subject: Life Skills

label: Coral Reefs
statement: Demonstrate the “Coral Reefs” objective: Know that coral reefs are built by tiny living animals called coral polyps, that reefs are home to more species than almost any other ocean habitat, and that they are sometimes called the 'rainforests of the sea'.
subject: Science

label: Troy: Myth or History?
statement: Demonstrate the “Troy: Myth or History?” objective: Explore how Heinrich Schliemann's excavation at Hisarlik in modern Turkey raised questions about whether the Trojan War described in Homer's Iliad was historical, partly historical, or entirely mythical — understanding that archaeology and literary sources can support or contradict each other, and that the line between myth and history in the ancient world is often blurred.
subject: History

label: Standard English Verbs
statement: Demonstrate the “Standard English Verbs” objective: Use Standard English verb inflections in place of non-standard local forms.
subject: English

label: Grouping Living Things
statement: Demonstrate the “Grouping Living Things” objective: Recognise that living things can be grouped in a variety of ways based on observable features.
subject: Science

label: Fractions of a whole (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions of a whole (age 8+)” objective: Express whole numbers as fractions (e.g. 3 = 3/1) and recognise fractions equivalent to whole numbers (e.g. 4/4 = 1, 6/1 = 6).
subject: Mathematics

label: AI in Daily Life
statement: Demonstrate the “AI in Daily Life” objective: Spotting AI in daily life: face unlock on a phone, video recommendations, spelling auto-correct, automatic doors that detect people; technology that seems to 'know' things.
subject: Computing

label: Ethics in Business
statement: Demonstrate the “Ethics in Business” objective: Being honest, being fair, treating workers well, not harming the environment; what makes a 'good' business; whether businesses should care about more than profit.
subject: Life Skills

label: Egyptian Gods and Goddesses
statement: Demonstrate the “Egyptian Gods and Goddesses” objective: Name and describe key Egyptian gods and goddesses: Ra the sun god who sailed across the sky each day, Osiris the ruler of the afterlife, Isis the goddess of magic and motherhood, Anubis the jackal-headed god of mummification, Horus the falcon-headed sky god, Thoth the ibis-headed god of writing, and Bastet the cat goddess of protection.
subject: History

label: Modern Archaeology and Egyptian Ethics
statement: Demonstrate the “Modern Archaeology and Egyptian Ethics” objective: Understand that modern Egyptologists use advanced technologies — CT scanning of mummies, satellite imagery to find buried structures, DNA analysis — alongside traditional excavation, and think critically about the ethics of archaeology: whether mummies should be displayed in museums, who owns ancient artefacts, and how colonial-era collecting affects how we study and present ancient Egypt today.
subject: History

label: Arrays for multiplication (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Arrays for multiplication (age 7+)” objective: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends.
subject: Mathematics

label: Pushes & Pulls
statement: Demonstrate the “Pushes & Pulls” objective: Understand that pushes and pulls are forces that can change the speed or direction of an object's motion, and compare the effects of different strengths and directions.
subject: Science

label: Number Sets & Infinity
statement: Demonstrate the “Number Sets & Infinity” objective: Appreciate the infinite nature of the sets of integers, real numbers, and rational numbers; position integers on a number line and distinguish between rational and irrational numbers.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Particle Model
statement: Demonstrate the “The Particle Model” objective: Use the particle model to explain the properties of solids, liquids, and gases — including differences in arrangement, movement, and spacing — and apply the model to explain density, compressibility, and the anomalous expansion of water.
subject: Science

label: Simplifying Fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Simplifying Fractions” objective: Use common factors to simplify fractions to their simplest form; use common multiples to express fractions with a common denominator.
subject: Mathematics

label: Grammar Terms: Clauses and Conjunctions
statement: Demonstrate the “Grammar Terms: Clauses and Conjunctions” objective: Use and understand Year 3 grammatical terminology accurately when discussing reading and writing: preposition, conjunction, word family, prefix, clause, subordinate clause, direct speech, consonant letter, vowel letter, inverted commas/speech marks.
subject: English

label: Evidence-Based Classification
statement: Demonstrate the “Evidence-Based Classification” objective: Give reasons for classifying plants and animals based on specific characteristics, using evidence to justify classification decisions.
subject: Science

label: Parts of Plant and Animal Cells
statement: Demonstrate the “Parts of Plant and Animal Cells” objective: Describe the functions of the main components of plant and animal cells: cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, vacuole, mitochondria, ribosomes, and chloroplasts.
subject: Science

label: Borrowing & Debt
statement: Demonstrate the “Borrowing & Debt” objective: What borrowing money means; that loans must be repaid with interest; what credit is; why too much debt can be risky; responsible borrowing.
subject: Life Skills

label: Pitching an Idea
statement: Demonstrate the “Pitching an Idea” objective: Presenting a business idea to others convincingly; explaining what makes it good and why people should support it; building confidence in public speaking about ideas.
subject: Life Skills

label: Scatter Graphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Scatter Graphs” objective: Plot bivariate data on a scatter graph with correctly labelled axes and appropriate scales; describe the correlation (positive, negative, none) and draw an estimated line of best fit where appropriate.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Carbon Cycle
statement: Demonstrate the “The Carbon Cycle” objective: Describe the carbon cycle, tracing carbon through photosynthesis, respiration, feeding, decomposition, and combustion, and explain the role of each process.
subject: Science

label: Line graphs (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Line graphs (age 10+)” objective: Interpret and construct pie charts and line graphs; use these to solve problems.
subject: Mathematics

label: Egyptian Social Hierarchy
statement: Demonstrate the “Egyptian Social Hierarchy” objective: Describe the social structure of ancient Egypt as a pyramid-shaped hierarchy: the pharaoh at the top, then priests and nobles, followed by scribes and soldiers, then craftworkers and merchants, and farmers and labourers at the base — understanding that a person's position was usually inherited and determined their whole way of life.
subject: History

label: Angles in triangles (age 6+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Angles in triangles (age 6+)” objective: Distinguish defining attributes of shapes (e.g. triangles are closed and three-sided) from non-defining attributes (e.g. colour, orientation, overall size).
subject: Mathematics

label: Comparing and ordering measurements
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing and ordering measurements” objective: Compare and order lengths, mass, and capacity and record results using >, <, and =.
subject: Mathematics

label: Radiometric Dating
statement: Demonstrate the “Radiometric Dating” objective: Explain how radiometric dating works — radioactive isotopes decay at a known rate (half-life), so measuring the ratio of parent to daughter isotope in a rock or fossil gives an absolute age; distinguish between carbon-14 (useful up to ~50,000 years) and uranium-lead (useful for millions to billions of years).
subject: Science

label: Historical Sources on Ancient Egypt
statement: Demonstrate the “Historical Sources on Ancient Egypt” objective: Explain how knowledge of ancient Egypt is built from multiple source types — inscriptions, papyri, artefacts, and physical remains — and critically evaluate each: what biases, gaps, and distortions exist? Explore how Champollion’s decipherment of hieroglyphs transformed the field, and why the same artefact can be interpreted differently by different scholars.
subject: History

label: Ring of Fire
statement: Demonstrate the “Ring of Fire” objective: Recognise that volcanoes and earthquakes tend to happen in certain places — especially around the edges of the Pacific Ocean (Ring of Fire) — not randomly across the Earth.
subject: Science

label: Segmenting words into sounds
statement: Demonstrate the “Segmenting words into sounds” objective: Segment spoken words into phonemes and spell CVC and simple phonetically regular words by writing a letter or letters for each sound.
subject: English

label: What is a minibeast?
statement: Demonstrate the “What is a minibeast?” objective: What is a minibeast? Small creatures without backbones, found in gardens, parks, and woodland. Bug hunts — searching under logs, stones, and leaves using magnifying glasses to observe minibeasts up close.
subject: Science

label: Days, Weeks, Months & Years
statement: Demonstrate the “Days, Weeks, Months & Years” objective: Recognise and use language relating to dates, including days of the week, weeks, months, and years.
subject: Mathematics

label: Medieval Pyramid of Power
statement: Demonstrate the “Medieval Pyramid of Power” objective: How medieval society was organised: king at the top, then lords, then knights, then peasants/serfs; who owed what to whom; the pyramid of power and mutual obligations.
subject: History

label: Animal Migration
statement: Demonstrate the “Animal Migration” objective: Know that many animals make incredible journeys called migrations — Arctic terns fly from pole to pole, monarch butterflies travel thousands of miles across North America, wildebeest cross the Serengeti following rain, and humpback whales swim between polar feeding grounds and tropical breeding waters — and that these journeys are linked to food, breeding, and seasons.
subject: Science

label: Fossils & Palaeontologists
statement: Demonstrate the “Fossils & Palaeontologists” objective: Understand that fossils are the remains of ancient living things preserved in rock, and that scientists called palaeontologists study fossils to learn about dinosaurs.
subject: Science

label: Personal Growth Over Time
statement: Demonstrate the “Personal Growth Over Time” objective: Reflect on your own growth over time — the things that challenge you now are not fixed, and noticing how you have already changed builds genuine self-knowledge.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: The first Olympics
statement: Demonstrate the “The first Olympics” objective: Know that the Olympic Games began in ancient Greece at a place called Olympia as athletic competitions held in honour of Zeus, and that the modern Olympic Games we watch today were inspired by those ancient games.
subject: History

label: Adapting Speech to Context
statement: Demonstrate the “Adapting Speech to Context” objective: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, using formal English when appropriate to task and situation while adjusting tone, vocabulary, and style for different audiences.
subject: English

label: Power of Eruptions
statement: Demonstrate the “Power of Eruptions” objective: Appreciate that volcanic eruptions are powerful events that can change the landscape.
subject: Science

label: Writing Character & Dialogue
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing Character & Dialogue” objective: Write narratives that develop real or imagined experiences using effective technique — including establishing context and point of view, developing characters through dialogue, pacing, and description, using varied transitions, and providing a reflective conclusion.
subject: English

label: Plural vs Possessive in Nouns
statement: Demonstrate the “Plural vs Possessive in Nouns” objective: Distinguish between the plural -s suffix and the possessive -'s suffix in nouns.
subject: English

label: Famous Dinosaur Species
statement: Demonstrate the “Famous Dinosaur Species” objective: Recognise and name common well-known dinosaur species: Tyrannosaurus rex, Triceratops, Stegosaurus, and Brachiosaurus/Diplodocus, describing a basic feature of each.
subject: Science

label: Thunder & Lightning
statement: Demonstrate the “Thunder & Lightning” objective: Know that thunder and lightning happen during thunderstorms: lightning is a giant spark of electricity that forms in clouds, thunder is the sound the lightning makes, and we see lightning before hearing thunder because light travels faster than sound.
subject: Science

label: Powers of Ten Notation
statement: Demonstrate the “Powers of Ten Notation” objective: Interpret and compare numbers in standard form A × 10ⁿ where 1 ≤ A < 10 and n is an integer; convert between ordinary numbers and standard form.
subject: Mathematics

label: Energy Loss Between Levels
statement: Demonstrate the “Energy Loss Between Levels” objective: Explain how energy is transferred between trophic levels in a food chain, why energy is lost at each stage, and use pyramids of biomass/numbers to represent this.
subject: Science

label: AI Mistakes and Limitations
statement: Demonstrate the “AI Mistakes and Limitations” objective: Machines make mistakes; they only know what they've been shown; bad training data leads to bad results; AI is not magic — just maths on data; showing edge cases and failures.
subject: Computing

label: Types of rocks
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of rocks” objective: Use vocabulary for Earth's geological processes and rock types — igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic, erosion, weathering, deposition, fossil, sediment, strata, permeable, impermeable — and apply these when explaining how rocks form and how landscapes change over time.
subject: Science

label: Classification Keys
statement: Demonstrate the “Classification Keys” objective: Explore and use classification keys to identify, group, and name living things in local and wider environments.
subject: Science

label: Vowel Digraphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Vowel Digraphs” objective: Read and spell words containing common vowel digraphs (ai, ay, ee, ea, oa, oe, oo, oi, oy) including where a digraph can represent more than one sound.
subject: English

label: Spotting Constellations
statement: Demonstrate the “Spotting Constellations” objective: Recognise a few star patterns (constellations) in the night sky, starting with the Big Dipper (the Plough), and understand that the North Star (Polaris) can be found using the Big Dipper.
subject: Science

label: Egyptian Gods and the Afterlife
statement: Demonstrate the “Egyptian Gods and the Afterlife” objective: Understand that the ancient Egyptians believed in many gods and goddesses and believed that life continued after death in a wonderful afterlife — which is why they took great care to prepare bodies and fill tombs with food, jewellery, and precious objects for the dead person to use.
subject: History

label: The Circulatory System
statement: Demonstrate the “The Circulatory System” objective: Identify and name the main parts of the human circulatory system and describe the functions of the heart, blood vessels, and blood.
subject: Science

label: Moon Phases
statement: Demonstrate the “Moon Phases” objective: Observe and describe the Moon's changing shape over about a month, recognising that it goes through a repeating cycle of phases from new moon (invisible) to full moon (complete circle) and back again.
subject: Science

label: Predator Hunting Strategies
statement: Demonstrate the “Predator Hunting Strategies” objective: Understand that predators have evolved hunting strategies — wolves hunt in packs, chameleons use their long tongues, spiders build webs, crocodiles ambush at water's edge — and prey animals have evolved defences — porcupine spines, skunk spray, poison dart frog toxins, zebra stripes confusing predators, playing dead.
subject: Science

label: Hidden Voices of Greece and Rome
statement: Demonstrate the “Hidden Voices of Greece and Rome” objective: Examine the lives of people usually left out of the Greek and Roman story — enslaved people who made up roughly 30% of Athens and powered Rome's economy, women whose lives varied dramatically between Athens (largely confined to the home) and Sparta (physical training, property ownership), and conquered peoples across both empires — and evaluate whose voices are missing from the historical record and why.
subject: History

label: Pictograms and tally charts
statement: Demonstrate the “Pictograms and tally charts” objective: Interpret and construct simple pictograms, tally charts, block diagrams, and simple tables.
subject: Mathematics

label: Egyptian Timelines and Maps
statement: Demonstrate the “Egyptian Timelines and Maps” objective: Read and construct historical timelines — place Ancient Egyptian periods, pharaohs, and key events on a timeline relative to each other and to the present day; interpret maps showing the Nile delta, trade routes, and the location of key sites.
subject: History

label: Split Digraphs and Magic E
statement: Demonstrate the “Split Digraphs and Magic E” objective: Read and spell words containing split digraphs (a-e, e-e, i-e, o-e, u-e) where a final 'e' makes the preceding vowel long.
subject: English

label: Cells, Tissues & Organs
statement: Demonstrate the “Cells, Tissues & Organs” objective: Understand that the body is organised in a hierarchy: tiny cells are the building blocks, groups of similar cells form tissues, tissues combine into organs (like the heart or stomach), and organs work together in organ systems (like the circulatory system).
subject: Science

label: Commutative Multiplication
statement: Demonstrate the “Commutative Multiplication” objective: Understand and apply the commutative property of multiplication and recognise that division is not commutative.
subject: Mathematics

label: Writing for an audience
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing for an audience” objective: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organisation are appropriate to the task, purpose, and audience, maintaining a consistent style and structure throughout.
subject: English

label: Adding Fractions (Same Denominator)
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding Fractions (Same Denominator)” objective: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator, including results greater than one whole (e.g. 5/8 + 6/8 = 11/8).
subject: Mathematics

label: Invasive Species
statement: Demonstrate the “Invasive Species” objective: Understand that invasive species are animals (or plants) that have been introduced to a place where they don't naturally belong — like grey squirrels outcompeting red squirrels in the UK, cane toads poisoning native predators in Australia, or rabbits devastating ecosystems in Australia — and that they can cause serious harm to native wildlife by competing for food, spreading disease, or having no natural predators.
subject: Science

label: Drawing Conclusions from Discussion
statement: Demonstrate the “Drawing Conclusions from Discussion” objective: Review the key ideas expressed in discussions and draw conclusions in light of information and knowledge gained from the discussion.
subject: English

label: Fluent adding and subtracting within 100
statement: Demonstrate the “Fluent adding and subtracting within 100” objective: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
subject: Mathematics

label: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Two-step addition and subtraction problems” objective: Solve addition and subtraction two-step problems in contexts, deciding which operations and methods to use and why.
subject: Mathematics

label: Angles in triangles (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Angles in triangles (age 10+)” objective: Find unknown angles in triangles, quadrilaterals, and regular polygons using angle sum properties.
subject: Mathematics

label: Emotional Patterns Over Time
statement: Demonstrate the “Emotional Patterns Over Time” objective: Reflect on their own emotional patterns over time — noticing recurring triggers, understanding their typical responses, and recognising how their emotional awareness has grown.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Offspring resemble parents
statement: Demonstrate the “Offspring resemble parents” objective: Observe that young plants and animals resemble their parents but are not identical, recognising inherited similarities and individual differences.
subject: Science

label: Fractions of amounts
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions of amounts” objective: Recognise, find, name, and write fractions 1/3, 1/4, 2/4, and 3/4 of a length, shape, set of objects, or quantity.
subject: Mathematics

label: Calculating the Mean
statement: Demonstrate the “Calculating the Mean” objective: Calculate and interpret the mean as an average of a data set.
subject: Mathematics

label: Bar graphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Bar graphs” objective: Interpret and present discrete and continuous data using appropriate graphical methods, including bar charts and time graphs.
subject: Mathematics

label: Mummification Step by Step
statement: Demonstrate the “Mummification Step by Step” objective: Describe the step-by-step process of mummification: the body was washed, internal organs were removed and placed in canopic jars, the body was dried with natron salt for 40 days, then wrapped in linen bandages with amulets tucked between the layers, and finally placed in a decorated coffin (sarcophagus).
subject: History

label: Personal Goal-Setting
statement: Demonstrate the “Personal Goal-Setting” objective: Set realistic personal goals, create a simple plan to achieve them, monitor their own progress, and adjust their approach when things aren't working.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Penguins
statement: Demonstrate the “Penguins” objective: Know key facts about penguins — they live in the Antarctic and Southern Hemisphere, they cannot fly but are excellent swimmers, Emperor penguins are the largest and huddle together in winter to keep warm, and penguin parents take turns keeping their egg warm on their feet in freezing temperatures.
subject: Science

label: Plant Reproduction
statement: Demonstrate the “Plant Reproduction” objective: Describe the structure of a flower and explain the processes of wind and insect pollination, fertilisation, seed and fruit formation, and seed dispersal in plants.
subject: Science

label: Power: watts and energy per second
statement: Demonstrate the “Power: watts and energy per second” objective: Define power as the rate of energy transfer (power = energy ÷ time, measured in watts), and compare energy transfer rates in different everyday contexts.
subject: Science

label: Habitats & Basic Needs
statement: Demonstrate the “Habitats & Basic Needs” objective: Identify that most living things live in habitats to which they are suited and describe how habitats provide for basic needs and how organisms depend on each other.
subject: Science

label: Earth's Frozen Water
statement: Demonstrate the “Earth's Frozen Water” objective: Understand the cryosphere and its role in Earth's water system — the cryosphere is all frozen water on Earth (ice sheets, glaciers, sea ice, permafrost, snow cover); polar ice sheets hold about 69% of Earth's fresh water; if all polar ice melted, sea levels would rise over 65 metres; and the water cycle connects polar ice to the global system through evaporation, precipitation, and meltwater flowing into oceans.
subject: Science

label: Questioning Your Own Biases
statement: Demonstrate the “Questioning Your Own Biases” objective: Reflect on their own assumptions and biases — recognising that everyone carries unconscious assumptions about others, and that actively questioning these assumptions is an ongoing practice that leads to greater fairness and empathy.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Natural Disaster Solutions
statement: Demonstrate the “Natural Disaster Solutions” objective: Generate and compare multiple solutions to reduce the impacts of natural Earth processes on humans, such as earthquakes, floods, or volcanic eruptions.
subject: Science

label: Coin Values
statement: Demonstrate the “Coin Values” objective: Recognise and know the value of different coins and notes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Being a Good Seller
statement: Demonstrate the “Being a Good Seller” objective: Customer service, fairness, and honesty in business; keeping promises to customers; why being trustworthy matters for repeat business and reputation.
subject: Life Skills

label: Reading tables
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading tables” objective: Complete, read, and interpret information in tables, including timetables.
subject: Mathematics

label: Measuring length (age 6+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring length (age 6+)” objective: Measure the length of an object using same-size length units laid end to end with no gaps or overlaps.
subject: Mathematics

label: Siege Warfare
statement: Demonstrate the “Siege Warfare” objective: How castles were attacked and defended: siege weapons (trebuchets, battering rams, siege towers), boiling liquids, arrow slits, murder holes; the drama of a medieval siege.
subject: History

label: Making Something to Sell
statement: Demonstrate the “Making Something to Sell” objective: The experience of creating a product to sell — a craft, a drawing, baked goods; what makes something worth buying; pride in making something others want.
subject: Life Skills

label: Athens Versus Sparta
statement: Demonstrate the “Athens Versus Sparta” objective: Compare Athens and Sparta as two very different Greek city-states: Athens focused on learning, arts, debate, and democracy, while Sparta focused on military training, discipline, and obedience — and understand that a city-state was a city that ruled itself like a small country.
subject: History

label: Reading Cladograms
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading Cladograms” objective: Read and create simple cladograms (branching diagrams) that show how groups of dinosaurs are related based on shared features, understanding that species sharing more features are more closely related.
subject: Science

label: Taxes & Public Services
statement: Demonstrate the “Taxes & Public Services” objective: What taxes are and why people pay them; how taxes fund schools, hospitals, roads, and emergency services; that governments decide how to spend tax money.
subject: Life Skills

label: Expanded noun phrases
statement: Demonstrate the “Expanded noun phrases” objective: Use expanded noun phrases to describe and specify, adding adjectives and other modifiers before a noun (e.g., 'the blue butterfly', 'the old, creaky door').
subject: English

label: Fractions on a number line (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions on a number line (age 9+)” objective: Move fluently between real-world situations, diagrams, number lines, bar models, and symbolic equations involving multi-digit multiplication, fractions, decimals, and percentages, explaining connections between representations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Greek Philosophers and Medicine
statement: Demonstrate the “Greek Philosophers and Medicine” objective: Know that Greek thinkers called philosophers developed ways of understanding the world that still influence us today — Socrates asked challenging questions to test ideas (the Socratic method), Plato imagined the ideal society, Aristotle observed and classified the natural world — and that Hippocrates is called the father of medicine for insisting on natural causes of illness rather than blaming the gods.
subject: History

label: Writing a Précis
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing a Précis” objective: Precis longer passages by summarising the main ideas and key information concisely while maintaining the essential meaning and removing non-essential detail.
subject: English

label: AI and Fairness in Decisions
statement: Demonstrate the “AI and Fairness in Decisions” objective: Whether AI should make important decisions about people: jobs, loans, justice; who is responsible when AI makes unfair decisions; introduction to algorithmic fairness.
subject: Computing

label: Using evidence to answer questions
statement: Demonstrate the “Using evidence to answer questions” objective: Identify differences, similarities, or changes related to scientific ideas and use straightforward scientific evidence to answer questions or support findings.
subject: Science

label: Basic Body Needs
statement: Demonstrate the “Basic Body Needs” objective: Know that the body needs food for energy, water to stay hydrated, sleep to rest and grow, and exercise to keep muscles and the heart strong — and that these are basic needs every human body has.
subject: Science

label: How Materials Change State
statement: Demonstrate the “How Materials Change State” objective: Explain melting, freezing, boiling, condensing, and sublimation using the particle model, interpreting heating and cooling curves to identify melting and boiling points.
subject: Science

label: Conductors and insulators
statement: Demonstrate the “Conductors and insulators” objective: Recognise some common conductors and insulators, and associate metals with being good conductors of electricity.
subject: Science

label: Choosing mathematical tools
statement: Demonstrate the “Choosing mathematical tools” objective: Select and use appropriate tools and representations strategically: choose between mental, written, and diagrammatic methods; use calculators for checking; select fraction models suited to the task.
subject: Mathematics

label: Polar Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Polar Animals” objective: Explore animals of the Arctic and Antarctic — polar bears, Arctic foxes, and walruses in the north; penguins, seals, and albatrosses in the south — and understand how polar animals survive extreme cold through thick fur or blubber, huddling behaviour, and seasonal changes like white winter coats.
subject: Science

label: Counting Unit Cubes
statement: Demonstrate the “Counting Unit Cubes” objective: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes using cubic cm, cubic in, cubic ft, and other units.
subject: Mathematics

label: Converting measurement units
statement: Demonstrate the “Converting measurement units” objective: Convert between different units of measure (e.g. kilometre to metre, hour to minute, minute to second, year to month, week to day).
subject: Mathematics

label: Building a simple circuit
statement: Demonstrate the “Building a simple circuit” objective: Construct a simple series electrical circuit, identifying and naming its basic parts: cells, wires, bulbs, switches, and buzzers.
subject: Science

label: Climate Change Basics
statement: Demonstrate the “Climate Change Basics” objective: Understand the basics of climate change: Earth’s atmosphere traps some of the Sun's heat (the greenhouse effect), burning fossil fuels adds extra greenhouse gases (especially CO₂), this is making Earth gradually warmer, and this warming changes weather patterns, melts ice, and raises sea levels.
subject: Science

label: Types of Teeth
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of Teeth” objective: Identify the different types of human teeth (incisors, canines, molars) and describe their functions in eating.
subject: Science

label: Rainforest Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Animals” objective: Explore animals of the tropical rainforest — the most species-rich habitat on Earth — learning that the forest has layers (canopy, understory, forest floor) with different animals at each level: toucans and monkeys in the canopy, jaguars and frogs on the floor, and that rainforests are found near the equator.
subject: Science

label: Reducing Human Impact
statement: Demonstrate the “Reducing Human Impact” objective: Communicate solutions that will reduce the impact of humans on the land, water, air, and other living things in the local environment.
subject: Science

label: Heating experiments and Q = mcΔT
statement: Demonstrate the “Heating experiments and Q = mcΔT” objective: Plan and carry out experiments to measure energy transferred during heating, including using the equation Q = mcΔT, recording temperature changes over time, and evaluating sources of error.
subject: Science

label: Dressing for the Weather
statement: Demonstrate the “Dressing for the Weather” objective: Choose appropriate clothing and equipment for different weather conditions — coat and umbrella for rain, sun hat and sunscreen for hot sun, warm layers for cold — understanding that weather affects what we do and how we prepare each day.
subject: Science

label: Plant-Eaters vs Meat-Eaters
statement: Demonstrate the “Plant-Eaters vs Meat-Eaters” objective: Sort dinosaurs into plant-eaters (herbivores) and meat-eaters (carnivores) by looking at clues like tooth shape — flat teeth for plants, sharp teeth for meat.
subject: Science

label: Learning from Failure
statement: Demonstrate the “Learning from Failure” objective: Not every business idea works; entrepreneurs try, fail, learn, and try again; iteration and resilience as core entrepreneurial skills; famous failure-to-success stories.
subject: Life Skills

label: The world contains many cultures, traditions
statement: Demonstrate the “The world contains many cultures, traditions” objective: Understand that the world contains many cultures, traditions, and belief systems, and that learning about others' perspectives enriches our own understanding — developing genuine curiosity about and respect for cultural diversity.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Addition and subtraction word problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Addition and subtraction word problems” objective: Solve word problems involving lengths within 100, using addition and subtraction with drawings and equations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Mixed and Conflicting Emotions
statement: Demonstrate the “Mixed and Conflicting Emotions” objective: Understand that people can experience mixed or conflicting emotions at the same time — feeling excited and nervous about starting a new school, or happy for a friend who won but disappointed for yourself.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Using and Evaluating Textual Evidence
statement: Demonstrate the “Using and Evaluating Textual Evidence” objective: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of what a text says explicitly and what can be inferred, distinguishing between strong and weak evidence and explaining how the evidence supports a point.
subject: English

label: How Many in Total?
statement: Demonstrate the “How Many in Total?” objective: Cardinality principle: the last number said when counting a set tells how many objects are in the set, regardless of arrangement or order counted.
subject: Mathematics

label: Letter Formation Families
statement: Demonstrate the “Letter Formation Families” objective: Understand which letters belong to which handwriting families based on similar formation patterns and practise letters in groups.
subject: English

label: Properties of triangles and quadrilaterals
statement: Demonstrate the “Properties of triangles and quadrilaterals” objective: Derive and illustrate properties of triangles, quadrilaterals, and circles using appropriate language, including interior angles, diagonals, symmetry, and relationships between side lengths.
subject: Mathematics

label: Choosing measurement units
statement: Demonstrate the “Choosing measurement units” objective: Choose and use appropriate standard units to measure length (m/cm), mass (kg/g), temperature (°C), and capacity (litres/ml) to the nearest appropriate unit.
subject: Mathematics

label: Castle Design Through the Ages
statement: Demonstrate the “Castle Design Through the Ages” objective: How castles were built and evolved: from wooden motte-and-bailey to stone keeps to concentric castles; rooms and their uses; how castle design responded to new attack methods.
subject: History

label: Tenths (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Tenths (age 8+)” objective: Count up and down in hundredths; recognise that hundredths arise when dividing an object by 100 or dividing tenths by 10.
subject: Mathematics

label: Dinosaurs Were Real
statement: Demonstrate the “Dinosaurs Were Real” objective: Understand that dinosaurs were real animals that lived on Earth a very long time ago and are now extinct — none are alive today.
subject: Science

label: How Sound Waves Travel
statement: Demonstrate the “How Sound Waves Travel” objective: Explain that sound is produced by vibrating objects and travels as a longitudinal pressure wave through solids, liquids, and gases; describe reflection of sound (echoes) and absorption; explain why sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
subject: Science

label: Deep-Sea Creatures
statement: Demonstrate the “Deep-Sea Creatures” objective: Explore life in the deep sea: animals that make their own light (bioluminescence), creatures adapted to crushing pressure and total darkness, and hydrothermal vents where life thrives without sunlight.
subject: Science

label: Fraction-Decimal Equivalents
statement: Demonstrate the “Fraction-Decimal Equivalents” objective: Recognise and write decimal equivalents of 1/4, 1/2, and 3/4.
subject: Mathematics

label: Research & Note-Taking
statement: Demonstrate the “Research & Note-Taking” objective: Gather relevant information from print and digital sources, summarise or paraphrase information in notes and finished work, and provide a basic bibliography or list of sources.
subject: English

label: Reporting & Recounting
statement: Demonstrate the “Reporting & Recounting” objective: Report on a topic or recount an experience with organised facts and descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.
subject: English

label: Active, Dormant & Extinct
statement: Demonstrate the “Active, Dormant & Extinct” objective: Classify volcanoes as active (could erupt any time), dormant (sleeping but could wake up), or extinct (will not erupt again).
subject: Science

label: Figurative Language and Literary Devices
statement: Demonstrate the “Figurative Language and Literary Devices” objective: Determine the meaning of figurative and connotative language in context, analyse the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, and identify literary devices such as metaphor, simile, personification, allusion, and irony.
subject: English

label: Shape patterns
statement: Demonstrate the “Shape patterns” objective: Look for and use mathematical structure: apply properties of operations, place-value patterns, and relationships between shapes to solve problems efficiently.
subject: Mathematics

label: Understanding fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding fractions” objective: Move fluently between real-world situations, diagrams, and symbolic equations involving three-digit numbers and fractions, explaining what each part represents.
subject: Mathematics

label: Written Multiplication & Division
statement: Demonstrate the “Written Multiplication & Division” objective: Write and calculate mathematical statements for multiplication and division using known tables, including two-digit × one-digit, using mental and progressing to formal written methods.
subject: Mathematics

label: Narrator's Point of View
statement: Demonstrate the “Narrator's Point of View” objective: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including distinguishing between first-person and third-person narration and explaining how the narrator's perspective shapes the reader's understanding.
subject: English

label: Animal Nutrition
statement: Demonstrate the “Animal Nutrition” objective: Understand that animals, including humans, need the right types and amounts of nutrition, and that animals cannot make their own food.
subject: Science

label: Boudicca's Revolt Against Rome
statement: Demonstrate the “Boudicca's Revolt Against Rome” objective: Tell the story of Boudicca, queen of the Iceni tribe, who led a fierce revolt against Roman rule in Britain — burning Colchester, London, and St Albans — before her army was defeated, and understand her significance as a symbol of resistance against a powerful empire.
subject: History

label: What Is an Earthquake
statement: Demonstrate the “What Is an Earthquake” objective: Know what an earthquake is: a sudden shaking of the ground that can be strong or weak.
subject: Science

label: Testing Materials for Uses
statement: Demonstrate the “Testing Materials for Uses” objective: Give reasons, based on evidence from comparative and fair tests, for the particular uses of everyday materials including metals, wood, and plastic.
subject: Science

label: Types of angles (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of angles (age 8+)” objective: Use and interpret standard geometric diagram conventions: mark right angles with a small square, equal lengths with single or double tick marks, and equal angles with arc marks; label angles in three-letter notation (∠ABC) and individual angles with a single letter or number; draw diagrams showing angles at a point, angles on a straight line, and angles inside polygons with these conventions; read diagrams with these marks to identify given information and find unknown values.
subject: Mathematics

label: Measuring length (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring length (age 7+)” objective: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, metre sticks, and measuring tapes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Hidden and Masked Feelings
statement: Demonstrate the “Hidden and Masked Feelings” objective: Recognise that people sometimes hide or mask their true feelings — smiling when they're actually sad, or saying 'I'm fine' when they're not — and understand why someone might do this.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Reading between the lines
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading between the lines” objective: Ask and answer questions about key details in literary and informational texts; make simple inferences based on what characters say and do.
subject: English

label: Antonyms & Synonyms
statement: Demonstrate the “Antonyms & Synonyms” objective: Demonstrate understanding of words by relating them to their antonyms (opposites) and synonyms (words with similar meanings), using synonym and antonym relationships to refine vocabulary and improve precision in writing.
subject: English

label: Plants and animals in their habitats
statement: Demonstrate the “Plants and animals in their habitats” objective: Use a model to represent the relationship between the needs of different plants and animals and the places they live, connecting organism needs to habitat features.
subject: Science

label: Pharaohs and Tutankhamun
statement: Demonstrate the “Pharaohs and Tutankhamun” objective: Know that ancient Egypt was ruled by powerful kings and queens called pharaohs, who lived in grand palaces and made the laws — and that one of the most famous pharaohs is Tutankhamun, a boy who became pharaoh as a child and whose golden tomb was discovered thousands of years later.
subject: History

label: Fraction Word Problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Fraction Word Problems” objective: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with unlike denominators, using visual models and benchmark fractions to estimate and assess reasonableness.
subject: Mathematics

label: Number bonds to 9
statement: Demonstrate the “Number bonds to 9” objective: Find the number that makes 10 when added to a given number from 1 to 9 (number bonds to 10).
subject: Mathematics

label: Structural Adaptations
statement: Demonstrate the “Structural Adaptations” objective: Understand that animals have structural adaptations (body features like the giraffe's long neck, eagle's talons, dolphin's streamlined shape), behavioural adaptations (migration, hibernation, tool use), and physiological adaptations (antifreeze in Arctic fish blood, echolocation in bats) — and that these developed over many generations through natural selection.
subject: Science

label: Expanded noun phrases (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Expanded noun phrases (age 8+)” objective: Expand noun phrases with modifying adjectives, nouns, and preposition phrases to add detail.
subject: English

label: Equivalent fractions (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Equivalent fractions (age 9+)” objective: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to (n×a)/(n×b) using visual models; use this principle to recognise and generate equivalent fractions, including tenths and hundredths.
subject: Mathematics

label: Connecting Representations
statement: Demonstrate the “Connecting Representations” objective: Move between real-world situations, drawings, and number sentences, explaining how each representation connects to the others (quantitative reasoning).
subject: Mathematics

label: Hazard Assessment & Evacuation
statement: Demonstrate the “Hazard Assessment & Evacuation” objective: Explain probabilistic hazard assessment using eruption recurrence intervals and fault slip rates; describe how volcano observatories monitor ground deformation, gas emissions, and seismicity to issue alert levels; explore why communities remain near active hazards (fertile volcanic soil, poverty, cultural ties); discuss the ethics and politics of evacuation decisions and the social justice dimensions of disaster risk.
subject: Science

label: Place Value × 10 and ÷ 10
statement: Demonstrate the “Place Value × 10 and ÷ 10” objective: Recognise that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.
subject: Mathematics

label: Recommendation Systems and Filter Bubbles
statement: Demonstrate the “Recommendation Systems and Filter Bubbles” objective: How recommendation systems work: YouTube, Netflix, and shop websites track what you click and find patterns; filter bubbles; the difference between helpful suggestions and manipulation.
subject: Computing

label: In-Depth Character and Setting Analysis
statement: Demonstrate the “In-Depth Character and Setting Analysis” objective: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details from the text such as a character's thoughts, words, actions, and interactions.
subject: English

label: Transformations on a Grid
statement: Demonstrate the “Transformations on a Grid” objective: Identify, describe, and represent the position of a shape following a reflection or translation using appropriate language; know that the shape has not changed.
subject: Mathematics

label: Rock Layers & Relative Dating
statement: Demonstrate the “Rock Layers & Relative Dating” objective: Understand that rock layers (strata) form in sequence with the oldest at the bottom and the youngest at the top, and that fossils found in deeper layers are older — this is the principle of relative dating.
subject: Science

label: Conservation of Mass
statement: Demonstrate the “Conservation of Mass” objective: Measure and provide evidence that the total weight of matter is conserved regardless of the type of change (heating, cooling, or mixing).
subject: Science

label: Inverse: addition undoes subtraction
statement: Demonstrate the “Inverse: addition undoes subtraction” objective: Recognise and use the inverse relationship between addition and subtraction to check calculations and solve missing-number problems.
subject: Mathematics

label: Inclusion and Exclusion in Athens
statement: Demonstrate the “Inclusion and Exclusion in Athens” objective: Analyse who was included and excluded from Athenian democracy — only free adult male citizens (roughly 30% of adults) could participate, while women, enslaved people (who may have made up a third of the population), and foreign residents (metics) were excluded — and evaluate whether Athens truly deserves the title 'birthplace of democracy' by comparing it with modern representative democracies.
subject: History

label: Naming the Planets
statement: Demonstrate the “Naming the Planets” objective: Name the planets in our solar system in order from the Sun and use vocabulary for space — planet, star, sun, moon, satellite, orbit, solar system, galaxy, universe, asteroid, comet — applying these correctly when describing the structure of the solar system and objects we see in the sky.
subject: Science

label: Estimating answers (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Estimating answers (age 9+)” objective: Apply the area formula (l × w) and perimeter formula (2l + 2w) for rectangles including squares in real-world and mathematical problems; calculate and compare areas using standard units (cm², m²) and estimate areas of irregular shapes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Journey to Mars
statement: Demonstrate the “Journey to Mars” objective: Evaluate the engineering and human challenges of long-duration spaceflight to Mars — radiation exposure, muscle and bone loss, psychological isolation, communication delays — and assess the current state of the SETI programme: what methods are used, what has been detected so far, and what the Fermi Paradox is.
subject: Science

label: Pictograms and tally charts (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Pictograms and tally charts (age 11+)” objective: Construct and interpret frequency tables, bar charts, pie charts, pictograms, and vertical line charts for both categorical and grouped numerical data, choosing appropriate representations for the data type.
subject: Mathematics

label: Multi-Step Multiply & Divide
statement: Demonstrate the “Multi-Step Multiply & Divide” objective: Solve problems involving multiplication and division, including scaling problems and correspondence problems where n objects are connected to m objects.
subject: Mathematics

label: Area of compound shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Area of compound shapes” objective: Recognise area as additive; find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing into non-overlapping rectangles and summing their areas.
subject: Mathematics

label: Past, Present and Progressive Tense
statement: Demonstrate the “Past, Present and Progressive Tense” objective: Use verbs to convey past and present tense correctly and consistently, including the progressive form (e.g., she is drumming, he was shouting), understanding how tense indicates time.
subject: English

label: Fair testing (age 8+)
