statement: Demonstrate the “Fair testing (age 8+)” objective: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.
subject: Science

label: Medieval Worlds Beyond Europe
statement: Demonstrate the “Medieval Worlds Beyond Europe” objective: The medieval world beyond Europe: the Islamic Golden Age (maths, medicine, architecture), the Mali Empire and Mansa Musa, Song Dynasty China; how the medieval world was connected through trade routes like the Silk Road.
subject: History

label: Equivalent fractions on a number line
statement: Demonstrate the “Equivalent fractions on a number line” objective: Understand two fractions as equivalent if they are the same size or the same point on a number line; recognise and show families of common equivalent fractions using diagrams.
subject: Mathematics

label: Bar Models for Ratios
statement: Demonstrate the “Bar Models for Ratios” objective: Represent ratio and proportion problems using bar models (rectangular strips divided into equal parts labelled with quantities) and tape diagrams (segmented strips showing part-to-part and part-to-whole relationships); use these visual models to set up and solve unequal sharing, scaling, and percentage problems — drawing the diagram first, then reading off the answer.
subject: Mathematics

label: Greenhouse Gas Science
statement: Demonstrate the “Greenhouse Gas Science” objective: Describe the electromagnetic spectrum and distinguish between short-wave solar radiation and long-wave infrared radiation emitted by Earth; explain how greenhouse gas molecules (CO2, CH4, N2O, H2O) absorb and re-emit infrared through molecular vibration while O2 and N2 do not; distinguish the natural greenhouse effect (which makes Earth habitable) from the enhanced greenhouse effect driven by human emissions; evaluate the relative potency of different greenhouse gases.
subject: Science

label: Phonics Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Phonics Vocabulary” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of phonics and word structure — phoneme, grapheme, GPC (grapheme-phoneme correspondence), blend, segment, digraph, CVC, vowel, consonant, syllable, root word, suffix, prefix, and homophone — and understand that these words describe the building blocks that phonics instruction is built on.
subject: English

label: Percentages (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Percentages (age 9+)” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of ratio and proportion — ratio, proportion, percentage, scale, equivalent, unequal, relative size, part-to-part, part-to-whole, and out of — and understand the difference between ratio (comparing parts to parts) and proportion (comparing a part to the whole).
subject: Mathematics

label: Venn Diagrams and Counting Outcomes
statement: Demonstrate the “Venn Diagrams and Counting Outcomes” objective: Construct and interpret Venn diagrams with two or three sets to organise and count outcomes; use systematic listing and the product rule for counting to enumerate all possible outcomes of combined events.
subject: Mathematics

label: Addition and subtraction within 1000
statement: Demonstrate the “Addition and subtraction within 1000” objective: Add and subtract within 1000 using concrete models, drawings, and strategies based on place value; understand composing and decomposing tens and hundreds.
subject: Mathematics

label: Mary Anning, Fossil Hunter
statement: Demonstrate the “Mary Anning, Fossil Hunter” objective: Know who Mary Anning was — a pioneering fossil hunter from Lyme Regis, England, who discovered ichthyosaur and plesiosaur skeletons in the early 1800s and contributed to our understanding of prehistoric life.
subject: Science

label: Time Units and Calendar Facts
statement: Demonstrate the “Time Units and Calendar Facts” objective: Know the number of seconds in a minute and the number of days in each month, year, and leap year.
subject: Mathematics

label: Coral Bleaching & Acidification
statement: Demonstrate the “Coral Bleaching & Acidification” objective: Explain the mutualistic symbiosis between coral polyps and photosynthetic zooxanthellae; describe how heat stress causes bleaching (corals expel zooxanthellae and turn white); explain ocean acidification chemistry: CO2 dissolves in seawater to form carbonic acid, lowering pH and dissolving calcium carbonate skeletons; connect reef loss to the collapse of habitat for ~25% of marine species; evaluate current reef restoration efforts.
subject: Science

label: Simple Food Chains
statement: Demonstrate the “Simple Food Chains” objective: Describe how animals obtain their food from plants and other animals, using the idea of a simple food chain, and identify different sources of food.
subject: Science

label: Finding a missing number in addition
statement: Demonstrate the “Finding a missing number in addition” objective: Understand subtraction as finding an unknown addend (e.g. 10 − 8 = ? is the same as 8 + ? = 10).
subject: Mathematics

label: Defining Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Defining Words” objective: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (e.g., 'a duck is a bird that swims'), making real-life connections between words and their use.
subject: English

label: Force & Motion Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Force & Motion Vocabulary” objective: Use technical vocabulary for force and motion — balanced forces, unbalanced forces, resultant force, acceleration, deceleration, speed, moment, lever, fulcrum, mechanical advantage — and apply these when explaining and predicting how forces affect the motion and position of objects.
subject: Science

label: Greek theatre
statement: Demonstrate the “Greek theatre” objective: Know that the ancient Greeks invented theatre, performing tragedies and comedies in large open-air amphitheatres with actors wearing masks — and that plays were performed as part of religious festivals honouring the god Dionysus, with audiences of thousands.
subject: History

label: Connecting maths to real life
statement: Demonstrate the “Connecting maths to real life” objective: Represent real-world problems with number sentences, bar models, or diagrams, and interpret the mathematical result back in context.
subject: Mathematics

label: Asking Questions
statement: Demonstrate the “Asking Questions” objective: Ask relevant questions to extend understanding; ask and answer questions to seek help, get information, or clarify something not understood.
subject: English

label: Single Letter Sounds
statement: Demonstrate the “Single Letter Sounds” objective: Know the primary sound for each consonant and the short and long sounds for the five major vowels; respond speedily to single-letter graphemes.
subject: English

label: Why Polar Seasons Are Extreme
statement: Demonstrate the “Why Polar Seasons Are Extreme” objective: Understand why the poles have extreme seasons — Earth's axis is tilted at about 23.5°, so as it orbits the Sun, each pole spends half the year tilted toward the Sun (continuous daylight, warmer summer) and half tilted away (continuous darkness, bitter winter); this tilt also drives the annual cycle of sea ice expanding in winter and retreating in summer, and triggers animal behaviours like migration and breeding.
subject: Science

label: Shape patterns (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Shape patterns (age 7+)” objective: Look for and use mathematical structure: apply place-value patterns to three-digit operations, use multiplication/division relationships, and exploit shape properties to classify.
subject: Mathematics

label: Equivalent fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Equivalent fractions” objective: Recognise and show, using diagrams, equivalent fractions with small denominators.
subject: Mathematics

label: Newton's Third Law
statement: Demonstrate the “Newton's Third Law” objective: State and apply Newton's Third Law: every force has an equal and opposite reaction force acting on a different object, distinguishing action-reaction pairs from balanced forces.
subject: Science

label: Gut Bacteria & Digestion
statement: Demonstrate the “Gut Bacteria & Digestion” objective: Explain the role of gut microbiome bacteria in digestion, including breaking down dietary fibre and contributing to a healthy gut environment.
subject: Science

label: Greek Gods with Roman Names
statement: Demonstrate the “Greek Gods with Roman Names” objective: Understand that the Romans adopted the Greek gods but gave them new names — Zeus became Jupiter, Hera became Juno, Ares became Mars, Athena became Minerva, Poseidon became Neptune, Aphrodite became Venus — and that this shows how deeply Rome was influenced by Greek culture.
subject: History

label: Animal Body Groups
statement: Demonstrate the “Animal Body Groups” objective: Describe and compare the external body structure of common animals across groups (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals).
subject: Science

label: Sorting 2-D and 3-D shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Sorting 2-D and 3-D shapes” objective: Compare and sort common 2-D and 3-D shapes and everyday objects by their properties.
subject: Mathematics

label: Rehearsing and Varying Sentences
statement: Demonstrate the “Rehearsing and Varying Sentences” objective: Compose and rehearse sentences orally before writing, progressively building varied and rich vocabulary and an increasing range of sentence structures including dialogue.
subject: English

label: Factors, multiples, and primes
statement: Demonstrate the “Factors, multiples, and primes” objective: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100; identify common factors and common multiples of two numbers; use these concepts to solve problems.
subject: Mathematics

label: Plant Cells vs Animal Cells
statement: Demonstrate the “Plant Cells vs Animal Cells” objective: Compare plant and animal cells, identifying shared features and structures unique to plant cells (cell wall, vacuole, chloroplasts).
subject: Science

label: The Water Cycle
statement: Demonstrate the “The Water Cycle” objective: Understand the water cycle: the Sun heats water in oceans and lakes causing it to evaporate into water vapour, the vapour rises and cools to form clouds (condensation), and water falls back to Earth as rain, snow, or hail (precipitation) — then the cycle repeats.
subject: Science

label: Seasons & Weather Patterns
statement: Demonstrate the “Seasons & Weather Patterns” objective: Know that weather changes with the seasons — spring brings rain and new growth, summer is warmest with long days, autumn brings cooling and falling leaves, winter is coldest with short days — and that this pattern repeats every year.
subject: Science

label: Advanced Multi-Step Problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Advanced Multi-Step Problems” objective: Make sense of complex multi-step problems involving ratio, proportion, algebra, negative numbers, and all four operations with fractions and decimals by analysing given and unknown quantities, planning solution strategies, and evaluating reasonableness using estimation and inverse operations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Coins & Notes
statement: Demonstrate the “Coins & Notes” objective: Recognising common coins and notes, knowing their values, and understanding that different combinations can make the same amount.
subject: Life Skills

label: Sun, Moon, and stars
statement: Demonstrate the “Sun, Moon, and stars” objective: Use observations of the sun, moon, and stars to describe predictable patterns such as the sun rising and setting, the moon changing shape, and stars appearing at night.
subject: Science

label: The Atmosphere
statement: Demonstrate the “The Atmosphere” objective: Know that Earth is surrounded by a layer of air called the atmosphere, that air has weight and exerts pressure, that the atmosphere protects us from harmful radiation and keeps the planet warm enough for life, and that weather happens in the lowest layer (troposphere).
subject: Science

label: Deformation & Fluid Pressure
statement: Demonstrate the “Deformation & Fluid Pressure” objective: Explain forces associated with deforming objects (elastic and inelastic deformation), thermal expansion and contraction of materials, and how fluid pressure acts in all directions and increases with depth.
subject: Science

label: Fossils Reveal Ancient Environments
statement: Demonstrate the “Fossils Reveal Ancient Environments” objective: Understand that fossils tell us not only about ancient animals but also about ancient environments — for example, marine fossils found on a mountaintop show that area was once underwater.
subject: Science

label: Expressive and Sensory Language
statement: Demonstrate the “Expressive and Sensory Language” objective: Recognise recurring literary language in stories and poetry, identify words and phrases that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses, and discuss favourite words and phrases.
subject: English

label: Decimal place value
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimal place value” objective: Round decimals with one decimal place to the nearest whole number.
subject: Mathematics

label: Using objects to model real problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Using objects to model real problems” objective: Use objects, drawings, or simple number sentences to represent a real-world situation (early mathematical modelling).
subject: Mathematics

label: Diphthongs and complex vowels
statement: Demonstrate the “Diphthongs and complex vowels” objective: Read and spell words containing diphthongs and complex vowel patterns (ow, ou, ew, ue, ie, aw, au) and words ending in -y as a vowel sound.
subject: English

label: Statistical Analysis Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Statistical Analysis Vocabulary” objective: Read, write, and use the vocabulary of statistical analysis — mean, median, mode, range, frequency, data, sample, average, chart, table, graph, pie chart, scatter graph, correlation — with understanding of what each term describes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Looking After Money
statement: Demonstrate the “Looking After Money” objective: Keeping money safe; not losing coins or notes; understanding that money has real value and should be treated carefully; basic money responsibility.
subject: Life Skills

label: Understanding fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding fractions” objective: Solve problems involving unequal sharing and grouping using knowledge of fractions and multiples.
subject: Mathematics

label: Equivalent fractions (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Equivalent fractions (age 8+)” objective: Generate simple equivalent fractions and explain why they are equivalent using visual fraction models.
subject: Mathematics

label: Animal Intelligence
statement: Demonstrate the “Animal Intelligence” objective: Explore animal intelligence and complex behaviour — chimpanzees and crows use tools, dolphins recognise themselves in mirrors, octopuses solve puzzles and escape enclosures, elephants mourn their dead, meerkats teach their young to handle scorpions — understanding that many animals think, learn, and have social lives more complex than once believed.
subject: Science

label: Grouping Species Using DNA
statement: Demonstrate the “Grouping Species Using DNA” objective: Explain cladistics: organisms are grouped by shared derived characters, not just similarity; how phylogenetic trees are built using molecular data (DNA sequence alignment) and the molecular clock; explain why birds are technically a group within dinosaurs (crown Avemetatarsalia); distinguish convergent evolution (unrelated species evolving similar traits) from parallel evolution; introduce horizontal gene transfer and why the tree of life is more accurately a web; explain why classification systems keep changing as new data emerge.
subject: Science

label: Climate Change at the Poles
statement: Demonstrate the “Climate Change at the Poles” objective: Understand how climate change is affecting polar regions — Arctic sea ice is shrinking dramatically (losing about 13% per decade since 1979), the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets are losing mass and contributing to sea level rise, permafrost is thawing and releasing methane (a powerful greenhouse gas), and these changes create positive feedback loops where melting leads to more warming which leads to more melting.
subject: Science

label: Reading and writing numbers to 20
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading and writing numbers to 20” objective: Read and write numerals from 0 to 20.
subject: Mathematics

label: Knowing all letters
statement: Demonstrate the “Knowing all letters” objective: Recognise and name all uppercase and lowercase letters of the alphabet; name the letters in order and use letter names to distinguish between alternative spellings.
subject: English

label: Proportion Graphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Proportion Graphs” objective: Represent proportional relationships using double number lines (two parallel number lines aligned at 0) and ratio tables; recognise that equivalent ratios generate straight lines through the origin when graphed.
subject: Mathematics

label: AI in Computer Games
statement: Demonstrate the “AI in Computer Games” objective: How computer game characters 'decide' what to do; simple rule-based AI vs learning AI; NPCs, difficulty adjustment; AI as the opponent in chess or board games.
subject: Computing

label: How Language Choices Affect the Reader
statement: Demonstrate the “How Language Choices Affect the Reader” objective: Evaluate how authors use language including figurative language, considering the impact of word choices, imagery, and literary devices on the reader.
subject: English

label: How Natural Selection Works
statement: Demonstrate the “How Natural Selection Works” objective: Explain natural selection as the mechanism of evolution: heritable variation + competition for resources + differential survival and reproduction = change in allele frequency over generations.
subject: Science

label: Dividing by two-digit numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Dividing by two-digit numbers” objective: Divide numbers up to 4 digits by a two-digit number using formal written short division where appropriate, interpreting remainders according to context.
subject: Mathematics

label: Ray Diagrams & Images
statement: Demonstrate the “Ray Diagrams & Images” objective: Construct ray diagrams to show the formation of images by plane mirrors and converging lenses, identifying whether images are real or virtual, magnified or diminished, upright or inverted.
subject: Science

label: Habitat Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Habitat Vocabulary” objective: Name and use vocabulary for where living things are found — habitat, environment, microhabitat, conditions, woodland, ocean, desert, rainforest, pond — and use terms to describe what animals need to survive: food, water, shelter, space, and suitable conditions.
subject: Science

label: Short Research Projects
statement: Demonstrate the “Short Research Projects” objective: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic, gather information from print and digital sources, and take brief organised notes.
subject: English

label: Taking Turns and Sharing
statement: Demonstrate the “Taking Turns and Sharing” objective: Take turns, share materials, and play cooperatively with others — understanding that group activities work better when everyone gets a fair go and that waiting for your turn is part of being a good friend.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Expanding Single Brackets
statement: Demonstrate the “Expanding Single Brackets” objective: Expand (multiply out) a single term over a bracket using the distributive property, e.g., 3(2x + 5) = 6x + 15; expand expressions involving negative multipliers.
subject: Mathematics

label: Number Pattern Relationships
statement: Demonstrate the “Number Pattern Relationships” objective: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules; identify relationships between corresponding terms; form ordered pairs and graph them on a coordinate plane.
subject: Mathematics

label: Suffixes
statement: Demonstrate the “Suffixes” objective: Apply suffix spelling rules that require changes to the root word: dropping final -e before vowel suffixes, changing -y to -i, doubling final consonants in short-vowel words; use suffixes -ment, -ness, -ful, -less, -ly.
subject: English

label: What Is a Rainforest?
statement: Demonstrate the “What Is a Rainforest?” objective: Know that a rainforest is a thick, tall forest found in hot, wet places near the Equator where it rains almost every day, creating a warm, damp environment where plants and animals thrive.
subject: Science

label: Generalising Patterns
statement: Demonstrate the “Generalising Patterns” objective: Recognise and use repeated reasoning to generalise: spot calculation patterns, describe rules for sequences, and predict results using known mathematical facts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Expressions & Equations Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Expressions & Equations Vocabulary” objective: Understand and use the concepts and vocabulary of expressions, equations, inequalities, terms, and factors; distinguish between an expression (no equals sign), an equation (equals sign), and an inequality (inequality sign).
subject: Mathematics

label: Heart & Blood Circulation
statement: Demonstrate the “Heart & Blood Circulation” objective: Describe the circulatory system in detail: the heart has four chambers (two atria, two ventricles) that pump blood in a double loop — one to the lungs for oxygen and one to the rest of the body to deliver it — through arteries, veins, and tiny capillaries.
subject: Science

label: Polar Oceans and World Climate
statement: Demonstrate the “Polar Oceans and World Climate” objective: Understand how polar oceans connect to the global climate system — cold, dense polar water sinks and drives thermohaline circulation (a global conveyor belt of ocean currents), sea ice reflects sunlight back to space (the albedo effect) helping regulate Earth's temperature, and the Southern Ocean around Antarctica is one of the most productive marine ecosystems on Earth due to upwelling nutrients.
subject: Science

label: Checking Answers by Rounding
statement: Demonstrate the “Checking Answers by Rounding” objective: Use rounding to check answers to calculations and determine appropriate levels of accuracy in context.
subject: Mathematics

label: Finding halves and quarters (age 5+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Finding halves and quarters (age 5+)” objective: Recognise, find, and name a quarter as one of four equal parts of an object, shape, or quantity.
subject: Mathematics

label: Skeletons & Muscles
statement: Demonstrate the “Skeletons & Muscles” objective: Identify that humans and some other animals have skeletons and muscles for support, protection, and movement.
subject: Science

label: Single-Celled Organisms
statement: Demonstrate the “Single-Celled Organisms” objective: Explain how unicellular organisms such as bacteria and Amoeba carry out all the functions of life within a single cell.
subject: Science

label: Reading and writing numbers to 10,000,000
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading and writing numbers to 10,000,000” objective: Read, write, order, and compare numbers up to 10,000,000 and determine the value of each digit.
subject: Mathematics

label: Active and passive voice
statement: Demonstrate the “Active and passive voice” objective: Use the passive voice to shift focus from the agent to the action or recipient, understanding how passive constructions affect the presentation of information in formal and objective writing.
subject: English

label: Forces Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Forces Vocabulary” objective: Name and describe forces using precise vocabulary — force, push, pull, twist, stretch, squash, contact force, non-contact force, gravity, weight, friction, air resistance, upthrust — and distinguish between forces that require physical contact and forces that act at a distance.
subject: Science

label: Polar Climate Zone
statement: Demonstrate the “Polar Climate Zone” objective: Understand that polar regions belong to the polar climate zone — one of Earth's five main climate zones (tropical, arid, temperate, continental, polar) — characterised by temperatures rarely above 10°C even in summer, low precipitation (polar deserts receive less rain than the Sahara), and strong winds; know that latitude is the key factor determining climate zones, with polar regions above 60°N/S.
subject: Science

label: Division as Unknown Factor
statement: Demonstrate the “Division as Unknown Factor” objective: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem (e.g. find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8).
subject: Mathematics

label: Tree diagrams
statement: Demonstrate the “Tree diagrams” objective: Generate theoretical sample spaces for single and combined events using listing, tables, and tree diagrams, and calculate theoretical probabilities as the number of favourable outcomes divided by the total number of equally likely outcomes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Advanced Material Properties
statement: Demonstrate the “Advanced Material Properties” objective: Compare and group everyday materials based on advanced properties: hardness, solubility, transparency, electrical and thermal conductivity, and response to magnets.
subject: Science

label: Brain Science of Emotions
statement: Demonstrate the “Brain Science of Emotions” objective: Understand how the amygdala triggers emotional responses and how the prefrontal cortex (still developing in adolescence) regulates them; explain why stress hormones (cortisol, adrenaline) affect thinking and memory; understand that the adolescent brain's dopamine system makes feelings more intense; distinguish between emotion regulation (managing feelings effectively) and emotion suppression (pushing feelings down, which is counterproductive); introduce cognitive reappraisal as a research-backed technique for changing how we interpret a situation.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Water Transport in Plants
statement: Demonstrate the “Water Transport in Plants” objective: Investigate how water is transported within plants, using observations such as coloured water being drawn up through a stem.
subject: Science

label: Feelings Change and Differ
statement: Demonstrate the “Feelings Change and Differ” objective: Understand that everyone has feelings, that feelings change throughout the day, and that the same event can make different people feel different things.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: How fossils form
statement: Demonstrate the “How fossils form” objective: Identify evidence from patterns in rock formations and fossils in rock layers to support an explanation for changes in a landscape over time.
subject: Science

label: Fluent adding and subtracting within 5
statement: Demonstrate the “Fluent adding and subtracting within 5” objective: Fluently add and subtract within 5.
subject: Mathematics

label: Halves and quarters (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Halves and quarters (age 8+)” objective: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths to the nearest half and quarter inch; display the data on a line plot with a scale marked in whole numbers, halves, and quarters.
subject: Mathematics

label: Adding within 100
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding within 100” objective: Add within 100 using strategies based on place value, including adding a two-digit and one-digit number, and a two-digit and a multiple of 10.
subject: Mathematics

label: Comparing Characters Across Stories
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing Characters Across Stories” objective: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories; identify similarities and differences between two texts on the same topic.
subject: English

label: Reflecting Light
statement: Demonstrate the “Reflecting Light” objective: Notice that light is reflected from surfaces, and that shiny smooth surfaces reflect light best.
subject: Science

label: Weather vs climate
statement: Demonstrate the “Weather vs climate” objective: Obtain and combine information to describe climates in different regions of the world, distinguishing between weather and climate.
subject: Science

label: Evaluating Arguments in Non-Fiction
statement: Demonstrate the “Evaluating Arguments in Non-Fiction” objective: Evaluate arguments and claims in non-fiction texts — assess whether reasoning is sound, evidence is relevant and sufficient, distinguish between fact and opinion, and recognise bias, propaganda, and rhetorical techniques.
subject: English

label: Mixed & Improper Fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Mixed & Improper Fractions” objective: Use the four operations with formal written methods applied to integers, decimals, proper and improper fractions, and mixed numbers, all both positive and negative.
subject: Mathematics

label: Seasonal changes
statement: Demonstrate the “Seasonal changes” objective: Observe changes across the four seasons and describe weather associated with each season, including how day length varies.
subject: Science

label: Animal Record-Holders
statement: Demonstrate the “Animal Record-Holders” objective: Know some of the world's animal record-holders — the blue whale is the largest animal ever, the cheetah is the fastest land animal, the bee hummingbird is the smallest bird, the giraffe is the tallest — and compare their sizes to familiar objects.
subject: Science

label: Complex Multi-Step Problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Complex Multi-Step Problems” objective: Make sense of complex multi-step problems involving large numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages by analysing what is known and unknown, planning multi-step strategies, and evaluating reasonableness through estimation and inverse operations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Taking Apart & Rebuilding
statement: Demonstrate the “Taking Apart & Rebuilding” objective: Observe that an object made of a small set of pieces can be disassembled and made into a new object, understanding that the pieces still exist.
subject: Science

label: Forms of Poetry and Performance
statement: Demonstrate the “Forms of Poetry and Performance” objective: Recognise different forms of poetry (free verse, narrative poetry, haiku) and discuss their features; prepare poems and play scripts to read aloud and perform with understanding through intonation, tone, volume and action.
subject: English

label: Arrays for multiplication
statement: Demonstrate the “Arrays for multiplication” objective: Use arrays to represent multiplication and division situations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Life Changed Over Time
statement: Demonstrate the “Life Changed Over Time” objective: Recognise that living things have changed over time and that fossils provide information about organisms that inhabited the Earth millions of years ago.
subject: Science

label: What Multiplication Means
statement: Demonstrate the “What Multiplication Means” objective: Interpret products of whole numbers (e.g. 5 × 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7).
subject: Mathematics

label: Systematic Listing
statement: Demonstrate the “Systematic Listing” objective: Enumerate possibilities of combinations of two variables systematically (e.g. all ways to choose from a set of options).
subject: Mathematics

label: Social insects: ants and bees
statement: Demonstrate the “Social insects: ants and bees” objective: Social insects: how ants and bees live and work together in colonies. Queens, workers, and drones. Division of labour — some gather food, some build, some guard. Ant tunnels and bee hives as organised homes. Parallels to human teamwork.
subject: Science

label: Monitoring Comprehension
statement: Demonstrate the “Monitoring Comprehension” objective: Notice the difference between decoding words and actually understanding them — recognise when you've read the words but not grasped the meaning, and do something about it.
subject: English

label: How Tectonic Plates Move
statement: Demonstrate the “How Tectonic Plates Move” objective: Understand that convection currents in the molten mantle drive the movement of rigid tectonic plates; distinguish between convergent (collision/subduction), divergent (spreading ridges), and transform (sliding) plate boundaries; explain why volcanoes, earthquakes, and mountain chains cluster at boundaries; introduce the Wilson cycle of supercontinent assembly and breakup.
subject: Science

label: Area with Fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Area with Fractions” objective: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling with unit-fraction squares; show that the area equals the product of the side lengths.
subject: Mathematics

label: Square and cube numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Square and cube numbers” objective: Recognise and use square numbers and cube numbers, and the notation for squared (²) and cubed (³).
subject: Mathematics

label: Understanding angles (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding angles (age 8+)” objective: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas.
subject: Mathematics

label: Different Types of Texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Different Types of Texts” objective: Recognise common types of texts (storybooks, poems, non-fiction); name the author and illustrator and define the role of each in telling or presenting a text.
subject: English

label: Quadratic Graphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Quadratic Graphs” objective: Recognise that quadratic functions produce curved (parabolic) graphs, distinguish them from linear graphs, and use plotted quadratic graphs to estimate values and find approximate solutions.
subject: Mathematics

label: Angles with parallel lines
statement: Demonstrate the “Angles with parallel lines” objective: Understand and use the relationship between parallel lines cut by a transversal: corresponding angles, alternate interior angles, and co-interior (same-side interior) angles; use these to find unknown angles.
subject: Mathematics

label: Community Rights and Responsibilities
statement: Demonstrate the “Community Rights and Responsibilities” objective: Understand their rights and responsibilities as a member of a community — that everyone has a right to be treated with respect and to feel safe, and that with rights come responsibilities to treat others the same way.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Vocabulary: ethics and citizenship
statement: Demonstrate the “Vocabulary: ethics and citizenship” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of ethics and citizenship — bullying, cyberbullying, bystander, upstander, peer pressure, digital citizenship, rights, responsibility, and ethical — and understand the distinctions between these closely related terms.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Morals in Fables, Folktales and Myths
statement: Demonstrate the “Morals in Fables, Folktales and Myths” objective: Explain how the central message, lesson, or moral of a story is conveyed through key details across diverse text types including fables, folktales, and myths.
subject: English

label: Types of angles
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of angles” objective: Identify acute and obtuse angles; compare and order angles up to two right angles by size.
subject: Mathematics

label: Ratio Problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Ratio Problems” objective: Solve problems involving the relative sizes of two quantities where missing values can be found by using integer multiplication and division facts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Greek gods & Mount Olympus
statement: Demonstrate the “Greek gods & Mount Olympus” objective: Know that the ancient Greeks believed in many gods and goddesses who lived on Mount Olympus — including Zeus (king of the gods, thunder), Athena (wisdom), Poseidon (the sea), Hermes (messages), and Aphrodite (love) — and that each god had special powers and a role in the world.
subject: History

label: Choosing Formal Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Choosing Formal Vocabulary” objective: Distinguish between formal and informal vocabulary, selecting words appropriate for formal speech and writing such as 'discover' instead of 'find out' and 'request' instead of 'ask for'.
subject: English

label: Ohm's Law: voltage, current, resistance
statement: Demonstrate the “Ohm's Law: voltage, current, resistance” objective: Apply Ohm's Law (V = IR) to calculate current, voltage, or resistance in a simple circuit, and explain that resistance opposes the flow of current.
subject: Science

label: Inheritance Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Inheritance Vocabulary” objective: Use vocabulary for variation and inheritance — inherited characteristic, acquired characteristic, variation, offspring, trait, species, breed, genetic, environment — and apply these when comparing organisms and explaining similarities and differences within and between species.
subject: Science

label: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
statement: Demonstrate the “Fall of the Western Roman Empire” objective: Describe how the Western Roman Empire gradually declined due to a combination of factors — military pressure from invading peoples, political instability, economic problems, and an overstretched empire — and finally fell in AD 476, while the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire continued for nearly a thousand more years.
subject: History

label: Vocabulary: self
statement: Demonstrate the “Vocabulary: self” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of self-reflection — self-awareness, reflect, pattern, trigger, assumption, impact, perspective, and notice — and understand that having precise words for these inner experiences makes them easier to understand and talk about.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Reading and Comparing Bar Graphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading and Comparing Bar Graphs” objective: Solve comparison, sum, and difference problems using information presented in a bar graph.
subject: Mathematics

label: Forming Capital Letters
statement: Demonstrate the “Forming Capital Letters” objective: Form capital letters correctly; print many upper- and lowercase letters legibly.
subject: English

label: Patterns in Your Own Reactions
statement: Demonstrate the “Patterns in Your Own Reactions” objective: Notice patterns in your own reactions — 'I tend to respond like this when I'm tired, left out, or put on the spot'.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Symbiosis
statement: Demonstrate the “Symbiosis” objective: Understand symbiosis — close relationships between different species — including mutualism (both benefit, like clownfish and anemones), commensalism (one benefits without harming the other, like remora fish riding sharks), and parasitism (one benefits at the other's expense, like ticks on deer) — and recognise these relationships in nature.
subject: Science

label: Space Exploration Milestones
statement: Demonstrate the “Space Exploration Milestones” objective: Describe key milestones in human space exploration: the Space Race (Sputnik, Yuri Gagarin, Apollo 11 Moon landing), the Space Shuttle era, the International Space Station, and current missions (Artemis programme, Mars exploration plans, commercial spaceflight).
subject: Science

label: How switches work
statement: Demonstrate the “How switches work” objective: Recognise that a switch opens and closes a circuit, controlling whether a lamp lights or a buzzer sounds.
subject: Science

label: Reflecting on Your Language Use
statement: Demonstrate the “Reflecting on Your Language Use” objective: Reflect on yourself as a language user — how your reading, writing, and speaking shift across audiences, purposes, and contexts, and where you want to develop further.
subject: English

label: Makes someone a good friend
statement: Demonstrate the “Makes someone a good friend” objective: Understand what makes someone a good friend — being kind, honest, reliable, and including others — and recognise behaviours that are not friendly, such as being bossy, leaving people out, or saying mean things.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Temperate Rainforests
statement: Demonstrate the “Temperate Rainforests” objective: Know that not all rainforests are tropical — temperate rainforests exist in cooler, wet regions like the Pacific Northwest of North America, western Scotland and Wales, southern Chile, and New Zealand — with similar features (high rainfall, moss-draped trees, dense canopy) but different species, including ancient oaks, giant redwoods, and tree ferns.
subject: Science

label: Describing Rules & Patterns
statement: Demonstrate the “Describing Rules & Patterns” objective: When you notice a pattern repeating, describe it as a rule that works every time — then test whether the rule holds in new cases.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Linear number sequences
statement: Demonstrate the “Linear number sequences” objective: Generate and describe linear number sequences, including those with negative and decimal steps; identify the term-to-term rule.
subject: Mathematics

label: Square and cube numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Square and cube numbers” objective: Use integer powers and associated real roots (square, cube, and higher); recognise powers of 2, 3, 4, and 5; distinguish between exact representations of roots and their decimal approximations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Literary and Language Terminology
statement: Demonstrate the “Literary and Language Terminology” objective: Discuss reading, writing, and spoken language with precise and confident use of linguistic and literary terminology — including terms for word classes, sentence types, clause types, literary devices, and text-level features.
subject: English

label: Apostrophes for possession (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Apostrophes for possession (age 7+)” objective: Use the possessive apostrophe accurately with both regular and irregular plural nouns (e.g., the girls' bags, the children's toys), distinguishing singular from plural possession.
subject: English

label: 2-D shapes (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “2-D shapes (age 10+)” objective: Draw 2-D shapes using given dimensions and angles, using a ruler and protractor accurately.
subject: Mathematics

label: Prejudice and Discrimination
statement: Demonstrate the “Prejudice and Discrimination” objective: Understand the impact of prejudice and discrimination on individuals and communities — that treating people unfairly because of their identity causes real harm — and recognise their own responsibility to stand against it.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Fluent adding and subtracting within 1000
statement: Demonstrate the “Fluent adding and subtracting within 1000” objective: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
subject: Mathematics

label: Times tables
statement: Demonstrate the “Times tables” objective: Recall and use multiplication and division facts for the 2, 5, and 10 multiplication tables.
subject: Mathematics

label: Modelling with Sketches
statement: Demonstrate the “Modelling with Sketches” objective: Develop a simple sketch, drawing, or physical model to illustrate how the shape of an object helps it function as needed to solve a given problem.
subject: Science

label: Order of operations (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Order of operations (age 10+)” objective: Look for and use mathematical structure: exploit the hierarchy of 2-D shapes to deduce properties; use order of operations and algebraic structure to simplify expressions; connect fraction–decimal–percentage equivalences; use ratio structure to solve proportion problems efficiently.
subject: Mathematics

label: Fractions of a whole (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions of a whole (age 9+)” objective: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number using visual models and equations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Rainforests & Global Climate
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforests & Global Climate” objective: Understand the connection between rainforests and global climate — rainforests absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen through photosynthesis, store enormous amounts of carbon in their biomass, and generate rainfall through transpiration; when forests are burned or cleared, stored carbon is released as CO₂, accelerating climate change and disrupting regional rainfall patterns.
subject: Science

label: Geography & Local Weather
statement: Demonstrate the “Geography & Local Weather” objective: Know that different places around the world have very different typical weather — tropical places are hot and wet all year, deserts are very dry, polar regions are freezing cold — and that geography (distance from the equator, altitude, nearness to the sea) affects local weather.
subject: Science

label: Paragraph Cohesion
statement: Demonstrate the “Paragraph Cohesion” objective: Link ideas across paragraphs using a wider range of cohesive devices including word repetition, grammatical connections such as adverbials, and ellipsis to create coherent extended texts.
subject: English

label: Subtracting multiples of 10
statement: Demonstrate the “Subtracting multiples of 10” objective: Subtract multiples of 10 (10–90) from multiples of 10 using place value strategies.
subject: Mathematics

label: Similes & Metaphors
statement: Demonstrate the “Similes & Metaphors” objective: Understand and identify similes (comparisons using like or as) and metaphors (direct comparisons stating something is something else) in texts, explaining how each creates imagery and conveys meaning.
subject: English

label: Fractions, Decimals & Percentages
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions, Decimals & Percentages” objective: Look for and use mathematical structure: exploit the relationship between fractions, decimals, and percentages; use factor pairs to simplify multiplication; apply angle facts to find unknowns; use properties of regular polygons systematically.
subject: Mathematics

label: Patterns with Powers of Ten
statement: Demonstrate the “Patterns with Powers of Ten” objective: Explain patterns in zeros when multiplying by powers of 10 and in decimal-point placement when multiplying/dividing by a power of 10; use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10 (e.g. 10³ = 1000).
subject: Mathematics

label: Odd or Even
statement: Demonstrate the “Odd or Even” objective: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members.
subject: Mathematics

label: Comparing fractions (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing fractions (age 8+)” objective: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about size; record comparisons with >, =, or < symbols.
subject: Mathematics

label: Telling Time: Minutes
statement: Demonstrate the “Telling Time: Minutes” objective: Tell and write the time to five minutes, including quarter past and quarter to, and draw clock hands to show these times.
subject: Mathematics

label: Time and Attention Management
statement: Demonstrate the “Time and Attention Management” objective: Manage their own time and attention effectively — prioritising tasks, minimising distractions, and maintaining focus on important work even when it's not the most exciting option.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: AI Data Collection and Privacy
statement: Demonstrate the “AI Data Collection and Privacy” objective: What data AI systems collect about you; who has it and why it matters; cookies, tracking, smart speakers always listening; your data is valuable.
subject: Computing

label: Basic Informational Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Basic Informational Writing” objective: Compose informative or explanatory texts that introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement or section.
subject: English

label: Fair Trade & Ethics
statement: Demonstrate the “Fair Trade & Ethics” objective: Where products come from and who makes them; that people around the world produce what we buy; fair pay for workers; making ethical choices as consumers.
subject: Life Skills

label: Plot Structure and Character Development
statement: Demonstrate the “Plot Structure and Character Development” objective: Analyse how plot structure unfolds through episodes or key events, and how characters develop, respond to challenges, and change over the course of a narrative — including the relationship between character, setting, and plot.
subject: English

label: Lines of symmetry
statement: Demonstrate the “Lines of symmetry” objective: Complete a simple symmetric figure with respect to a specific line of symmetry.
subject: Mathematics

label: Prefixes and suffixes
statement: Demonstrate the “Prefixes and suffixes” objective: Read words containing common prefixes and suffixes from the Y3-4 programme, applying knowledge of root words, prefixes and suffixes (morphology and etymology) to read aloud and understand new words.
subject: English

label: Nth-Term Rules
statement: Demonstrate the “Nth-Term Rules” objective: Find the nth-term expression for an arithmetic sequence by identifying the common difference and the zero-term, and use it to determine any term in the sequence or test whether a given number belongs to the sequence.
subject: Mathematics

label: 2-D shapes (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “2-D shapes (age 8+)” objective: Identify lines of symmetry in 2-D shapes presented in different orientations; recognise line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.
subject: Mathematics

label: Insect life cycles: complete metamorphosis
statement: Demonstrate the “Insect life cycles: complete metamorphosis” objective: Insect life cycles — complete metamorphosis in detail. Egg → larva → pupa → adult. The larva (caterpillar, grub, maggot) looks completely different from the adult. Inside the pupa the body is rebuilt. Butterflies, beetles, flies, and ladybirds all undergo complete metamorphosis.
subject: Science

label: Drawing Particle Diagrams
statement: Demonstrate the “Drawing Particle Diagrams” objective: Draw and interpret particle diagrams — dot representations showing the arrangement, spacing, and movement of particles in solids (close, regular, vibrating in place), liquids (close, random, flowing past each other), and gases (widely spaced, moving rapidly in all directions) — and use these diagrams to explain observable properties such as fixed shape, fixed volume, and compressibility.
subject: Science

label: Comparing Possible Solutions
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing Possible Solutions” objective: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints.
subject: Science

label: Coordinates (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Coordinates (age 11+)” objective: Plot and read coordinates in all four quadrants of the Cartesian plane, using positive and negative x- and y-values to describe positions precisely.
subject: Mathematics

label: Observation vs Interpretation
statement: Demonstrate the “Observation vs Interpretation” objective: Notice the difference between what you observed and what you think it means — 'the ice melted' is an observation; 'the ice melted because of the heat' is an interpretation.
subject: Science

label: Revising and editing (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Revising and editing (age 8+)” objective: Read back your own writing critically and independently — notice where meaning is unclear, where a word could be stronger, or where the reader might be confused; make revisions without needing teacher prompts, using your own judgment about what is and isn't working.
subject: English

label: Understanding fractions (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding fractions (age 7+)” objective: Communicate with mathematical precision: use correct place-value and fraction vocabulary, specify units in measurement answers, and use notation accurately.
subject: Mathematics

label: Decomposing a shape into more equal shares
statement: Demonstrate the “Decomposing a shape into more equal shares” objective: Understand that decomposing a shape into more equal shares creates smaller shares.
subject: Mathematics

label: Grammar Terms: Voice and Punctuation
statement: Demonstrate the “Grammar Terms: Voice and Punctuation” objective: Know and use Year 6 grammatical terminology accurately: subject, object, active voice, passive voice, synonym, antonym, ellipsis, hyphen, colon, semi-colon, bullet points.
subject: English

label: Local weather patterns
statement: Demonstrate the “Local weather patterns” objective: Use and share observations of local weather conditions to describe patterns over time, recording temperature, rainfall, and other conditions.
subject: Science

label: Cleopatra and the End of Egypt
statement: Demonstrate the “Cleopatra and the End of Egypt” objective: Know that ancient Egypt eventually came to an end: the last pharaoh was Cleopatra VII, who allied with Rome but was defeated by Octavian (later Augustus) in 31 BCE, after which Egypt became a province of the Roman Empire — ending over 3,000 years of pharaonic rule and beginning a new chapter in Egypt's history.
subject: History

label: Polar Exploration Then & Now
statement: Demonstrate the “Polar Exploration Then & Now” objective: Compare historical polar exploration with modern polar science — the Heroic Age (1897–1922) relied on ships, dogs, and human endurance with many fatalities, while today's polar scientists use GPS, satellites, icebreaker ships, heated research stations, and aircraft; understand that modern challenges include studying climate change data, and that polar science now includes diverse international teams including women scientists like glaciologist Liz Thomas and marine biologist Sylvia Earle.
subject: Science

label: Types of Teeth
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of Teeth” objective: Identify the four types of human teeth (incisors for cutting, canines for tearing, premolars and molars for grinding) and understand that tooth shape is linked to function, just as in other animals — herbivores have flat teeth, carnivores have sharp teeth.
subject: Science

label: Vocabulary: resilience and self
statement: Demonstrate the “Vocabulary: resilience and self” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of resilience and self-management — including regulate, resilience, growth mindset, fixed mindset, self-talk, trigger, setback, persevere, and distress — and understand what each word means in practice.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Numbers on a number line
statement: Demonstrate the “Numbers on a number line” objective: Understand inequalities as statements comparing expressions, represent solutions on a number line, and solve simple linear inequalities using the same inverse-operation methods as equations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Animal Groups & Survival
statement: Demonstrate the “Animal Groups & Survival” objective: Construct an argument that some animals form groups that help members survive, such as herds, packs, or colonies.
subject: Science

label: Coordinates (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Coordinates (age 8+)” objective: Plot specified points on a coordinate grid and draw sides to complete a given polygon.
subject: Mathematics

label: Adding and subtracting tens mentally
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding and subtracting tens mentally” objective: Add and subtract a two-digit number and tens mentally and using concrete/pictorial representations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Revising and editing
statement: Demonstrate the “Revising and editing” objective: Proof-read own writing to check for errors in spelling, grammar, and punctuation; evaluate and revise writing with teacher/peer support, re-reading to ensure meaning is clear and tense is consistent.
subject: English

label: How Diffusion Works
statement: Demonstrate the “How Diffusion Works” objective: Explain diffusion as the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration, and describe its role in moving materials (oxygen, carbon dioxide, glucose) in and between cells.
subject: Science

label: Understanding Bullying
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding Bullying” objective: Understand what bullying is — repeated behaviour intended to hurt someone, including physical, verbal, social (exclusion, spreading rumours), and cyberbullying — and know that it is always wrong and what to do if they experience or witness it.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Writing Algebraic Equations
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing Algebraic Equations” objective: Express missing number problems algebraically using letters for unknowns; translate word problems into equations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Fractions as parts of shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions as parts of shapes” objective: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas and express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
subject: Mathematics

label: Phrases & Clauses
statement: Demonstrate the “Phrases & Clauses” objective: Understand and analyse the function of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial, prepositional) and clauses (main, subordinate, relative) in general and in specific sentences, including recognising and correcting misplaced and dangling modifiers.
subject: English

label: Decimal place value (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimal place value (age 8+)” objective: Compare numbers with the same number of decimal places up to two decimal places.
subject: Mathematics

label: Percentages (age 12+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Percentages (age 12+)” objective: Solve problems involving percentage increase, percentage decrease, finding the original value after a percentage change, and calculating simple interest.
subject: Mathematics

label: Comparing fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing fractions” objective: Compare and order unit fractions, and fractions with the same denominator.
subject: Mathematics

label: Likelihood Language
statement: Demonstrate the “Likelihood Language” objective: Use probability language to describe and compare the likelihood of everyday events using words such as certain, likely, even chance, unlikely, impossible.
subject: Mathematics

label: Hieroglyphs and Papyrus
statement: Demonstrate the “Hieroglyphs and Papyrus” objective: Know that the ancient Egyptians used a special writing system called hieroglyphs — pictures and symbols that stood for sounds and words — and that they wrote on a paper-like material called papyrus, which was made from a plant that grew along the Nile.
subject: History

label: Dividing fractions (unit fractions)
statement: Demonstrate the “Dividing fractions (unit fractions)” objective: Interpret and compute division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number (e.g. 1/3 ÷ 4 = 1/12); use visual models and the relationship between multiplication and division to explain the result.
subject: Mathematics

label: Sunlight warms things up
statement: Demonstrate the “Sunlight warms things up” objective: Make observations to determine the effect of sunlight on Earth's surface, noticing that sunlight warms the ground, water, and objects.
subject: Science

label: Understanding fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding fractions” objective: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8); use operations on fractions to solve problems involving data in line plots (e.g. redistribute total equally).
subject: Mathematics

label: Cloud Types
statement: Demonstrate the “Cloud Types” objective: Identify the three main cloud types — cumulus (fluffy, fair weather), stratus (flat layers, overcast or drizzle), and cirrus (thin wisps, high up) — and understand that clouds form when water vapour in the air cools and condenses into tiny droplets.
subject: Science

label: Decimal place value (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimal place value (age 9+)” objective: Round decimals with two decimal places to the nearest whole number and to one decimal place.
subject: Mathematics

label: Analysing Text Structure
statement: Demonstrate the “Analysing Text Structure” objective: Analyse how a text's structure — including its overall organisation, use of chapters, stanzas, scenes, paragraphs, or sections — contributes to its meaning, style, and development of ideas.
subject: English

label: Weather-Resistant Engineering
statement: Demonstrate the “Weather-Resistant Engineering” objective: Understand that engineers design buildings, flood defences, and warning systems to protect communities from extreme weather — hurricane-resistant roofs, flood barriers, tornado shelters, and early-warning alert systems — and evaluate the merits of these solutions.
subject: Science

label: Medieval Legacy in Modern Life
statement: Demonstrate the “Medieval Legacy in Modern Life” objective: What the Middle Ages gave us: Parliament, universities, common law, Gothic architecture, the English language (Anglo-Saxon + Norman French), place names, surnames; why we are still fascinated by the medieval world.
subject: History

label: Numbers on a number line
statement: Demonstrate the “Numbers on a number line” objective: Solve word problems involving elapsed time by adding and subtracting time intervals in minutes, including using a number line.
subject: Mathematics

label: Estimation to check answers to calculations
statement: Demonstrate the “Estimation to check answers to calculations” objective: Use estimation to check answers to calculations and determine, in the context of a problem, an appropriate degree of accuracy.
subject: Mathematics

label: Understanding People in Their Own Time
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding People in Their Own Time” objective: Understand that people in the past saw the world very differently from us — judge their actions by the context they lived in, not only by today's values.
subject: History

label: Real-World to Maths Connections
statement: Demonstrate the “Real-World to Maths Connections” objective: Move between a real-world situation and a mathematical representation using concrete objects, drawings, diagrams, tables, number sentences, or bar models.
subject: Mathematics

label: What Division Means
statement: Demonstrate the “What Division Means” objective: Interpret whole-number quotients (e.g. 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share or the number of equal groups).
subject: Mathematics

label: Spelling Contracted Forms
statement: Demonstrate the “Spelling Contracted Forms” objective: Spell contracted forms correctly by placing the apostrophe where letters are omitted (can't, didn't, I'll, it's, etc.).
subject: English

label: Identifying Reasons Behind a Speaker's Points
statement: Demonstrate the “Identifying Reasons Behind a Speaker's Points” objective: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points, evaluating whether the reasoning is logical and the evidence is relevant.
subject: English

label: Idioms & Proverbs
statement: Demonstrate the “Idioms & Proverbs” objective: Recognise and interpret common idioms (break the ice, hit the nail on the head), adages (actions speak louder than words), and proverbs (a stitch in time saves nine), understanding their figurative meanings and when to use them.
subject: English

label: Mass Extinctions in Earth History
statement: Demonstrate the “Mass Extinctions in Earth History” objective: Compare the five major mass extinction events in Earth history (End-Ordovician, Late Devonian, End-Permian, End-Triassic, K-Pg), describe proposed kill mechanisms for each (glaciation, oceanic anoxia, volcanic mega-eruptions, asteroid impact), and explain why mass extinctions, while catastrophic, also open ecological space for subsequent evolutionary radiations.
subject: Science

label: Working with money
statement: Demonstrate the “Working with money” objective: Model real-world problems involving measurement, money, and time by choosing appropriate representations and interpreting results in context.
subject: Mathematics

label: Discovering Tutankhamun's Tomb
statement: Demonstrate the “Discovering Tutankhamun's Tomb” objective: Understand that we know about ancient Egypt because archaeologists have dug up and studied objects buried in the sand for thousands of years — and that one of the most exciting discoveries ever was when Howard Carter found the hidden tomb of Tutankhamun in 1922, filled with golden treasures.
subject: History

label: The Race to the South Pole
statement: Demonstrate the “The Race to the South Pole” objective: Know the story of the race to the South Pole in detail — Norwegian Roald Amundsen and British Robert Falcon Scott both set out in 1911, Amundsen arrived first on 14 December using dog sleds and careful planning, Scott arrived 34 days later using man-hauled sledges and tragically died with his team on the return journey; also know about Ernest Shackleton's 1914 Endurance expedition where the ship was trapped and crushed by ice, and Shackleton's extraordinary boat journey to South Georgia to rescue his crew.
subject: Science

label: Multiplying by Tens
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiplying by Tens” objective: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10–90 using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Life Cycle of Stars
statement: Demonstrate the “Life Cycle of Stars” objective: Understand the basics of a star’s life cycle: stars are born in clouds of gas and dust (nebulae), shine for millions or billions of years by fusing hydrogen, and eventually die — massive stars explode as supernovae while smaller stars fade into white dwarfs.
subject: Science

label: Antarctic Treaty & Research
statement: Demonstrate the “Antarctic Treaty & Research” objective: Know that Antarctica is governed by the Antarctic Treaty (signed 1959, in force since 1961) — which sets Antarctica aside for peaceful purposes and scientific research, bans military activity and mining, and is signed by over 50 countries; understand that international research stations study climate, astronomy, biology, and geology, and that Antarctica is the closest thing on Earth to a continent for science rather than politics.
subject: Science

label: Measuring length (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring length (age 10+)” objective: Recognise volume as an attribute of solid figures; understand that a unit cube (side length 1 unit) has 'one cubic unit' of volume and can be used to measure volume; a solid packed with n unit cubes has volume n cubic units.
subject: Mathematics

label: Explaining Relationships in Texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Explaining Relationships in Texts” objective: Explain the relationships or interactions between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts in historical, scientific, or technical texts based on specific information.
subject: English

label: Choosing representations strategically
statement: Demonstrate the “Choosing representations strategically” objective: Select and use tools and representations strategically: choose between mental methods, formal written methods, protractors, fraction strips, and diagrams based on the demands of the problem.
subject: Mathematics

label: Simple Calming Strategies
statement: Demonstrate the “Simple Calming Strategies” objective: Use simple calming strategies when feeling upset or overwhelmed — such as taking deep breaths, counting to ten, or going to a quiet space — and understand that these help the body and mind settle down.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Resolving Disagreements with Friends
statement: Demonstrate the “Resolving Disagreements with Friends” objective: Resolve simple disagreements with peers by talking it through — explaining how they feel, listening to the other person's side, and finding a compromise or solution that both can accept.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Justifying Views About Texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Justifying Views About Texts” objective: Provide reasoned justifications for views about texts, supporting interpretations and opinions with evidence and logical arguments.
subject: English

label: Classifying Organisms
statement: Demonstrate the “Classifying Organisms” objective: Describe how living things are classified into broad groups (micro-organisms, plants, animals) according to common observable characteristics, similarities, and differences.
subject: Science

label: How Fossils Form
statement: Demonstrate the “How Fossils Form” objective: Explain in simple terms how fossils form: an organism dies and is quickly buried in sediment; over millions of years minerals replace the remains and the sediment turns to rock, preserving the shape.
subject: Science

label: Global Wind Patterns
statement: Demonstrate the “Global Wind Patterns” objective: Explain that unequal solar heating drives large-scale atmospheric circulation: Hadley cells (0-30°), Ferrel cells (30-60°), and polar cells (60-90°) produce the trade winds, westerlies, and polar easterlies; describe how the Coriolis effect from Earth's rotation deflects winds rightward in the Northern Hemisphere; explain the jet stream as a fast high-altitude wind that steers weather systems; connect jet stream waviness and Arctic amplification to prolonged extreme weather.
subject: Science

label: Generalising with repeated reasoning
statement: Demonstrate the “Generalising with repeated reasoning” objective: Recognise and use repeated reasoning to generalise: describe algebraic rules for nth terms, use properties of operations to simplify, and verify generalisations with specific cases.
subject: Mathematics

label: 10 or 100 More or Less
statement: Demonstrate the “10 or 100 More or Less” objective: Find 10 or 100 more or less than a given number up to 1000.
subject: Mathematics

label: Senses, Brain & Responses
statement: Demonstrate the “Senses, Brain & Responses” objective: Use a model to describe that animals receive information through their senses, process it in their brain, and respond in different ways.
subject: Science

label: Skip Counting (4s, 8s, 50s, 100s)
statement: Demonstrate the “Skip Counting (4s, 8s, 50s, 100s)” objective: Count from 0 in multiples of 4, 8, 50, and 100.
subject: Mathematics

label: Angle sums in triangles and polygons
statement: Demonstrate the “Angle sums in triangles and polygons” objective: Derive and use the angle sum in a triangle (180°), use it to deduce the angle sum in any polygon ((n−2) × 180°), and calculate interior and exterior angles of regular polygons.
subject: Mathematics

label: Commas Before Joining Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Commas Before Joining Words” objective: Use a comma before a coordinating conjunction (and, but, or, so, yet) when joining two independent clauses in a compound sentence.
subject: English

label: Firsthand and Secondhand Accounts
statement: Demonstrate the “Firsthand and Secondhand Accounts” objective: Compare and contrast a firsthand account (autobiography, diary, letter) with a secondhand account (biography, textbook, news report) of the same event or topic, identifying differences in focus and information provided.
subject: English

label: Multiplying fractions (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiplying fractions (age 11+)” objective: Interpret fractions and percentages as operators — find a fraction or percentage of an amount by multiplying, understanding that 'of' means multiply (e.g., 3/4 of 200 = 3/4 × 200 = 150).
subject: Mathematics

label: Adjectives vs adverbs
statement: Demonstrate the “Adjectives vs adverbs” objective: Use adjectives and adverbs correctly, choosing between them depending on whether a noun or verb/adjective is being modified (e.g., 'She ran quickly' vs 'She is quick').
subject: English

label: How the Body Stays in Balance
statement: Demonstrate the “How the Body Stays in Balance” objective: Explain homeostasis as the process of maintaining a stable internal environment; describe the main feedback loop systems (negative feedback) using blood glucose regulation (insulin/glucagon) and body temperature as concrete examples; and connect the endocrine system (hormone-secreting glands) to the nervous system as two complementary communication systems with different speeds and durations.
subject: Science

label: Simple Chance Experiments
statement: Demonstrate the “Simple Chance Experiments” objective: Conduct simple probability experiments — flipping a coin, rolling a die, pulling coloured counters from a bag — record results, and compare experimental outcomes with expected theoretical outcomes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Grammar Terms: Pronouns and Determiners
statement: Demonstrate the “Grammar Terms: Pronouns and Determiners” objective: Know and use Year 4 grammar terminology including determiner, pronoun, possessive pronoun, and adverbial.
subject: English

label: Constructing mathematical arguments
statement: Demonstrate the “Constructing mathematical arguments” objective: Construct and present logical mathematical arguments involving multiple steps and formal reasoning; critique others' reasoning about fractions, algebra, ratio, or geometry and clearly explain errors or alternative approaches.
subject: Mathematics

label: Planning Narratives
statement: Demonstrate the “Planning Narratives” objective: Plan narrative writing by considering how authors have developed characters and settings, drawing on techniques observed in texts read, heard, or performed.
subject: English

label: Ocean Pollution & Harm
statement: Demonstrate the “Ocean Pollution & Harm” objective: Identify ways humans harm the ocean — plastic pollution, overfishing, oil spills, and ocean acidification from carbon dioxide — and understand that most ocean pollution comes from land-based activities, not just ships.
subject: Science

label: Common Plants & Trees
statement: Demonstrate the “Common Plants & Trees” objective: Identify and name common wild and garden plants, including deciduous and evergreen trees.
subject: Science

label: What Is Wind?
statement: Demonstrate the “What Is Wind?” objective: Know that wind is moving air, that it can be gentle (a breeze) or very strong (a gale), and that wind can move things like leaves, kites, flags, and even push people.
subject: Science

label: Choosing the Right Coping Strategy
statement: Demonstrate the “Choosing the Right Coping Strategy” objective: Understand that different situations require different coping strategies — what works for anger might not work for sadness, and what helps at school might be different from what helps at home.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: First Quadrant Coordinates
statement: Demonstrate the “First Quadrant Coordinates” objective: Describe positions on a 2-D grid as coordinates in the first quadrant.
subject: Mathematics

label: How Palaeontologists Work
statement: Demonstrate the “How Palaeontologists Work” objective: Describe how palaeontologists work in the field and lab: prospecting for exposed fossils, careful excavation with hand tools, plaster jacketing for transport, preparation in the lab, and scientific description and publication.
subject: Science

label: Types of Weather
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of Weather” objective: Identify and describe different types of weather — sunny, rainy, windy, snowy, cloudy, foggy, stormy — and describe what the weather is like today using simple vocabulary.
subject: Science

label: Nutrient Cycling in Thin Soil
statement: Demonstrate the “Nutrient Cycling in Thin Soil” objective: Understand the paradox of nutrient cycling in rainforests — despite lush growth, rainforest soil is typically thin and nutrient-poor because most nutrients are locked in living organisms, not the soil; decomposition is rapid in the warm, wet conditions, and nutrients released from dead material are immediately absorbed by plant roots and fungi, creating a fast, closed-loop recycling system.
subject: Science

label: Reasoning with Equivalences
statement: Demonstrate the “Reasoning with Equivalences” objective: Recognise and use repeated reasoning to generalise: extend patterns in equivalent fractions and percentage conversions, derive unknown facts from known facts, describe general rules for sequences and predict terms.
subject: Mathematics

label: Personal Coping Toolkit
statement: Demonstrate the “Personal Coping Toolkit” objective: Reflect on which self-regulation and coping strategies work best for them personally, building a 'toolkit' of approaches they can draw on in different situations and sharing what works with others.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Ancient Egypt's Lasting Legacy
statement: Demonstrate the “Ancient Egypt's Lasting Legacy” objective: Evaluate ancient Egypt's lasting legacy: the Egyptians developed early forms of medicine, mathematics (used to build pyramids and survey land after floods), astronomy (calendar based on star observations), and engineering that influenced later civilisations including Greece and Rome — and compare ancient Egypt with other early civilisations (Mesopotamia, Indus Valley, Shang Dynasty) to identify shared features like writing, agriculture, cities, and organised religion.
subject: History

label: Real Dinosaurs vs Fiction
statement: Demonstrate the “Real Dinosaurs vs Fiction” objective: Distinguish real dinosaurs from fictional or commonly confused creatures — pterosaurs (flying reptiles) and plesiosaurs (marine reptiles) were not dinosaurs, and movie dinosaurs are not always accurate.
subject: Science

label: Measuring angles (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring angles (age 11+)” objective: Draw and measure line segments and angles accurately using ruler and protractor, and interpret scale drawings to extract real measurements.
subject: Mathematics

label: Magnetic Poles
statement: Demonstrate the “Magnetic Poles” objective: Describe magnets as having two poles (north and south) and predict whether two magnets will attract or repel based on which poles face each other.
subject: Science

label: Addition and subtraction strategies (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Addition and subtraction strategies (age 10+)” objective: Add and subtract decimals to hundredths using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate strategies to written methods and explain reasoning.
subject: Mathematics

label: Order of operations
statement: Demonstrate the “Order of operations” objective: Understand and apply the conventional order of operations (PEMDAS/BODMAS) to carry out calculations involving the four operations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Measuring with different units
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring with different units” objective: Measure the length of an object using two different length units and describe how the measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen.
subject: Mathematics

label: Purpose, audience, and context
