statement: Demonstrate the “Purpose, audience, and context” objective: Identify the purpose, audience, and context of a text and use this knowledge to support comprehension — recognising how writing aimed at different audiences (academic, popular, persuasive) uses different conventions, register, and tone.
subject: English

label: Setting Learning Goals
statement: Demonstrate the “Setting Learning Goals” objective: Set a specific learning goal, work towards it with a deliberate plan, then honestly assess whether you achieved it and what you would change.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Peer Pressure and Resisting It
statement: Demonstrate the “Peer Pressure and Resisting It” objective: Understand peer pressure — the influence friends and peers can have on your choices and behaviour — and develop strategies for resisting pressure to do something they know is wrong or that makes them uncomfortable.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Risk, Uncertainty, and Cognitive Bias
statement: Demonstrate the “Risk, Uncertainty, and Cognitive Bias” objective: Distinguish between risk (decisions with known probabilities) and uncertainty (decisions with unknown outcomes); identify cognitive biases that distort risk assessment: availability heuristic (judging likelihood by how easily examples come to mind), present bias (overvaluing the immediate over the future), optimism bias (underestimating personal risk), and groupthink; understand why adolescent brains are biologically calibrated toward higher risk tolerance; apply a structured decision-making framework to real choices; understand the role of personal values in decisions where facts alone cannot determine the answer.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Designing for Weather Hazards
statement: Demonstrate the “Designing for Weather Hazards” objective: Make a claim about the merit of a design solution that reduces the impacts of a weather-related hazard such as flooding, wind damage, or extreme temperatures.
subject: Science

label: How Authors Treat Similar Themes
statement: Demonstrate the “How Authors Treat Similar Themes” objective: Compare and contrast stories in the same genre on their approaches to similar themes and topics, identifying how different authors treat common ideas.
subject: English

label: The Digestive Journey
statement: Demonstrate the “The Digestive Journey” objective: Trace the journey of food through the digestive system: food enters the mouth where teeth break it down and saliva begins digestion, travels down the oesophagus to the stomach, passes through the small intestine where nutrients are absorbed, and waste moves through the large intestine.
subject: Science

label: Tricky words
statement: Demonstrate the “Tricky words” objective: Spell common exception words from memory that do not follow regular phonic patterns, including the days of the week.
subject: English

label: Species Distribution & Change
statement: Demonstrate the “Species Distribution & Change” objective: Explain how environmental change (climate change, habitat loss, pollution) affects the distribution of species, including range shifts, local extinction, and invasive species.
subject: Science

label: Energy stores and transfers
statement: Demonstrate the “Energy stores and transfers” objective: Identify the main energy stores (kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic potential, thermal, chemical, nuclear, electromagnetic) and the pathways by which energy is transferred between stores (mechanically, electrically, by heating, by radiation).
subject: Science

label: Using Simple Formulae
statement: Demonstrate the “Using Simple Formulae” objective: Use simple formulae expressed in words or symbols to calculate values (e.g. perimeter = 2 × (length + width)).
subject: Mathematics

label: Real-World Robots
statement: Demonstrate the “Real-World Robots” objective: What a robot really is — not the sci-fi version; robots in factories, robot vacuum cleaners, robot arms in surgery; that robots follow instructions given by people.
subject: Computing

label: Area by Tiling
statement: Demonstrate the “Area by Tiling” objective: Find the area of a rectangle by tiling it with unit squares and show that the result equals the product of the side lengths.
subject: Mathematics

label: Using Multiple Sources
statement: Demonstrate the “Using Multiple Sources” objective: Draw on information from multiple print or digital sources, demonstrating the ability to locate an answer to a question quickly or solve a problem efficiently.
subject: English

label: Earth's Layers
statement: Demonstrate the “Earth's Layers” objective: Know that Earth has layers — a thin outer crust, a thick hot mantle, and a core at the centre — and that the inside of the Earth is extremely hot.
subject: Science

label: Reading and writing numbers (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading and writing numbers (age 9+)” objective: Read, write, order, and compare whole numbers up to at least 1,000,000 using base-ten numerals, number names, expanded form, and place-value understanding.
subject: Mathematics

label: Place value of each digit
statement: Demonstrate the “Place value of each digit” objective: Recognise the place value of each digit in a four-digit number (thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones).
subject: Mathematics

label: Efficiency, Sankey diagrams, and work done
statement: Demonstrate the “Efficiency, Sankey diagrams, and work done” objective: Calculate energy efficiency as the ratio of useful output energy to total input energy, construct and interpret Sankey diagrams, and calculate work done using work = force × distance.
subject: Science

label: How authors support their points
statement: Demonstrate the “How authors support their points” objective: Explain how an author of an informational text uses reasons and evidence to support particular points, evaluating whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient.
subject: English

label: Why seasons change
statement: Demonstrate the “Why seasons change” objective: Make observations at different times of year to relate the amount of daylight to the time of year, noticing longer days in summer and shorter days in winter.
subject: Science

label: Coordinate Transformations
statement: Demonstrate the “Coordinate Transformations” objective: Identify properties of translations, rotations, and reflections; describe and perform these transformations on given figures, and understand that the image is congruent to the original.
subject: Mathematics

label: Building an energy-converting device
statement: Demonstrate the “Building an energy-converting device” objective: Apply scientific ideas to design, test, and refine a device that converts energy from one form to another.
subject: Science

label: Variation in Species
statement: Demonstrate the “Variation in Species” objective: Explain variation within and between species, distinguishing between continuous variation (e.g. height) and discontinuous variation (e.g. blood group), and between genetic and environmental causes.
subject: Science

label: Unit fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Unit fractions” objective: Recognise, find, and write fractions of a discrete set of objects: unit fractions and non-unit fractions with small denominators.
subject: Mathematics

label: Modelling with multiplication and fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Modelling with multiplication and fractions” objective: Model real-world problems involving multiplication, area, fractions, and unit conversion by choosing appropriate representations and interpreting mathematical results in context.
subject: Mathematics

label: All times tables to 12×12
statement: Demonstrate the “All times tables to 12×12” objective: Recall multiplication and division facts for multiplication tables up to 12 × 12.
subject: Mathematics

label: Machine Learning Basics
statement: Demonstrate the “Machine Learning Basics” objective: How machine learning works at a conceptual level: show the computer many examples, it finds patterns, then it makes predictions about new things; hands-on experience with Teachable Machine or similar tool.
subject: Computing

label: Drawing Force Diagrams
statement: Demonstrate the “Drawing Force Diagrams” objective: Draw and interpret force diagrams showing forces as labelled arrows — where the arrow's length represents the force's magnitude and its direction shows which way the force acts; show multiple forces on one object; identify from the diagram whether forces are balanced (equal arrows in opposite directions, no resultant) or unbalanced (arrows of different sizes, producing a resultant); represent the resultant with a single arrow.
subject: Science

label: The subjunctive mood
statement: Demonstrate the “The subjunctive mood” objective: Use the subjunctive form in formal writing and speech to express wishes, demands, suggestions, or hypothetical situations (e.g., 'If I were you', 'I suggest that he go', 'Were they to arrive').
subject: English

label: Ways to Pay
statement: Demonstrate the “Ways to Pay” objective: Different ways to pay: cash, debit cards, contactless, online payments, mobile payments; that digital payments still use real money; keeping payment details safe.
subject: Life Skills

label: Organ Systems Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Organ Systems Vocabulary” objective: Use technical vocabulary for the major organ systems — organ, organ system, circulatory system, digestive system, respiratory system, skeletal system, muscular system, nutrient, oxygen, carbon dioxide, blood vessel, artery, vein, capillary, enzyme — and describe the function of each system using these terms.
subject: Science

label: Emotions and Decision-Making
statement: Demonstrate the “Emotions and Decision-Making” objective: Understand how emotions influence thinking and decision-making — that strong feelings can cloud judgement, that we often make different choices when calm versus when upset, and that recognising this gives us more control.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Measuring length and height (age 5+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring length and height (age 5+)” objective: Measure and begin to record lengths and heights using non-standard and standard units.
subject: Mathematics

label: Trigonometry basics
statement: Demonstrate the “Trigonometry basics” objective: Use the trigonometric ratios sin, cos, and tan in right-angled triangles to find unknown sides and angles, including setting up the correct ratio for a given problem.
subject: Mathematics

label: Interpreting visual information in texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Interpreting visual information in texts” objective: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively in informational texts (e.g., charts, graphs, diagrams, timelines, animations) and explain how it contributes to understanding the text.
subject: English

label: Tides, Waves & Currents
statement: Demonstrate the “Tides, Waves & Currents” objective: Know that the ocean has tides (water level rises and falls twice a day, caused mainly by the Moon's gravity), waves (caused by wind), and currents (rivers of water flowing through the ocean that carry warmth and nutrients around the world).
subject: Science

label: Cold-Weather Adaptations
statement: Demonstrate the “Cold-Weather Adaptations” objective: Understand how polar animals are adapted to survive extreme cold — blubber (thick fat layer) insulates seals and whales, hollow fur traps air for warmth in polar bears, counter-current heat exchange in penguin flippers prevents heat loss, Arctic foxes grow thick white winter coats for camouflage and warmth, and some animals migrate to avoid the harshest months.
subject: Science

label: Dividing by 10 and 100
statement: Demonstrate the “Dividing by 10 and 100” objective: Find the effect of dividing a one- or two-digit number by 10 and 100, identifying the value of the digits as ones, tenths, and hundredths.
subject: Mathematics

label: Tenths (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Tenths (age 9+)” objective: Recognise and use thousandths; relate them to tenths, hundredths, and their decimal equivalents (e.g. 1/1000 = 0.001, 35/1000 = 0.035).
subject: Mathematics

label: Understanding angles (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding angles (age 9+)” objective: Use the properties of rectangles to deduce related facts and find missing lengths and angles.
subject: Mathematics

label: Building the Pyramids
statement: Demonstrate the “Building the Pyramids” objective: Understand how the pyramids were built: thousands of workers moved enormous stone blocks using ramps, rollers, and sledges, the work was organised by the pharaoh's officials, and the design evolved from flat-topped mastabas to step pyramids (like Djoser's) to the smooth-sided Great Pyramid — and know that later pharaohs were buried in hidden rock-cut tombs in the Valley of the Kings.
subject: History

label: Data and Information for Computers
statement: Demonstrate the “Data and Information for Computers” objective: What data is: information that computers use — numbers, words, pictures, sounds; everything a computer knows comes from data that people give it.
subject: Computing

label: Expanding Double Brackets
statement: Demonstrate the “Expanding Double Brackets” objective: Expand products of two or more binomials, e.g., (x + 3)(x - 2) = x² + x - 6, using the grid method or FOIL; simplify the result by collecting like terms.
subject: Mathematics

label: Irregular past tense verbs
statement: Demonstrate the “Irregular past tense verbs” objective: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregular verbs correctly (e.g., sat, hid, told, went, came, ran), recognising that these do not follow the regular -ed pattern.
subject: English

label: Changing Ideas About Space
statement: Demonstrate the “Changing Ideas About Space” objective: Understand that ideas about the solar system changed over time: ancient people believed Earth was at the centre (geocentric model, Ptolemy), until Copernicus proposed the Sun was at the centre (heliocentric model), later confirmed by Galileo’s telescope observations.
subject: Science

label: Synthesising across multiple texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Synthesising across multiple texts” objective: Integrate information from several texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably, combining information without plagiarising.
subject: English

label: Explaining Mathematical Reasoning
statement: Demonstrate the “Explaining Mathematical Reasoning” objective: With teacher prompting, explain and justify mathematical reasoning using drawings, number sentences, or words.
subject: Mathematics

label: 2-D shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “2-D shapes” objective: Recognise and name common 2-D shapes (circles, triangles, rectangles including squares).
subject: Mathematics

label: Place value understanding and number facts
statement: Demonstrate the “Place value understanding and number facts” objective: Use place value understanding and number facts to solve problems.
subject: Mathematics

label: Deep-Ocean Exploration Technology
statement: Demonstrate the “Deep-Ocean Exploration Technology” objective: Explain how crewed submersibles (Alvin, Deepsea Challenger) and remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) allow exploration of the deep; describe acoustic seafloor mapping using sonar and why only ~25% of the ocean floor has been mapped at high resolution; explore why the deep ocean is harder to explore than the surface of the Moon (pressure, cold, darkness, communication difficulties); survey astrobiology missions targeting ocean worlds in our solar system.
subject: Science

label: Compound Units
statement: Demonstrate the “Compound Units” objective: Use compound units such as speed (distance ÷ time), unit pricing (cost ÷ quantity), and density (mass ÷ volume); solve problems involving compound units.
subject: Mathematics

label: Feeling of not understanding
statement: Demonstrate the “Feeling of not understanding” objective: Notice the feeling of not understanding — recognise when something is confusing rather than reading or listening past it.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Character Traits and Motivation
statement: Demonstrate the “Character Traits and Motivation” objective: Analyse character traits, motivations, and feelings using text evidence, and distinguish one's own point of view from that of the narrator or characters.
subject: English

label: Rainforest Conservation
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Conservation” objective: Know the main approaches to rainforest conservation — protected areas and national parks, reforestation and rewilding programmes, sustainable certification schemes (Rainforest Alliance, FSC), recognition of indigenous land rights as the most effective form of forest protection, and international agreements like REDD+ that pay countries to keep forests standing.
subject: Science

label: Polar Ecosystems Compared
statement: Demonstrate the “Polar Ecosystems Compared” objective: Compare Arctic and Antarctic ecosystems — the Arctic has both terrestrial (tundra) and marine ecosystems supporting large land mammals and indigenous human communities, while the Antarctic is almost entirely marine-based with virtually no land plants or mammals; both regions have short, intense food chains anchored by phytoplankton and krill, and both are disproportionately affected by climate change and human activity.
subject: Science

label: Fractions on a number line
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions on a number line” objective: Recognise and use fractions as numbers: place unit fractions and non-unit fractions with small denominators on a number line.
subject: Mathematics

label: Oceans & Climate
statement: Demonstrate the “Oceans & Climate” objective: Understand the connection between the ocean and climate: the ocean absorbs heat and carbon dioxide, drives weather patterns through evaporation, and ocean currents distribute warmth around the planet — making the ocean Earth's climate engine.
subject: Science

label: Shapes of land and water
statement: Demonstrate the “Shapes of land and water” objective: Develop a model to represent the shapes and kinds of land (mountains, valleys, plains) and bodies of water (rivers, lakes, oceans) in an area.
subject: Science

label: Pitch of Sounds
statement: Demonstrate the “Pitch of Sounds” objective: Find patterns between the pitch of a sound and features of the object that produced it.
subject: Science

label: Expressing Feelings with Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Expressing Feelings with Words” objective: Express their own feelings appropriately using words rather than actions — saying 'I feel angry because...' instead of hitting, shouting, or withdrawing.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Syllables (age 6+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Syllables (age 6+)” objective: Decode words of two or more syllables by breaking them into syllable chunks, applying knowledge that every syllable must contain a vowel sound, and blending the parts together.
subject: English

label: 10 More or 10 Less
statement: Demonstrate the “10 More or 10 Less” objective: Mentally find 10 more or 10 less than a given two-digit number without counting.
subject: Mathematics

label: Algebraic Notation
statement: Demonstrate the “Algebraic Notation” objective: Use and interpret algebraic notation including: ab for a × b, 3y for y + y + y, a² for a × a, a/b for a ÷ b, coefficients as fractions, and brackets for grouping; read and write algebraic expressions fluently.
subject: Mathematics

label: Where Elements Come From
statement: Demonstrate the “Where Elements Come From” objective: Explain stellar nucleosynthesis: the Big Bang produced mainly hydrogen and helium; main-sequence fusion builds elements up to iron; and supernovae produce elements heavier than iron and scatter them into space — meaning the atoms in our bodies were forged in ancient stars.
subject: Science

label: What Living Things Need
statement: Demonstrate the “What Living Things Need” objective: Understand what plants and animals (including humans) need to survive: water, food, air, and suitable conditions.
subject: Science

label: Ocean Food Chains
statement: Demonstrate the “Ocean Food Chains” objective: Describe a simple ocean food chain: tiny plants (phytoplankton) are eaten by small animals, which are eaten by bigger fish, which are eaten by top predators like sharks — showing that all ocean life depends on others for food.
subject: Science

label: Everyday Kindness and Care
statement: Demonstrate the “Everyday Kindness and Care” objective: Show kindness and care towards others in simple everyday ways — comforting a friend who is upset, helping someone who has dropped their things, sharing without being asked, and saying kind words.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Properties of Operations
statement: Demonstrate the “Properties of Operations” objective: Apply properties of operations (commutative, associative, distributive) as strategies to multiply and divide.
subject: Mathematics

label: Numbers to 10,000
statement: Demonstrate the “Numbers to 10,000” objective: Identify, represent, and estimate numbers up to 10,000 using different representations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Contact & Non-Contact Forces
statement: Demonstrate the “Contact & Non-Contact Forces” objective: Notice that some forces need contact between two objects (contact forces) while magnetic forces can act at a distance (non-contact forces).
subject: Science

label: Different viewpoints in texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Different viewpoints in texts” objective: Describe how a narrator's or speaker's point of view influences how events are described, recognising the difference between limited and omniscient narration and how perspective shapes storytelling.
subject: English

label: Thinking Before Starting
statement: Demonstrate the “Thinking Before Starting” objective: Before starting something new, stop and think: what do I already know about this topic?
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Why We Have Seasons
statement: Demonstrate the “Why We Have Seasons” objective: Explain that the seasons are caused by the tilt of Earth's axis during its orbit around the Sun, distinguishing this from the common misconception that seasons are caused by changing distance from the Sun.
subject: Science

label: Knowing What You Don't Know
statement: Demonstrate the “Knowing What You Don't Know” objective: Monitor your own vocabulary gaps — notice words you half-know, distinguish confident from uncertain knowledge, and develop strategies to resolve the uncertainty.
subject: English

label: Life Cycle of a Star
statement: Demonstrate the “Life Cycle of a Star” objective: Describe the life cycle of a star from nebula through main sequence to its end state (white dwarf, neutron star, or black hole depending on mass), and relate the life cycle to the origin of elements heavier than hydrogen.
subject: Science

label: Naming Basic Emotions
statement: Demonstrate the “Naming Basic Emotions” objective: Name and recognise basic emotions — happy, sad, angry, scared, excited, and surprised — in themselves and in others by looking at facial expressions and body language.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Classifying shapes by properties
statement: Demonstrate the “Classifying shapes by properties” objective: Compare and classify geometric shapes based on their properties and sizes; understand that attributes belonging to a category also belong to all subcategories; classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.
subject: Mathematics

label: Building Writing Stamina
statement: Demonstrate the “Building Writing Stamina” objective: Write about real events and for different purposes, developing stamina for sustained writing across genres beyond narrative (e.g., recounts, letters, instructions).
subject: English

label: Earth's atmosphere
statement: Demonstrate the “Earth's atmosphere” objective: Develop a model to describe ways the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere interact as connected Earth systems.
subject: Science

label: Immunity & Vaccines
statement: Demonstrate the “Immunity & Vaccines” objective: Distinguish innate (non-specific, immediate) from adaptive (specific, memory-forming) immunity; explain how B cells produce antibodies that recognise specific antigens, how T cells destroy infected cells, and why immunological memory makes vaccines work; and describe the gut microbiome as a community of trillions of microbes that significantly influences immune function.
subject: Science

label: Multiplying and dividing
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiplying and dividing” objective: Multiply and divide whole numbers and those involving decimals by 10, 100, and 1000.
subject: Mathematics

label: Muscles Work in Pairs
statement: Demonstrate the “Muscles Work in Pairs” objective: Explain that muscles work in antagonistic pairs — one contracts while the other relaxes — to produce movement, using the bicep and tricep as a key example.
subject: Science

label: Using a Microscope
statement: Demonstrate the “Using a Microscope” objective: Use a light microscope correctly to prepare, focus, and examine biological specimens, including making accurate labelled drawings at an appropriate magnification.
subject: Science

label: Vivid Word Choices
statement: Demonstrate the “Vivid Word Choices” objective: Choose precise and vivid words and phrases to create specific effects in writing.
subject: English

label: Early Maths Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Early Maths Vocabulary” objective: Use mathematical words carefully when counting, comparing, and describing shapes and positions.
subject: Mathematics

label: Conjunctions, Prepositions and Interjections
statement: Demonstrate the “Conjunctions, Prepositions and Interjections” objective: Explain the function of conjunctions, prepositions, and interjections in general and in particular sentences, understanding how each word class contributes to meaning.
subject: English

label: Reading Decimal Places
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading Decimal Places” objective: Identify the value of each digit in numbers given to three decimal places (e.g. in 4.378, the 7 represents 7 hundredths).
subject: Mathematics

label: Building on Others in Discussions
statement: Demonstrate the “Building on Others in Discussions” objective: Pose and respond to specific questions in discussions, making comments that contribute to the discussion and elaborate on the remarks of others.
subject: English

label: Series vs parallel circuits
statement: Demonstrate the “Series vs parallel circuits” objective: Describe and apply the rules for current, voltage, and resistance in series and parallel circuits, and explain the practical uses of each circuit type.
subject: Science

label: Reading and drawing circuit diagrams
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading and drawing circuit diagrams” objective: Draw and read simple circuit diagrams using standard symbols for cells, bulbs, switches, buzzers, and wires; identify whether a circuit is complete or broken from a diagram; match circuit diagrams to physical circuits.
subject: Science

label: The Heart & Blood
statement: Demonstrate the “The Heart & Blood” objective: Understand that the heart is a muscle that pumps blood around the body through tubes called blood vessels, and that we can feel our heartbeat by placing a hand on our chest or fingers on our wrist.
subject: Science

label: Inference vs Explicit Meaning
statement: Demonstrate the “Inference vs Explicit Meaning” objective: Distinguish between what a text explicitly says and what you have inferred, assumed, or read in — knowing which is which is fundamental to honest comprehension.
subject: English

label: Division as equal sharing
statement: Demonstrate the “Division as equal sharing” objective: Understand division as sharing equally into groups or as grouping (how many groups of a given size can be made).
subject: Mathematics

label: Ethical Frameworks and Moral Reasoning
statement: Demonstrate the “Ethical Frameworks and Moral Reasoning” objective: Introduce the three main ethical frameworks: consequentialism (judge actions by outcomes and overall welfare), deontology (judge actions by adherence to rules and duties regardless of consequences), and virtue ethics (judge actions by the character they reflect); apply each framework to real-world moral dilemmas: climate responsibility, AI ethics, civil disobedience, wealth inequality, healthcare rationing; understand the strengths and limitations of each framework; develop the capacity for careful moral reasoning — the ability to think through ethical questions systematically rather than relying only on intuition or group opinion.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Earth & Space Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Earth & Space Vocabulary” objective: Use technical vocabulary for Earth's motion and the wider universe — rotation, revolution, axis, tilt, orbit, light year, gravitational force, atmosphere, lunar phases, waxing, waning, solstice, equinox, eclipse — and apply these when explaining day and night, the seasons, and the Moon's phases.
subject: Science

label: How animals adapt to environments
statement: Demonstrate the “How animals adapt to environments” objective: Identify how animals and plants are adapted to suit their environment and understand that adaptation may lead to evolution over time.
subject: Science

label: Upper and Lower Egypt
statement: Demonstrate the “Upper and Lower Egypt” objective: Understand that ancient Egypt was divided into Upper Egypt (the narrow river valley in the south) and Lower Egypt (the wide delta in the north), that the two lands were united under one pharaoh, and that Egyptians managed the Nile's water through irrigation canals and shadufs to grow crops year-round.
subject: History

label: Advanced Punctuation for Clarity
statement: Demonstrate the “Advanced Punctuation for Clarity” objective: Use punctuation confidently and accurately for effect and clarity — including semicolons to link related clauses, colons to introduce lists or explanations, dashes and parentheses for parenthetical information, ellipsis for omission or suspense, and commas for coordinate adjectives and nonrestrictive elements.
subject: English

label: Salt Water vs Fresh Water
statement: Demonstrate the “Salt Water vs Fresh Water” objective: Describe and graph the amounts of salt water and fresh water in various reservoirs to provide evidence about the distribution of water on Earth.
subject: Science

label: Caring for minibeasts
statement: Demonstrate the “Caring for minibeasts” objective: Caring for minibeasts: observing minibeasts gently, handling them carefully, putting them back where you found them. Why minibeasts matter — they help gardens grow, break down dead leaves, and feed other animals.
subject: Science

label: Division with Decimals
statement: Demonstrate the “Division with Decimals” objective: Use written division methods in cases where the answer has up to two decimal places; divide decimals to hundredths by whole numbers.
subject: Mathematics

label: Evidence Versus Interpretation
statement: Demonstrate the “Evidence Versus Interpretation” objective: Distinguish between historical evidence and historical interpretation — evidence is what survived, interpretation is the argument a historian builds from it, and the same evidence can support different arguments.
subject: History

label: What Plants Need to Thrive
statement: Demonstrate the “What Plants Need to Thrive” objective: Explore and compare the requirements of plants for life and growth: air, light, water, nutrients from soil, and room to grow.
subject: Science

label: The Medieval Church
statement: Demonstrate the “The Medieval Church” objective: The enormous power of the medieval Church: monasteries and the daily life of monks and nuns; building great cathedrals; pilgrimage as a religious journey; the Church's influence over everyday life.
subject: History

label: Real-world fraction multiplication
statement: Demonstrate the “Real-world fraction multiplication” objective: Solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers, using visual fraction models or equations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Evolution vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Evolution vocabulary” objective: Use technical vocabulary for evolution and natural selection — adaptation, evolution, natural selection, extinct, extinction, fossil record, species, common ancestor, mutation, variation — and explain the mechanism of natural selection using these terms in the correct sequence.
subject: Science

label: Translating and reflecting shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Translating and reflecting shapes” objective: Draw and translate simple shapes on the coordinate plane; reflect shapes in the axes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Wave Properties & Types
statement: Demonstrate the “Wave Properties & Types” objective: Describe waves in terms of amplitude, wavelength, frequency, and wave speed; distinguish transverse waves (oscillation perpendicular to direction of travel) from longitudinal waves (oscillation parallel); and use the wave equation v = fλ.
subject: Science

label: Greek and Roman Architecture
statement: Demonstrate the “Greek and Roman Architecture” objective: Identify Greek column styles — Doric (plain and sturdy), Ionic (scroll-shaped capitals), and Corinthian (ornate leafy capitals) — and Roman architectural innovations — the arch, the dome, and concrete — and spot their influence in modern public buildings such as courthouses, museums, government buildings, and monuments.
subject: History

label: Knights & Armour
statement: Demonstrate the “Knights & Armour” objective: What knights were: trained warriors who served a lord; armour, shields, swords, and lances; the code of chivalry as rules for how knights should behave.
subject: History

label: Adding and subtracting (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding and subtracting (age 10+)” objective: Solve addition and subtraction multi-step problems in contexts, deciding which operations and methods to use and why, with numbers up to 10,000,000 and decimals.
subject: Mathematics

label: Addition and subtraction within 20
statement: Demonstrate the “Addition and subtraction within 20” objective: Add and subtract within 20 using strategies such as making ten, decomposing a number leading to ten, and using known facts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Marketing Basics
statement: Demonstrate the “Marketing Basics” objective: How people find out about what you're selling; signs, posters, social media, word of mouth; being persuasive; the basics of advertising and promotion.
subject: Life Skills

label: Counting Within 1,000
statement: Demonstrate the “Counting Within 1,000” objective: Count within 1000, including skip-counting by 5s, 10s, and 100s.
subject: Mathematics

label: Brackets and dashes for parenthesis
statement: Demonstrate the “Brackets and dashes for parenthesis” objective: Use brackets, dashes, and commas to indicate parenthesis — additional information inserted into a sentence that could be removed without changing the sentence's core meaning.
subject: English

label: What Ocean Animals Need
statement: Demonstrate the “What Ocean Animals Need” objective: Understand that ocean animals need food, shelter, and the right conditions to survive — just like land animals — and that different parts of the ocean provide for different animals' needs.
subject: Science

label: Indigenous Ecological Knowledge
statement: Demonstrate the “Indigenous Ecological Knowledge” objective: Understand that indigenous peoples of the rainforest have developed deep ecological knowledge over thousands of years — using plants for medicine, food, and building materials, practising sustainable farming methods like shifting cultivation, and understanding animal behaviour and forest ecology in ways that modern science is only beginning to appreciate.
subject: Science

label: Rote counting to 100
statement: Demonstrate the “Rote counting to 100” objective: Rote count forwards and backwards from 0 to 100, beginning from 0, 1, or any given number, by ones.
subject: Mathematics

label: Preventing Erosion
statement: Demonstrate the “Preventing Erosion” objective: Compare multiple solutions designed to slow or prevent wind or water from changing the shape of the land.
subject: Science

label: Ecology Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Ecology Vocabulary” objective: Use vocabulary for feeding relationships and ecological roles — producer, consumer, predator, prey, herbivore, carnivore, omnivore, decomposer, food chain, food web, nutrient cycle — and describe how energy and matter flow through ecosystems using these terms.
subject: Science

label: Incredible insects: record-breakers
statement: Demonstrate the “Incredible insects: record-breakers” objective: Incredible insects — record-breakers and superpowers. Dung beetles are the strongest animals relative to body weight. Dragonflies are among the fastest flying insects. Fleas can jump over 150 times their own body length. Bombardier beetles spray boiling chemicals. The 'wow factor' of the insect world.
subject: Science

label: Palaeoart & Speculation
statement: Demonstrate the “Palaeoart & Speculation” objective: Understand that palaeoart — scientific illustrations and models of dinosaurs — is based on fossil evidence but involves informed speculation about skin colour, feathers, and soft tissues that don't usually fossilise.
subject: Science

label: Measuring & Plotting Lengths
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring & Plotting Lengths” objective: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths to the nearest whole unit and display the data on a line plot.
subject: Mathematics

label: Questioning First Impressions
statement: Demonstrate the “Questioning First Impressions” objective: Notice when your first reading of a social situation might be wrong — your assumptions about why someone acted a certain way are not always facts.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Listening and responding
statement: Demonstrate the “Listening and responding” objective: Listen and respond appropriately to adults and peers; follow agreed-upon rules for discussion such as listening to others and taking turns speaking.
subject: English

label: Pure Substances & Mixtures
statement: Demonstrate the “Pure Substances & Mixtures” objective: Distinguish between pure substances and mixtures, identify formulations as useful mixtures with precise compositions, and use melting and boiling points to test for purity.
subject: Science

label: Arrays for multiplication (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Arrays for multiplication (age 9+)” objective: Divide numbers up to four digits by a one-digit number using short division (and place-value/array strategies); interpret remainders appropriately for the context.
subject: Mathematics

label: Fairness, Equality and Equity
statement: Demonstrate the “Fairness, Equality and Equity” objective: Understand what fairness means and why it matters — recognising that fair doesn't always mean equal (everyone getting the same) but can mean equitable (everyone getting what they need), and applying this understanding in group situations.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Measuring Earthquake Strength
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring Earthquake Strength” objective: Know that scientists measure earthquakes using seismometers, that earthquakes release energy that travels as waves through the ground, and that a magnitude scale describes their strength.
subject: Science

label: Roman numerals to 100
statement: Demonstrate the “Roman numerals to 100” objective: Read Roman numerals to 100 (I to C) and understand that the numeral system changed over time to include zero and place value.
subject: Mathematics

label: Dissolving & Solutions
statement: Demonstrate the “Dissolving & Solutions” objective: Understand that some materials dissolve in liquid to form a solution, and describe how to recover a substance from a solution by evaporation.
subject: Science

label: Right Angles & Turns
statement: Demonstrate the “Right Angles & Turns” objective: Identify right angles; recognise that two right angles make a half-turn, three make three-quarters, and four make a complete turn.
subject: Mathematics

label: Estimating and comparing money
statement: Demonstrate the “Estimating and comparing money” objective: Estimate, compare, and calculate different measures including money in pounds and pence.
subject: Mathematics

label: Comparing Large Numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing Large Numbers” objective: Order and compare numbers beyond 1000.
subject: Mathematics

label: Breaking Tasks into Steps
statement: Demonstrate the “Breaking Tasks into Steps” objective: Break a challenging task into smaller, manageable steps rather than feeling overwhelmed by the whole thing — and celebrate progress along the way.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Perimeter (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Perimeter (age 10+)” objective: Recognise that shapes with the same area can have different perimeters and vice versa; explore this relationship systematically.
subject: Mathematics

label: Apostrophes: Contraction and Possession
statement: Demonstrate the “Apostrophes: Contraction and Possession” objective: Use apostrophes in writing for both contraction (marking omitted letters) and singular possession, distinguishing the two uses.
subject: English

label: Progressive and Continuous Tenses
statement: Demonstrate the “Progressive and Continuous Tenses” objective: Form and use the progressive (continuous) verb tenses — past progressive (was walking), present progressive (am walking), and future progressive (will be walking) — to convey ongoing actions at different times.
subject: English

label: The Red Queen Hypothesis
statement: Demonstrate the “The Red Queen Hypothesis” objective: Introduce the Red Queen hypothesis — species must keep evolving just to maintain fitness relative to co-evolving partners; describe predator-prey arms races (cheetah speed vs gazelle speed, bat echolocation vs moth hearing jamming) and parasite-host co-evolution (myxomatosis in rabbits); explain Darwin's hawk moth and orchid as a classic example of mutualistic co-evolution predicting an unknown species; understand that co-evolution is a major driver of biological diversification.
subject: Science

label: Area of Triangles & Parallelograms
statement: Demonstrate the “Area of Triangles & Parallelograms” objective: Calculate the area of parallelograms and triangles using formulae (A = b × h for parallelograms, A = ½ × b × h for triangles).
subject: Mathematics

label: Roman Army and Conquest of Britain
statement: Demonstrate the “Roman Army and Conquest of Britain” objective: Describe how the Roman army was organised into legions of highly trained soldiers, how Julius Caesar first raided Britain in 55 BC and Emperor Claudius later conquered it in AD 43, and explain why the Romans wanted to expand their empire — for land, resources, taxes, and glory.
subject: History

label: Advanced Figurative Language
statement: Demonstrate the “Advanced Figurative Language” objective: Understand and interpret figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meaning — including allusion, irony, pun, oxymoron, and extended metaphor — and distinguish between connotation and denotation when analysing or choosing words.
subject: English

label: Listening to Texts Read Aloud
statement: Demonstrate the “Listening to Texts Read Aloud” objective: Listen to and discuss poems, stories, and non-fiction at a level beyond independent reading; confirm understanding of texts read aloud by asking and answering questions about key details.
subject: English

label: Ancient Greece and Rome on the Map
statement: Demonstrate the “Ancient Greece and Rome on the Map” objective: Locate Greece and Italy on a map and know they are countries around the Mediterranean Sea where two great ancient civilisations — Ancient Greece and Ancient Rome — grew up thousands of years ago, long after the ancient Egyptians but long before our time.
subject: History

label: Pyramids and the Great Sphinx
statement: Demonstrate the “Pyramids and the Great Sphinx” objective: Know that the ancient Egyptians built enormous stone pyramids as tombs for the pharaohs, that the Great Pyramid at Giza was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World and is still standing today, and that the Great Sphinx — a statue with a lion's body and a human head — guards the pyramids.
subject: History

label: Flat vs Solid Shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Flat vs Solid Shapes” objective: Distinguish two-dimensional (flat) shapes from three-dimensional (solid) shapes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Edges, vertices, and faces
statement: Demonstrate the “Edges, vertices, and faces” objective: Identify and describe properties of 3-D shapes including the number of edges, vertices, and faces.
subject: Mathematics

label: Emotion Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Emotion Vocabulary” objective: Use a wider vocabulary of emotion words beyond the basics — including frustrated, worried, anxious, embarrassed, jealous, proud, disappointed, grateful, and lonely — and distinguish between similar emotions.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Ocean Currents and Global Heat
statement: Demonstrate the “Ocean Currents and Global Heat” objective: Explain thermohaline circulation (the global conveyor belt) as driven by temperature and salinity differences that cause dense water to sink; describe how the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) transfers heat from the tropics toward Europe; explain that oceans absorb more than 90% of excess heat and ~25% of CO2 from human emissions; explore what would happen to Northern European climates if circulation weakened.
subject: Science

label: Choosing Tenses for Precise Meaning
statement: Demonstrate the “Choosing Tenses for Precise Meaning” objective: Use verb tense to convey various times, sequences, states, and conditions, selecting tenses deliberately to express the precise timing and nature of actions and events.
subject: English

label: Adding and subtracting (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding and subtracting (age 8+)” objective: Add and subtract numbers with up to four digits using formal written methods of columnar addition and subtraction.
subject: Mathematics

label: Choosing the right strategy
statement: Demonstrate the “Choosing the right strategy” objective: Select and use appropriate tools and representations strategically, including choosing between mental methods, jottings, formal algorithms, and calculators for arithmetic with multi-digit numbers, decimals, and fractions.
subject: Mathematics

label: Simultaneous Equations
statement: Demonstrate the “Simultaneous Equations” objective: Understand that two linear equations can be solved simultaneously by finding the point where their graphs intersect, and interpret this graphically and algebraically as the pair of values satisfying both equations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Dinosaur-to-Bird Transition
statement: Demonstrate the “Dinosaur-to-Bird Transition” objective: Trace the evidence for the dinosaur-to-bird transition in depth: feathered theropods from the Liaoning Formation (China), the mix of dinosaur and bird features in Archaeopteryx, and the competing ground-up versus trees-down hypotheses for the origin of flight.
subject: Science

label: Composing Shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Composing Shapes” objective: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, quarter-circles) to create composite shapes, and compose new shapes from the composite shape.
subject: Mathematics

label: Aerobic Respiration
statement: Demonstrate the “Aerobic Respiration” objective: Explain aerobic respiration as the process by which organisms release energy from glucose using oxygen, producing carbon dioxide and water; write and interpret the word equation: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water.
subject: Science

label: Adding and subtracting
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding and subtracting” objective: Add and subtract one-digit and two-digit numbers to 20, including zero.
subject: Mathematics

label: Whales & Dolphins Are Mammals
statement: Demonstrate the “Whales & Dolphins Are Mammals” objective: Know that whales and dolphins are mammals, not fish — they breathe air, are warm-blooded, and feed their babies milk — even though they live in the ocean.
subject: Science

label: Earth's Atmosphere & CO2
statement: Demonstrate the “Earth's Atmosphere & CO2” objective: Describe the composition of Earth's atmosphere (mainly nitrogen and oxygen, with small amounts of CO₂ and other gases), explain how human activity increases CO₂, and describe the impact on global climate.
subject: Science

label: Wild, Farm & Pet Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Wild, Farm & Pet Animals” objective: Understand the difference between wild animals, farm animals, and pets — wild animals find their own food and shelter in nature; farm animals are kept by people for food, wool, or eggs; pets are animals people keep for companionship — and know that wild animals should be observed from a distance.
subject: Science

label: Material Properties Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Material Properties Vocabulary” objective: Use technical vocabulary to describe and compare material properties — conductor, insulator, thermal, electrical, transparent, opaque, translucent, soluble, insoluble, magnetic, flexible, rigid, density — and apply these terms precisely when selecting and justifying materials for particular purposes.
subject: Science

label: Asking for Help
statement: Demonstrate the “Asking for Help” objective: Ask for help when you've had a go yourself and are still stuck — knowing when to ask is a skill in itself.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: How fossils form
statement: Demonstrate the “How fossils form” objective: Describe in simple terms how fossils are formed when things that have lived are trapped within rock over millions of years.
subject: Science

label: Mental addition and subtraction (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Mental addition and subtraction (age 9+)” objective: Add and subtract numbers mentally with increasingly large numbers, using place-value knowledge and derived facts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Advertising & Spending
statement: Demonstrate the “Advertising & Spending” objective: How advertising tries to influence what we buy; being a critical consumer; understanding 'value for money'; the difference between emotional and rational spending.
subject: Life Skills

label: Emotional Intelligence
statement: Demonstrate the “Emotional Intelligence” objective: Introduce Goleman's emotional intelligence model (self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, social skills); develop vocabulary for complex emotional states (ambivalence, ennui, schadenfreude, awe, nostalgia, cognitive dissonance); understand the evidence linking emotional intelligence to wellbeing, relationship quality, and long-term life outcomes; reflect on personal emotional growth over the secondary school years; explore the relationship between emotional literacy and mental health, and know when to seek professional support.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Understanding fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding fractions” objective: Write simple fractions (e.g. 1/2 of 6 = 3) and recognise the equivalence of 2/4 and 1/2.
subject: Mathematics

label: Mathematical Precision
statement: Demonstrate the “Mathematical Precision” objective: Communicate with mathematical precision: use correct fraction/decimal vocabulary, name angle types accurately, specify units in measurement and money, and use notation (=, <, >, ÷, ×) correctly.
subject: Mathematics

label: Perimeter of Compound Shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Perimeter of Compound Shapes” objective: Measure and calculate the perimeter of composite rectilinear shapes in centimetres and metres.
subject: Mathematics

label: Evidence for Greek and Roman Life
statement: Demonstrate the “Evidence for Greek and Roman Life” objective: Understand that historians and archaeologists piece together ancient Greek and Roman life from evidence — pottery paintings, coins, inscriptions, ruins like Pompeii, and written texts by authors such as Homer and Pliny — and that the same evidence can be interpreted in different ways by different historians.
subject: History

label: Patterns & Codes for Information
statement: Demonstrate the “Patterns & Codes for Information” objective: Generate and compare multiple solutions that use patterns to transfer information, such as codes and signals.
subject: Science

label: Verb Voice and Mood
statement: Demonstrate the “Verb Voice and Mood” objective: Understand and use active and passive voice deliberately, and recognise verb moods (indicative, imperative, subjunctive, conditional) and their effects — choosing the appropriate voice and mood for purpose and audience.
subject: English

label: Grammar for Effect
statement: Demonstrate the “Grammar for Effect” objective: Analyse the effectiveness and impact of grammatical features in texts read — understanding how authors make deliberate grammatical choices (sentence length, passive voice, fronted adverbials, listing) to create specific effects on the reader.
subject: English

label: Exploring Ideas Through Talk
statement: Demonstrate the “Exploring Ideas Through Talk” objective: Use spoken language to develop understanding through speculating, hypothesising, imagining, and exploring ideas; use strategies to build vocabulary through talk.
subject: English

label: Building sentences
statement: Demonstrate the “Building sentences” objective: Understand that words combine to make sentences — a sentence expresses a complete thought; produce and expand complete sentences in speech and writing.
subject: English

label: Modal Verbs and Possibility
statement: Demonstrate the “Modal Verbs and Possibility” objective: Understand and use modal verbs (can, may, must, might, shall, will, could, should, would) and modal adverbs (perhaps, surely, certainly) to indicate degrees of possibility, necessity, and permission.
subject: English

label: Converting tenths to hundredths
statement: Demonstrate the “Converting tenths to hundredths” objective: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 and use this to add fractions with denominators 10 and 100 (e.g. 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100).
subject: Mathematics

label: The Rock Cycle
statement: Demonstrate the “The Rock Cycle” objective: Explain the rock cycle: how igneous rocks form from magma, sedimentary rocks from compressed sediment, and metamorphic rocks from heat and pressure, and how all rock types can transform into one another over geological time.
subject: Science

label: Honest Conversations and Conflict Repair
statement: Demonstrate the “Honest Conversations and Conflict Repair” objective: Understand how to have honest, direct conversations that address problems without attacking the person; apply the principles of non-violent communication (observation, feeling, need, request); understand the repair process after significant conflicts: taking responsibility without defensiveness, offering a genuine apology (without blame-shifting), and rebuilding trust through consistent behaviour over time; distinguish between a real apology and a face-saving 'sorry'; understand how friendships survive and deepen through navigated conflict rather than avoidance.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Simple Stories with Beginning and Ending
statement: Demonstrate the “Simple Stories with Beginning and Ending” objective: Write simple narratives by sequencing sentences to describe events in order; narrate a single event or linked events with a beginning, middle, and ending or reaction.
subject: English

label: Fractions of a whole
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions of a whole” objective: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a/b as a parts of size 1/b.
subject: Mathematics

label: Biodiversity
statement: Demonstrate the “Biodiversity” objective: Understand that biodiversity — the variety of different species in an ecosystem — is essential for healthy ecosystems, and that keystone species (like wolves in Yellowstone, sea otters in kelp forests, or bees as pollinators) have an outsized impact on their ecosystem, so that losing one key species can cause a cascade of changes affecting many others.
subject: Science

label: Irregular Plural Nouns
statement: Demonstrate the “Irregular Plural Nouns” objective: Form and use irregular plural nouns (e.g., children, teeth, mice, geese) in addition to regular plurals, recognising that some nouns have irregular plural forms that do not follow the -s/-es pattern.
subject: English

label: Culture and Experience Shape Emotions
statement: Demonstrate the “Culture and Experience Shape Emotions” objective: Understand that emotional responses are shaped by personal experiences, culture, and context — the same situation triggers different emotions in different people because of their backgrounds and past experiences.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Greek and Roman Legacy Today
statement: Demonstrate the “Greek and Roman Legacy Today” objective: Evaluate the lasting contributions of Greek and Roman civilisations to modern life — democracy, law, language (Latin roots), architecture (columns, arches, domes), sport (Olympics), philosophy, literature, and theatre — and understand that Greek ideas reached us through Rome, and then through later European civilisations, in a chain of cultural transmission.
subject: History

label: Explaining Events & Ideas
statement: Demonstrate the “Explaining Events & Ideas” objective: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in an informational text, including what happened and why, by citing specific textual evidence about causes, effects, and steps in a process.
subject: English

label: Rounding to 10, 100, 1000
statement: Demonstrate the “Rounding to 10, 100, 1000” objective: Round any number to the nearest 10, 100, or 1000.
subject: Mathematics

label: Patience and Delayed Gratification
statement: Demonstrate the “Patience and Delayed Gratification” objective: Wait for things they want without becoming very distressed — practising patience and delayed gratification in everyday situations like waiting their turn, waiting for a treat, or waiting for help.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Egypt and Its Neighbours
statement: Demonstrate the “Egypt and Its Neighbours” objective: Examine Egypt's relationships with neighbouring civilisations: trade networks reaching Nubia, the Levant, and Punt; the Hyksos invasion and the introduction of the chariot; and the New Kingdom empire and its conflict with the Hittites, culminating in the Battle of Kadesh and the world's earliest surviving peace treaty — understanding Egypt not as isolated but as part of a connected ancient world.
subject: History

label: Will the bulb light up?
statement: Demonstrate the “Will the bulb light up?” objective: Identify whether or not a lamp will light in a simple series circuit, based on whether the lamp is part of a complete loop with a battery.
subject: Science

label: Collecting Like Terms
statement: Demonstrate the “Collecting Like Terms” objective: Simplify algebraic expressions by collecting like terms — combine terms with the same variable and power (e.g., 3a + 2b + 5a = 8a + 2b) while maintaining equivalence.
subject: Mathematics

label: Comparing Design Solutions
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing Design Solutions” objective: Analyse data from tests of two objects designed to solve the same problem to compare the strengths and weaknesses of each design.
subject: Science

label: Fractions on a number line (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions on a number line (age 8+)” objective: Represent fractions on a number line: partition the interval 0 to 1 into b equal parts to locate 1/b, then mark off a lengths of 1/b from 0 to locate a/b.
subject: Mathematics

label: Dividing Quantities by Ratio
statement: Demonstrate the “Dividing Quantities by Ratio” objective: Divide a given quantity into two parts in a given part:part or part:whole ratio, and express the division as a fraction of the whole.
subject: Mathematics

label: Using New Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Using New Vocabulary” objective: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, being read to, and responding to texts in own speech and writing.
subject: English

label: Consistent verb tense
statement: Demonstrate the “Consistent verb tense” objective: Recognise and correct inappropriate shifts in verb tense within and across sentences and paragraphs, maintaining consistency unless a shift is required by meaning.
subject: English

label: Predator Loss and Ecosystem Effects
statement: Demonstrate the “Predator Loss and Ecosystem Effects” objective: Quantify energy transfer efficiency through trophic levels (~10% rule); explain trophic cascades: how removing an apex predator triggers a chain of ecosystem changes (sea otters → sea urchin explosion → kelp forest collapse); define 'fishing down the food web'; evaluate evidence for ocean rewilding — shark reintroduction, whale recovery driving nutrient cycling; understand why ecosystem-based fisheries management is needed.
subject: Science

label: Social Cues and Group Dynamics
statement: Demonstrate the “Social Cues and Group Dynamics” objective: Understand subtext, indirect communication, and social cues in adolescent peer groups; analyse the psychology of in-group and out-group dynamics and why belonging can come at the cost of exclusion; understand gossip as a social bonding and status mechanism, and its costs; develop strategies for navigating social hierarchies without compromising values; distinguish between assertiveness and aggression in peer settings; understand how to respond to exclusion — whether experiencing it or witnessing it.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Where water is found on Earth
statement: Demonstrate the “Where water is found on Earth” objective: Identify where water is found on Earth and understand that water can exist as solid (ice) or liquid, recognising water in oceans, rivers, glaciers, and underground.
subject: Science

label: 3-D shapes (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “3-D shapes (age 11+)” objective: Use the properties of faces, surfaces, edges, and vertices of 3-D shapes (cubes, cuboids, prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres) to solve problems, including visualising cross-sections.
subject: Mathematics

label: Vocabulary: working with others
statement: Demonstrate the “Vocabulary: working with others” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of working with others — cooperate, share, take turns, team, listen, agree, disagree respectfully, and include — and understand that these words describe habits that friendships and group work depend on.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Estimating volume
statement: Demonstrate the “Estimating volume” objective: Estimate volume of cuboids using 1 cm³ blocks; estimate capacity of containers using water.
subject: Mathematics

label: Measurable Attributes of Objects
statement: Demonstrate the “Measurable Attributes of Objects” objective: Describe and identify measurable attributes of objects such as length, height, weight, and capacity; use comparative language (longer, shorter, heavier, lighter, more, less).
subject: Mathematics

label: Estimating answers (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Estimating answers (age 10+)” objective: Find the volume of right rectangular prisms by packing with unit cubes and show it equals l × w × h (or base area × height); apply V = l × w × h and V = B × h to solve real-world problems; calculate, estimate, and compare volumes of cubes and cuboids in standard units (cm³, m³).
subject: Mathematics

label: Commas in lists
statement: Demonstrate the “Commas in lists” objective: Use commas to separate items in a list within a sentence (e.g., 'I bought apples, bananas, and oranges').
subject: English

label: Inside a Rainforest
statement: Demonstrate the “Inside a Rainforest” objective: Describe what it feels like inside a rainforest — hot and sticky (humid), dark on the ground because the treetops block the light, loud with animal calls and insect buzzing, and dripping with water from rain and condensation.
subject: Science

label: Measuring accurately
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring accurately” objective: Make systematic and careful observations, take accurate measurements using standard units and equipment including thermometers and data loggers.
subject: Science

label: Counting in 2s
statement: Demonstrate the “Counting in 2s” objective: Count in multiples of 2, 5, and 10 (skip counting).
subject: Mathematics

label: Why Earthquakes Happen
statement: Demonstrate the “Why Earthquakes Happen” objective: Understand that earthquakes happen when rocks underground suddenly move or break, releasing energy that shakes the ground.
subject: Science

label: The Five Senses
statement: Demonstrate the “The Five Senses” objective: Explore the five senses in detail: sight uses eyes to detect light, hearing uses ears to detect sound, touch uses skin to feel pressure and temperature, taste uses the tongue to detect flavours, and smell uses the nose to detect odours.
subject: Science

label: Types of Rock
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of Rock” objective: Know the three main types of rock — igneous (formed when lava or magma cools), sedimentary (formed from layers pressed together), and metamorphic — and that fossils are found in sedimentary rock.
subject: Science

label: Showing Your Working
statement: Demonstrate the “Showing Your Working” objective: Show and tell how a mathematical answer was found using objects, drawings, and spoken words.
subject: Mathematics

label: Drawing conclusions from evidence (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Drawing conclusions from evidence (age 9+)” objective: Report and present findings including conclusions, causal relationships, explanations, and a degree of trust in results using oral and written forms.
subject: Science

label: Seasonal changes (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Seasonal changes (age 8+)” objective: Represent data in tables and graphical displays to describe typical weather conditions expected during a particular season.
subject: Science

label: Sharing and Publishing Your Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Sharing and Publishing Your Writing” objective: Read own writing aloud clearly enough to be heard by peers and the teacher; use digital tools to produce and publish writing.
subject: English

label: Circuit vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Circuit vocabulary” objective: Use technical vocabulary for electrical circuits — circuit, component, cell, battery, current, voltage, resistance, conductor, insulator, switch, series circuit, parallel circuit — and apply these when describing, drawing, and designing working circuits.
subject: Science

label: Diet Imbalance & Deficiency
statement: Demonstrate the “Diet Imbalance & Deficiency” objective: Explain the health consequences of an imbalanced diet including obesity (excess energy), starvation (severe energy deficit), and deficiency diseases (lack of specific nutrients, e.g. scurvy, rickets).
subject: Science

label: Factor Pairs & Commutativity
statement: Demonstrate the “Factor Pairs & Commutativity” objective: Recognise and use factor pairs and commutativity in mental calculations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Drawing circuits with proper symbols
statement: Demonstrate the “Drawing circuits with proper symbols” objective: Use recognised symbols when representing a simple circuit in a diagram, including cell, wire, bulb, switch, buzzer, and motor.
subject: Science

label: Mixed numbers and improper fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Mixed numbers and improper fractions” objective: Recognise mixed numbers and improper fractions; convert from one form to the other (e.g. 2/5 + 4/5 = 6/5 = 1 1/5).
subject: Mathematics

label: Guided Multi-Step Problem Solving
statement: Demonstrate the “Guided Multi-Step Problem Solving” objective: With teacher guidance, make sense of multi-step and more complex problems by planning a pathway to the solution, identifying relevant information, and choosing appropriate operations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Spelling Word Lists (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Spelling Word Lists (age 7+)” objective: Spell words from the statutory word list for Years 3 and 4, including commonly misspelt words that do not follow regular patterns.
subject: English

label: Predicting Inherited Traits
statement: Demonstrate the “Predicting Inherited Traits” objective: Explain how alleles are inherited in sexual reproduction and use Punnett squares to predict the probability of offspring inheriting a characteristic, including dominant and recessive alleles.
subject: Science

label: Writing Process Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing Process Vocabulary” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of the writing process — compose, plan, draft, revise, edit, proofread, genre, audience, purpose, narrative, recount, instruction, paragraph, sequence, and detail — and understand that these words describe distinct steps and decisions that all writers make, not just tasks to tick off.
subject: English

label: Polar Bears
statement: Demonstrate the “Polar Bears” objective: Know key facts about polar bears — they live only in the Arctic (not the Antarctic), they have thick white fur and a layer of fat (blubber) to keep warm, they are excellent swimmers, and they hunt seals by waiting at holes in the sea ice.
subject: Science

label: What Is the Ocean?
statement: Demonstrate the “What Is the Ocean?” objective: Know that oceans are huge bodies of salt water that cover most of Earth's surface, and that the ocean is home to an enormous number of living things.
subject: Science

label: Humans Versus Machines
statement: Demonstrate the “Humans Versus Machines” objective: Comparing human and machine capabilities: creativity, empathy, common sense vs speed, memory, repetition; the Turing Test (simplified); what makes humans unique.
subject: Computing

label: Writing digits 0-9
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing digits 0-9” objective: Form digits 0-9 correctly and legibly.
subject: English

label: Food Chains & Energy Transfer
statement: Demonstrate the “Food Chains & Energy Transfer” objective: Construct and interpret food chains identifying producers, predators, and prey, and understand energy transfer between trophic levels.
subject: Science

label: Changing Your Mind with Evidence
statement: Demonstrate the “Changing Your Mind with Evidence” objective: Be willing to change your mind when evidence doesn't support your prediction — a result that surprises you is more valuable than one that confirms what you already thought.
subject: Science

label: Numbers on a number line
statement: Demonstrate the “Numbers on a number line” objective: Understand a coordinate system defined by two perpendicular number lines (axes) with an origin at (0,0); know that an ordered pair (x, y) specifies a unique point where the first number gives horizontal distance and the second gives vertical distance from the origin.
subject: Mathematics

label: Mental addition and subtraction (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Mental addition and subtraction (age 7+)” objective: Mentally add and subtract a three-digit number and ones.
subject: Mathematics

label: Simple Past, Present and Future
statement: Demonstrate the “Simple Past, Present and Future” objective: Form and use the simple past, present, and future verb tenses consistently in writing.
subject: English

label: Spaces Between Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Spaces Between Words” objective: Separate words with spaces in writing; understand that spaces mark word boundaries in print.
subject: English

label: Patterns and Classification
statement: Demonstrate the “Patterns and Classification” objective: Humans are great at spotting patterns; computers can learn to spot patterns too, but they need lots of examples; sorting and classification activities as the basis of machine learning.
subject: Computing

label: Alternative Spellings for Known Sounds
statement: Demonstrate the “Alternative Spellings for Known Sounds” objective: Recognise alternative grapheme-phoneme correspondences for known phonemes (e.g., /dʒ/ as ge/dge/g, /s/ as c, /n/ as kn/gn, /r/ as wr, /ʒ/ as s), reading words with less common spellings for familiar sounds.
subject: English

label: Dinosaurs Around the World
statement: Demonstrate the “Dinosaurs Around the World” objective: Understand that different dinosaurs lived on different continents and that fossil discoveries around the world show dinosaurs were a global phenomenon, with some species found only in certain regions.
subject: Science

label: Evidence for Evolution
statement: Demonstrate the “Evidence for Evolution” objective: Describe the main types of evidence for evolution: the fossil record (change over time), comparative anatomy (homologous structures), and the geographic distribution of related species.
subject: Science

label: Battle of Hastings and 1066
statement: Demonstrate the “Battle of Hastings and 1066” objective: The events of 1066: the death of Edward the Confessor, three claimants to the throne, the Battle of Hastings, William the Conqueror, and the Bayeux Tapestry as a historical source.
subject: History

label: What Astronauts Do
statement: Demonstrate the “What Astronauts Do” objective: Know that astronauts are people who travel to space in rockets, that humans have walked on the Moon (Apollo missions), and that astronauts today live and work on the International Space Station.
subject: Science

label: What the equals sign means
statement: Demonstrate the “What the equals sign means” objective: Understand the meaning of the equal sign as 'is the same as' and determine if equations are true or false.
subject: Mathematics

label: Similarities & Differences
statement: Demonstrate the “Similarities & Differences” objective: Notice and appreciate ways that people are similar to and different from each other — including appearance, family structures, languages spoken, foods eaten, and celebrations observed — and understand that differences make communities interesting.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Counting forwards and backwards (age 6+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Counting forwards and backwards (age 6+)” objective: Count forwards and backwards in tens from any number (not just multiples of 10).
subject: Mathematics

label: Neurons & Brain Structure
statement: Demonstrate the “Neurons & Brain Structure” objective: Explain how neurons transmit signals as electrochemical impulses across synapses, describe how the brain is organised (lobes and functions, limbic system for emotion), and explain neuroplasticity — why learning and practice physically change brain structure — connecting to optical illusions as evidence that the brain constructs reality rather than passively recording it.
subject: Science

label: Sorting & Categorising Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Sorting & Categorising Words” objective: Sort common objects and words into categories to understand how concepts relate; demonstrate understanding of opposites (antonyms) for common verbs and adjectives.
subject: English

label: Reading Ancient Climate Records
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading Ancient Climate Records” objective: Explain how ice cores preserve ancient air bubbles, isotope ratios, and volcanic markers allowing reconstruction of temperature and CO2 going back 800,000 years; describe tree rings, ocean sediment cores, coral skeletons, and pollen records as additional climate proxies; explain how climate models are built and validated against the palaeoclimate record; describe the IPCC process of synthesising scientific evidence across thousands of studies to produce consensus assessments.
subject: Science

label: Pictures and Text Working Together
statement: Demonstrate the “Pictures and Text Working Together” objective: Describe the relationship between illustrations and the text in which they appear; use pictures to support and extend comprehension.
subject: English

label: Animal Homes
statement: Demonstrate the “Animal Homes” objective: Know that animals make or find many different kinds of homes — birds build nests, rabbits dig burrows, bees live in hives, hermit crabs use empty shells, spiders spin webs — and that these shelters protect them and their young.
subject: Science

label: Universal Gravitation
statement: Demonstrate the “Universal Gravitation” objective: Describe gravity as a universal attractive force between all masses, explain that orbital motion arises because gravity provides the centripetal force keeping objects in orbit, and compare gravitational field strengths on different planets.
subject: Science

label: Why the author wrote it
statement: Demonstrate the “Why the author wrote it” objective: Distinguish one's own point of view from that of the author of an informational text and identify the author's purpose.
subject: English

label: Academic Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Academic Vocabulary” objective: Acquire and use accurately a broad range of general academic vocabulary and domain-specific words — drawing new vocabulary from reading and listening and deploying it consciously in writing and speech to achieve particular effects.
subject: English

label: Naming Major Bones
statement: Demonstrate the “Naming Major Bones” objective: Identify major bones of the human skeleton by name (skull, spine/vertebrae, ribcage, pelvis, femur, humerus) and explain the skeleton’s three jobs: supporting the body’s shape, protecting organs, and enabling movement with muscles.
subject: Science

label: Evaluating a Speaker's Argument
statement: Demonstrate the “Evaluating a Speaker's Argument” objective: Summarise the points a speaker makes and explain how each claim is supported by reasons and evidence, evaluating the logic and relevance of the support.
subject: English

label: What Is a Castle?
statement: Demonstrate the “What Is a Castle?” objective: What a castle is: a fortified building used as both a home and a defence; key parts including towers, moat, drawbridge, and thick walls; why castles were built.
subject: History

label: Ocean Food Webs
statement: Demonstrate the “Ocean Food Webs” objective: Understand ocean food webs: multiple interconnected food chains where energy flows from phytoplankton (producers) through zooplankton, small fish, and large predators, and that removing one species affects the whole web.
subject: Science

label: The insect body plan
statement: Demonstrate the “The insect body plan” objective: The insect body plan: all insects share three body parts (head, thorax, abdomen), six legs attached to the thorax, and antennae on the head. Most have wings. They have an exoskeleton — a hard outer shell — instead of bones inside.
subject: Science

label: Systemic Inequality and Allyship
