statement: Demonstrate the “Systemic Inequality and Allyship” objective: Move beyond 'treating everyone the same' to understand that structural advantages and disadvantages exist regardless of individual effort or intention; explore concrete examples of systemic inequality (educational attainment gaps, gender pay gap, representation in leadership); distinguish between individual prejudice and structural discrimination; understand intersectionality — how multiple aspects of identity interact; develop informed compassion rooted in evidence rather than pity; explore what being a genuine ally means in practice.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Angle Sum Rules
statement: Demonstrate the “Angle Sum Rules” objective: Know that angles at a point sum to 360° (one whole turn), angles on a straight line sum to 180°, and vertically opposite angles are equal; use these facts to find missing angles.
subject: Mathematics

label: Animal Life Stages
statement: Demonstrate the “Animal Life Stages” objective: Recognise that animals, including humans, have offspring which grow into adults, and describe basic animal life stages.
subject: Science

label: How Shadows Form
statement: Demonstrate the “How Shadows Form” objective: Recognise that shadows are formed when light from a source is blocked by an opaque object, and find patterns in how shadow size changes.
subject: Science

label: Human Life Stages
statement: Demonstrate the “Human Life Stages” objective: Describe the changes as humans develop to old age, including the stages of the human life cycle.
subject: Science

label: Deep-Sea Survival
statement: Demonstrate the “Deep-Sea Survival” objective: Explain how deep-sea animals cope with crushing pressure (no gas-filled spaces, flexible proteins, pressure-adapted enzymes); describe thermoregulation extremes — antifreeze glycoproteins in Antarctic fish, supercooling in wood frogs; introduce tardigrades and cryptobiosis (surviving desiccation, extreme temperatures, radiation, vacuum); survey other extremophiles (thermophiles at hydrothermal vents, halophiles in salt flats); consider what these organisms tell us about the limits of life.
subject: Science

label: Classifying Rainforest Organisms
statement: Demonstrate the “Classifying Rainforest Organisms” objective: Classify rainforest organisms into major groups — mammals (jaguars, monkeys, bats), birds (toucans, macaws, hummingbirds), reptiles (snakes, lizards, caimans), amphibians (tree frogs, poison dart frogs), insects (butterflies, ants, beetles), and plants (trees, epiphytes, ferns) — using observable features to sort them.
subject: Science

label: Reading Distance-Time Graphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading Distance-Time Graphs” objective: Read and plot distance-time graphs for moving objects; interpret the gradient (steepness) of a line as speed; identify stationary periods (horizontal sections), constant speed (straight diagonal lines), and relative speeds by comparing gradients; calculate average speed from the gradient of a straight-line segment using speed = distance ÷ time.
subject: Science

label: Structure of information texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Structure of information texts” objective: Describe the overall structure of an informational text (chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) and explain how the author's chosen structure helps convey information and ideas.
subject: English

label: Addition as combining or putting together two
statement: Demonstrate the “Addition as combining or putting together two” objective: Understand addition as combining or putting together two groups to find the total.
subject: Mathematics

label: Responding to Writing Feedback
statement: Demonstrate the “Responding to Writing Feedback” objective: With teacher guidance, re-read own writing aloud to check it sounds right; listen and respond to questions and suggestions from teacher or peers to add detail, clarify meaning, and strengthen writing — this is the scaffolded beginning of writing self-evaluation, not an independent skill.
subject: English

label: Insect anatomy in depth
statement: Demonstrate the “Insect anatomy in depth” objective: Insect anatomy in depth: compound eyes made of thousands of tiny lenses, spiracles (breathing holes along the body), diverse mouthparts (chewing mandibles in beetles, sucking proboscis in butterflies, sponging pad in flies), and moulting the exoskeleton to grow. Biomimicry — how engineers copy insect designs.
subject: Science

label: Estimating Lengths
statement: Demonstrate the “Estimating Lengths” objective: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimetres, and metres.
subject: Mathematics

label: Alternative Spellings for Sounds
statement: Demonstrate the “Alternative Spellings for Sounds” objective: Spell words using alternative grapheme choices for known phonemes, learning new spellings for sounds already encountered (e.g., /ɔ:/ as 'a' before ll, /ʌ/ as 'o', words ending -tion), including distinguishing common homophones.
subject: English

label: Identity and Belonging in Adolescence
statement: Demonstrate the “Identity and Belonging in Adolescence” objective: Understand that adolescence involves active construction of identity, leading to emotional complexity around questions of 'who am I?'; explore the emotional dynamics of belonging to multiple groups simultaneously (family, peer group, cultural or religious identity); understand social comparison and its intensification through social media; recognise that identity is not fixed and that uncertainty about identity is normal, not a sign of failure; develop language for navigating emotions tied to group membership and personal values.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Division with remainders
statement: Demonstrate the “Division with remainders” objective: Solve multi-step word problems using the four operations with whole numbers, including interpreting remainders in context; represent with equations using a letter for the unknown; check with estimation.
subject: Mathematics

label: Everyday Life in Ancient Egypt
statement: Demonstrate the “Everyday Life in Ancient Egypt” objective: Describe what everyday life was like for ordinary people in ancient Egypt: farmers grew wheat and barley near the Nile, families lived in mud-brick houses, children played games and had pets, and people ate bread, fish, fruit, and vegetables.
subject: History

label: Word Families and Root Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Word Families and Root Words” objective: Explore word families based on common root words, understanding how words are related in form and meaning through shared roots, prefixes and suffixes (e.g., solve → solution, solver, dissolve, insoluble).
subject: English

label: Converting Words into Verbs
statement: Demonstrate the “Converting Words into Verbs” objective: Convert nouns and adjectives into verbs by adding suffixes -ate, -ise (-ize), and -ify, understanding how word class changes affect sentence construction.
subject: English

label: Transparent, Translucent & Opaque
statement: Demonstrate the “Transparent, Translucent & Opaque” objective: Investigate the effect of placing objects made of different materials in the path of a beam of light, discovering transparent, translucent, and opaque materials.
subject: Science

label: Metric & Imperial Conversion
statement: Demonstrate the “Metric & Imperial Conversion” objective: Understand and use approximate equivalences between metric units and common imperial units (inches, pounds, pints).
subject: Mathematics

label: Representing numbers with objects
statement: Demonstrate the “Representing numbers with objects” objective: Represent numbers using objects, pictorial representations, and the number line.
subject: Mathematics

label: Sound Fading with Distance
statement: Demonstrate the “Sound Fading with Distance” objective: Recognise that sounds get fainter as the distance from the sound source increases.
subject: Science

label: Growth Mindset
statement: Demonstrate the “Growth Mindset” objective: Understand the concept of a growth mindset — that abilities and intelligence can grow with effort, practice, and good strategies — as opposed to a fixed mindset where you believe you're either good at something or you're not.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Pounds & Pence Notation
statement: Demonstrate the “Pounds & Pence Notation” objective: Recognise and use symbols for pounds (£) and pence (p) and combine amounts to make a particular value.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Pharaoh as Living God
statement: Demonstrate the “The Pharaoh as Living God” objective: Understand that the pharaoh was not just a ruler but was believed to be a living god — the intermediary between the gods and the people — and that the concept of Ma'at (truth, justice, and cosmic order) guided Egyptian law and government, with viziers and officials administering the kingdom on the pharaoh's behalf.
subject: History

label: Asking for Help
statement: Demonstrate the “Asking for Help” objective: Ask for help when they need it — from a friend, teacher, or family member — and understand that asking for help is a sign of strength, not weakness.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: How Parts Build a Whole Text
statement: Demonstrate the “How Parts Build a Whole Text” objective: Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fits together to provide the overall structure of a story, drama, or poem, analysing how each part contributes to the whole.
subject: English

label: Representing Addition and Subtraction
statement: Demonstrate the “Representing Addition and Subtraction” objective: Represent addition and subtraction using objects, drawings, and mental images.
subject: Mathematics

label: Waves & How They Move
statement: Demonstrate the “Waves & How They Move” objective: Develop a model of waves to describe patterns in terms of amplitude and wavelength, and understand that waves can cause objects to move.
subject: Science

label: Greek Myths and Heroes
statement: Demonstrate the “Greek Myths and Heroes” objective: Retell at least one Greek myth involving a hero and a monster — such as Theseus and the Minotaur in the labyrinth, Heracles (Hercules) and the lion, or Perseus and Medusa — and understand that these were stories ancient Greeks told to explain the world and teach lessons.
subject: History

label: Making a Simple Plan
statement: Demonstrate the “Making a Simple Plan” objective: Before starting a business, making a simple plan: what will I make or do, who will buy it, what do I need, how much will it cost, and what price will I charge?
subject: Life Skills

label: Reflection & Refraction
statement: Demonstrate the “Reflection & Refraction” objective: State the law of reflection (angle of incidence = angle of reflection) and explain refraction as the change in speed and direction when light crosses a boundary between two media; apply ray diagrams for plane mirrors and refracting surfaces.
subject: Science

label: Revising and editing (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Revising and editing (age 7+)” objective: Evaluate and edit writing by assessing effectiveness, proposing changes to grammar and vocabulary for consistency, and proof-reading for spelling, grammar and punctuation errors at Y3-4 level.
subject: English

label: Art & Architecture
statement: Demonstrate the “Art & Architecture” objective: Medieval cultural achievements: illuminated manuscripts, Gothic cathedrals (flying buttresses, stained glass), Gregorian chant, the Bayeux Tapestry; art and architecture as expressions of faith and power.
subject: History

label: Sun, Moon & Stars
statement: Demonstrate the “Sun, Moon & Stars” objective: Identify the Sun, Moon, and stars as objects in the sky and describe basic differences: the Sun gives light and heat during the day, stars are tiny points of light at night, and the Moon can appear in both the day and night sky.
subject: Science

label: The Brain Controls the Body
statement: Demonstrate the “The Brain Controls the Body” objective: Understand that the brain is the body’s control centre: it receives messages from the senses, thinks and makes decisions, and sends messages through nerves to tell muscles what to do.
subject: Science

label: Mental multiplication and division
statement: Demonstrate the “Mental multiplication and division” objective: Use place value, known and derived facts to multiply and divide mentally, including multiplying by 0 and 1, dividing by 1, and multiplying together three numbers.
subject: Mathematics

label: Saying Sentences Before Writing Them
statement: Demonstrate the “Saying Sentences Before Writing Them” objective: Say out loud what is going to be written; compose sentences orally before writing them down as preparation for independent writing.
subject: English

label: Heating & Cooling Changes
statement: Demonstrate the “Heating & Cooling Changes” objective: Observe and describe that some materials change state when heated or cooled, and measure the temperature at which changes occur in degrees Celsius.
subject: Science

label: Comparing fractions (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing fractions (age 10+)” objective: Compare and order fractions including fractions greater than 1, by converting to common denominators or using benchmarks.
subject: Mathematics

label: Calculating Percentages
statement: Demonstrate the “Calculating Percentages” objective: Solve problems involving the calculation of percentages of amounts (e.g. 15% of 360) and the use of percentages for comparison.
subject: Mathematics

label: Teamwork in Business
statement: Demonstrate the “Teamwork in Business” objective: Most businesses need more than one person; working together, dividing tasks, and using different people's strengths; the value of teamwork in business.
subject: Life Skills

label: Local Plants & Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Local Plants & Animals” objective: Identify and name a variety of plants and animals in their habitats, including microhabitats such as under a log or in a pond.
subject: Science

label: Rainforest Biodiversity
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Biodiversity” objective: Understand that rainforests are biodiversity hotspots — covering just 6% of Earth's land surface but containing over 50% of all known plant and animal species — and that this extraordinary richness makes them irreplaceable for global biodiversity and a priority for conservation.
subject: Science

label: Egyptian Maths and Engineering
statement: Demonstrate the “Egyptian Maths and Engineering” objective: Describe the Egyptian achievement in mathematics and engineering: the Rhind Mathematical Papyrus shows calculations of area, volume, and fractions; the precision of pyramid alignment (within 0.05° of true north) required sophisticated surveying; and Egyptian medical papyri describe detailed anatomical knowledge and pharmacological remedies — placing Egypt as a major contributor to the early history of science and technology.
subject: History

label: Addition and subtraction strategies
statement: Demonstrate the “Addition and subtraction strategies” objective: Use counting on and counting back as strategies for addition and subtraction.
subject: Mathematics

label: Temperature & Thermometers
statement: Demonstrate the “Temperature & Thermometers” objective: Understand temperature as how hot or cold something is, that a thermometer measures temperature, and use words like hot, warm, cool, and cold to describe how the air feels on different days.
subject: Science

label: Accurate Measurement
statement: Demonstrate the “Accurate Measurement” objective: Take measurements with increasing accuracy and precision using a range of scientific equipment, taking repeat readings when appropriate.
subject: Science

label: Fractions on a number line
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions on a number line” objective: Understand and use place value for decimals, measures, and integers of any size; extend the number system to include all positive and negative integers, decimals, and fractions on a single number line.
subject: Mathematics

label: Village Life
statement: Demonstrate the “Village Life” objective: Daily life for ordinary people in a medieval village: thatched houses, farming, baking bread, fetching water; how different life was from today.
subject: History

label: Ancient Egypt on the Timeline
statement: Demonstrate the “Ancient Egypt on the Timeline” objective: Place ancient Egypt on a timeline spanning over 3,000 years — from around 3100 BCE (unification under the first pharaoh) to 30 BCE (Roman conquest) — understanding that this civilisation lasted longer than the time between the Romans and today, and was divided into major periods: the Old Kingdom (pyramid age), Middle Kingdom, and New Kingdom (empire age).
subject: History

label: Growing Up & Puberty
statement: Demonstrate the “Growing Up & Puberty” objective: Describe the stages of human development from birth to old age: baby, toddler, child, adolescent (puberty), young adult, middle-aged adult, elderly — understanding the physical changes that happen at each stage, especially during puberty.
subject: Science

label: Onsets & Rimes
statement: Demonstrate the “Onsets & Rimes” objective: Blend and segment onsets and rimes in single-syllable words; isolate and pronounce individual phonemes (initial, medial, final) in CVC words; add or substitute phonemes to make new words.
subject: English

label: Animal Camouflage
statement: Demonstrate the “Animal Camouflage” objective: Know that many animals use camouflage — colours and patterns that help them blend into their surroundings — to hide from predators or to sneak up on prey, like a leaf insect that looks like a leaf or an Arctic hare that turns white in winter.
subject: Science

label: Protecting Endangered Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Protecting Endangered Animals” objective: Know how people work to protect endangered animals — through national parks and marine reserves, captive breeding programmes (like those that saved the California condor and Arabian oryx), anti-poaching patrols, wildlife corridors connecting habitats, and laws banning trade in endangered species — and understand that children can contribute through habitat-friendly choices.
subject: Science

label: Justifying mathematical reasoning
statement: Demonstrate the “Justifying mathematical reasoning” objective: Construct and follow multi-step mathematical arguments; identify errors in reasoning and explain why a method works or does not work.
subject: Mathematics

label: Energy from Food & the Sun
statement: Demonstrate the “Energy from Food & the Sun” objective: Use models to describe that energy in animals' food was once energy from the sun, transferred through plants or other organisms.
subject: Science

label: Multiplication as repeated addition
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiplication as repeated addition” objective: Understand multiplication as repeated addition and grouping equal sets.
subject: Mathematics

label: Speed & Distance-Time Graphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Speed & Distance-Time Graphs” objective: Calculate average speed using the equation speed = distance ÷ time, represent journeys on distance-time graphs, and interpret gradient as speed and flat sections as stationary periods.
subject: Science

label: Earth's rotation and day/night
statement: Demonstrate the “Earth's rotation and day/night” objective: Use the idea of the Earth's rotation to explain day and night and the apparent movement of the sun across the sky.
subject: Science

label: Punctuating Titles of Works
statement: Demonstrate the “Punctuating Titles of Works” objective: Use underlining, quotation marks, or italics to indicate titles of works, applying conventions for different types of works such as books, stories, poems, songs, and articles.
subject: English

label: Levers, Pulleys & Gears
statement: Demonstrate the “Levers, Pulleys & Gears” objective: Recognise that some mechanisms including levers, pulleys, and gears allow a smaller force to have a greater effect.
subject: Science

label: Everyday Safety Awareness
statement: Demonstrate the “Everyday Safety Awareness” objective: Keep themselves safe in everyday situations — knowing basic safety rules about roads, strangers, water, and the internet — and understanding who their trusted adults are and when to tell them something.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Choosing a Strategy
statement: Demonstrate the “Choosing a Strategy” objective: Before starting a study task, choose a deliberate strategy; after finishing, evaluate honestly whether that strategy actually helped.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Long multiplication
statement: Demonstrate the “Long multiplication” objective: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using formal written methods including long multiplication; illustrate with area models.
subject: Mathematics

label: Estimating by rounding
statement: Demonstrate the “Estimating by rounding” objective: Estimate the answer to a calculation and use inverse operations to check answers; apply to increasingly large numbers using rounding and inverse reasoning.
subject: Mathematics

label: Author's word choices
statement: Demonstrate the “Author's word choices” objective: Recognise how an author's deliberate choices — of words, structure, tone, and perspective — create particular effects on you as a reader.
subject: English

label: Addition in any order
statement: Demonstrate the “Addition in any order” objective: Understand and apply the commutative property of addition: addends can be added in any order.
subject: Mathematics

label: 3-D shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “3-D shapes” objective: Recognise and name common 3-D shapes (cubes, cuboids, pyramids, spheres, cylinders, cones).
subject: Mathematics

label: Research & Source Evaluation
statement: Demonstrate the “Research & Source Evaluation” objective: Summarise and organise material from reading and research — gathering relevant information from multiple sources, assessing credibility, integrating evidence without plagiarising, and supporting ideas with factual detail.
subject: English

label: Main Topic & Key Details
statement: Demonstrate the “Main Topic & Key Details” objective: Identify the main topic of a multi-paragraph informational text, determine the focus of specific paragraphs, and explain how key details support the main idea.
subject: English

label: Spelling Verb Endings
statement: Demonstrate the “Spelling Verb Endings” objective: Spell words with common suffixes (-s/-es for plurals and third person verbs, -ing, -ed, -er, -est) where no change to the root word is needed.
subject: English

label: Understanding angles (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding angles (age 10+)” objective: Recognise angles where they meet at a point, are on a straight line, or are vertically opposite; find missing angles using these properties.
subject: Mathematics

label: Social Enterprise
statement: Demonstrate the “Social Enterprise” objective: Using business skills to help others or solve social and environmental problems; making money AND making a difference; examples of social enterprises.
subject: Life Skills

label: Starting and Ending Sentences
statement: Demonstrate the “Starting and Ending Sentences” objective: Begin sentences with a capital letter and end them with the appropriate mark (full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark); recognise and name end punctuation.
subject: English

label: Positional Language
statement: Demonstrate the “Positional Language” objective: Describe the position of objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, next to.
subject: Mathematics

label: Fair testing
statement: Demonstrate the “Fair testing” objective: Set up simple practical enquiries, comparative tests, and fair tests, understanding the importance of changing only one variable at a time.
subject: Science

label: Minibeasts in the food chain
statement: Demonstrate the “Minibeasts in the food chain” objective: Minibeasts in the food chain: simple garden food chains. A caterpillar eats a leaf, a bird eats the caterpillar. The idea that minibeasts are food for other animals, and that minibeasts eat things too.
subject: Science

label: Solving Linear Equations
statement: Demonstrate the “Solving Linear Equations” objective: Use algebraic methods to solve linear equations in one variable, including equations that require rearrangement, expanding brackets, and collecting terms on both sides; solve equations with rational number coefficients.
subject: Mathematics

label: The K-Pg Extinction Event
statement: Demonstrate the “The K-Pg Extinction Event” objective: Describe the Cretaceous–Palaeogene (K-Pg) extinction event approximately 66 million years ago, including the asteroid impact theory and its evidence (iridium layer, Chicxulub crater), and understand that this ended the reign of non-avian dinosaurs.
subject: Science

label: Balanced Diet & Food Groups
statement: Demonstrate the “Balanced Diet & Food Groups” objective: Know the main food groups (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre, water) and understand that a balanced diet includes the right amounts from each group to keep the body healthy and provide energy, growth materials, and protection from illness.
subject: Science

label: How Organisms Shape Habitats
statement: Demonstrate the “How Organisms Shape Habitats” objective: Construct an argument supported by evidence for how plants and animals can change the environment to meet their needs.
subject: Science

label: Circulation & Breathing Together
statement: Demonstrate the “Circulation & Breathing Together” objective: Understand how the circulatory and respiratory systems work together: the lungs oxygenate the blood, the heart pumps it around the body, cells use the oxygen and produce carbon dioxide waste, and the blood carries the waste back to the lungs to be breathed out.
subject: Science

label: Evaporation & the Water Cycle
statement: Demonstrate the “Evaporation & the Water Cycle” objective: Identify the role of evaporation and condensation in the water cycle, and associate the rate of evaporation with temperature.
subject: Science

label: The Human Skeleton
statement: Demonstrate the “The Human Skeleton” objective: Describe the structure and four main functions of the human skeleton: support, protection, movement, and production of blood cells in bone marrow.
subject: Science

label: Acid Reactions & Salts
statement: Demonstrate the “Acid Reactions & Salts” objective: Describe and write word equations for the reactions of acids with metals, alkalis (neutralisation), and metal oxides/hydroxides, identifying the salt produced in each case.
subject: Science

label: Building with 3-D Shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Building with 3-D Shapes” objective: Compose three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, right circular cylinders) and create composite shapes; build new shapes from component shapes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Hyphens in Prefixed Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Hyphens in Prefixed Words” objective: Use hyphens to avoid ambiguity in compound modifiers and prefixed words, distinguishing between meanings that change based on hyphen placement.
subject: English

label: Place Value × 10 Pattern
statement: Demonstrate the “Place Value × 10 Pattern” objective: Recognise that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right (e.g. 700 ÷ 70 = 10).
subject: Mathematics

label: Planning a Task
statement: Demonstrate the “Planning a Task” objective: Make a simple plan before starting a task: what do I need to do, and what should I do first?
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Could there be another explanation?
statement: Demonstrate the “Could there be another explanation?” objective: For any result, ask: is there another explanation? — the first explanation that fits isn't always the right one, and good scientists actively look for alternatives.
subject: Science

label: Inside a Volcano
statement: Demonstrate the “Inside a Volcano” objective: Understand the inside of a volcano: magma is hot melted rock underground, lava is the same material after it reaches the surface, and volcanoes have a magma chamber, vent, and crater.
subject: Science

label: Rounding Answers
statement: Demonstrate the “Rounding Answers” objective: Solve problems which require answers to be rounded to specified degrees of accuracy.
subject: Mathematics

label: Degrees and turns
statement: Demonstrate the “Degrees and turns” objective: Know that angles are measured in degrees, where one degree is 1/360 of a full turn; understand that an angle turning through n one-degree angles has a measure of n degrees.
subject: Mathematics

label: Verb Prefixes and Meaning
statement: Demonstrate the “Verb Prefixes and Meaning” objective: Use verb prefixes (dis-, de-, mis-, over-, re-) to change verb meaning, understanding how each prefix modifies the action expressed by the root verb.
subject: English

label: Volcanoes & Mass Extinctions
statement: Demonstrate the “Volcanoes & Mass Extinctions” objective: Explain how large igneous provinces (LIPs) — massive outpourings of lava over millions of years — caused global warming and ocean acidification that drove mass extinctions; connect the Siberian Traps to the end-Permian extinction and the Deccan Traps to the end-Cretaceous event; explore how hydrothermal vents on the early Earth may have been the cradle of life; understand volcanoes as both destroyers and creators in the history of life.
subject: Science

label: Working Well in a Group
statement: Demonstrate the “Working Well in a Group” objective: Work effectively as part of a small group — contributing their own ideas, listening to others' ideas, taking on a fair share of the work, and supporting the group to reach a shared goal.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Persuasive Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Persuasive Writing” objective: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence — including introducing claims, acknowledging counterclaims, organising reasons logically, maintaining a formal style, and providing a concluding statement.
subject: English

label: Lines, Rays & Angles
statement: Demonstrate the “Lines, Rays & Angles” objective: Draw and identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines; identify these in two-dimensional figures.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Nervous System
statement: Demonstrate the “The Nervous System” objective: Understand that the nervous system has two parts — the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord) and nerves that branch throughout the body — and that nerve signals travel at high speed to coordinate senses, thought, and movement.
subject: Science

label: Budgeting Pocket Money
statement: Demonstrate the “Budgeting Pocket Money” objective: What a budget is; planning how to spend a fixed amount of pocket money or allowance; making trade-offs between different things you want to buy.
subject: Life Skills

label: White Light & Colour
statement: Demonstrate the “White Light & Colour” objective: Explain that white light is a mixture of all visible colours (ROYGBIV), describe dispersion through a prism, explain why objects appear coloured (selective reflection and absorption of wavelengths), and describe colour mixing with filters.
subject: Science

label: Light Travels in Straight Lines
statement: Demonstrate the “Light Travels in Straight Lines” objective: Recognise that light appears to travel in straight lines and use this to explain how we see objects and why shadows have the same shape as the objects that cast them.
subject: Science

label: Grammar Terms: Nouns, Verbs and Tense
statement: Demonstrate the “Grammar Terms: Nouns, Verbs and Tense” objective: Use and understand Year 2 grammatical terminology in discussion: noun, noun phrase, statement, question, exclamation, command, compound, suffix, adjective, adverb, verb, tense (past/present), apostrophe, comma.
subject: English

label: A Ten Is Ten Ones
statement: Demonstrate the “A Ten Is Ten Ones” objective: Understand that 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones — called a 'ten'.
subject: Mathematics

label: Financial Planning
statement: Demonstrate the “Financial Planning” objective: Setting longer-term financial goals; planning and prioritising spending; how saving regularly adds up over time; the value of thinking ahead with money.
subject: Life Skills

label: Medieval Clothing
statement: Demonstrate the “Medieval Clothing” objective: What people wore in medieval times: peasant clothes (wool, linen) vs noble clothes (silk, fur, bright colours); no zippers or buttons; how clothes showed your place in society.
subject: History

label: The multiples of 100
statement: Demonstrate the “The multiples of 100” objective: Understand that the multiples of 100 (100–900) each represent a number of hundreds with 0 tens and 0 ones.
subject: Mathematics

label: Coordinates (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Coordinates (age 10+)” objective: Describe positions on the full coordinate grid (all four quadrants); use coordinates with negative values.
subject: Mathematics

label: Insects in ecosystems
statement: Demonstrate the “Insects in ecosystems” objective: Insects in ecosystems: the many roles insects play. Pollinators (bees, butterflies, hoverflies), decomposers (dung beetles, fly larvae), food source for birds, bats, fish, and frogs, and pest controllers (ladybirds eating aphids). The thought experiment: what would happen if all insects disappeared?
subject: Science

label: Properties of materials
statement: Demonstrate the “Properties of materials” objective: Compare and group different kinds of rocks based on their appearance and simple physical properties such as hardness, texture, and colour.
subject: Science

label: The World of Minibeasts
statement: Demonstrate the “The World of Minibeasts” objective: Know that insects and other minibeasts (spiders, worms, snails, centipedes) are the most numerous and diverse group of animals on Earth — there are more species of beetle than any other animal — and that they play vital roles as pollinators (bees, butterflies), decomposers (woodlice, worms), and food for other animals.
subject: Science

label: Classifying shapes by line properties
statement: Demonstrate the “Classifying shapes by line properties” objective: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or angles of a specified size; recognise right triangles as a category.
subject: Mathematics

label: Representing numbers with objects (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Representing numbers with objects (age 8+)” objective: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set; solve one- and two-step comparison, sum, and difference problems using bar charts, pictograms, and tables.
subject: Mathematics

label: Irreversible Changes
statement: Demonstrate the “Irreversible Changes” objective: Explain that some changes result in the formation of new materials and are not usually reversible, such as burning, rusting, and reactions with acid.
subject: Science

label: Observing with Light Waves
statement: Demonstrate the “Observing with Light Waves” objective: Explain how the electromagnetic spectrum is the primary tool of modern astronomy — different wavelengths (radio, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma-ray) reveal different phenomena, why some telescopes must be in space, and what specific discoveries each wavelength range has enabled (e.g. CMB in microwave, black hole jets in X-ray, cold gas clouds in radio).
subject: Science

label: Dividing unit fractions and whole numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Dividing unit fractions and whole numbers” objective: Solve real-world problems involving division of unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions, using visual models and equations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Classifying living things (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Classifying living things (age 9+)” objective: Record data and results of increasing complexity using scientific diagrams, classification keys, tables, scatter graphs, bar and line graphs.
subject: Science

label: 3-D shapes (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “3-D shapes (age 10+)” objective: Recognise, describe, and build simple 3-D shapes, including making nets.
subject: Mathematics

label: Printing Press & Renaissance
statement: Demonstrate the “Printing Press & Renaissance” objective: The invention of the printing press by Gutenberg and its arrival in England with William Caxton; how printed books changed everything; the transition from the Middle Ages to the Renaissance.
subject: History

label: Finding efficient methods
statement: Demonstrate the “Finding efficient methods” objective: Notice when a calculation or pattern repeats and use this to count more efficiently or predict results.
subject: Mathematics

label: Goods & Services
statement: Demonstrate the “Goods & Services” objective: Some people make things (goods) and some people do things for others (services); recognising both in everyday life and understanding that both have value.
subject: Life Skills

label: Stop, Think, Then Choose
statement: Demonstrate the “Stop, Think, Then Choose” objective: Use a simple decision-making process when faced with a choice — stopping to think, identifying the options, considering the consequences of each option, and then choosing — rather than acting impulsively.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Determiners and articles
statement: Demonstrate the “Determiners and articles” objective: Use determiners (articles a/an/the and demonstratives this/that/these/those) correctly before nouns.
subject: English

label: Multi-Step Problem Solving
statement: Demonstrate the “Multi-Step Problem Solving” objective: With teacher support, make sense of multi-step problems involving larger numbers or mixed operations by breaking them into parts, choosing strategies, and checking answers for reasonableness — children at this stage are developing the habit with guidance; independent strategy evaluation comes later.
subject: Mathematics

label: Rules and agreements exist
statement: Demonstrate the “Rules and agreements exist” objective: Understand why rules and agreements exist — that they help keep people safe, make things fair, and help groups work well together — and follow agreed rules willingly rather than only when being watched.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Testing Push & Pull Designs
statement: Demonstrate the “Testing Push & Pull Designs” objective: Analyse data to determine if a design solution works as intended to change the speed or direction of an object with a push or pull.
subject: Science

label: Famous Eruptions & Pangaea
statement: Demonstrate the “Famous Eruptions & Pangaea” objective: Know about famous eruptions and their global effects: Mount St Helens (1980), Eyjafjallajökull (2010), and how large eruptions can affect weather and climate worldwide; understand that continents were once joined (Pangaea) and have slowly drifted apart.
subject: Science

label: Ethics in Real-World Issues
statement: Demonstrate the “Ethics in Real-World Issues” objective: Evaluate the ethical dimensions of real-world issues they encounter — such as environmental responsibility, fairness in sport, digital ethics, or social justice — considering multiple perspectives and forming a reasoned personal position.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Buying Things
statement: Demonstrate the “Buying Things” objective: How buying and selling works: prices, paying for items, receiving change; the basic transaction process in shops and markets.
subject: Life Skills

label: Trigraphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Trigraphs” objective: Read and spell words containing trigraphs — three-letter graphemes representing a single sound (igh, air, ear, are).
subject: English

label: Cancer & Stem Cells
statement: Demonstrate the “Cancer & Stem Cells” objective: Explain that cancer occurs when mutations in DNA disable normal cell-cycle controls, causing uncontrolled cell division and tumour formation; describe how stem cells differ from specialised cells and their potential for regenerative medicine; and evaluate the ethical debates around embryonic stem cell research and genetic testing.
subject: Science

label: Genetic Mutation
statement: Demonstrate the “Genetic Mutation” objective: Explain genetic mutation as a random change in DNA sequence, describe causes of mutation (e.g. radiation, chemicals, copying errors), and explain that most mutations are neutral, some harmful, and a few beneficial.
subject: Science

label: Your Impact on Others
statement: Demonstrate the “Your Impact on Others” objective: Reflect on how your behaviour lands on others — consider not just what you intended but what the actual impact was on the other person.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Self-Correcting While Reading
statement: Demonstrate the “Self-Correcting While Reading” objective: Check that text makes sense while reading and self-correct inaccurate reading by re-reading or using context.
subject: English

label: Inuit & Sami Peoples
statement: Demonstrate the “Inuit & Sami Peoples” objective: Know that indigenous peoples have lived in the Arctic for thousands of years — the Inuit across Canada, Alaska, and Greenland, and the Sami in northern Scandinavia — developing remarkable knowledge of the environment, using dog sleds and kayaks for transport, wearing animal-skin clothing for warmth, and building igloos as temporary shelters, with a deep respect for the animals and land they depend on.
subject: Science

label: Assertive Communication
statement: Demonstrate the “Assertive Communication” objective: Use assertive communication — expressing needs, opinions, and boundaries clearly and respectfully without being aggressive (pushy/demanding) or passive (giving in/staying silent) — including saying no when something doesn't feel right.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Choosing the Right Material
statement: Demonstrate the “Choosing the Right Material” objective: Identify and compare the suitability of everyday materials for particular uses, explaining why specific materials are chosen for specific purposes.
subject: Science

label: Having a Business Idea
statement: Demonstrate the “Having a Business Idea” objective: Where business ideas come from; spotting everyday problems and thinking of solutions; the difference between inventing something new and improving something that exists.
subject: Life Skills

label: The Digestive System
statement: Demonstrate the “The Digestive System” objective: Describe the simple functions of the basic parts of the human digestive system: mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine.
subject: Science

label: Measuring temperature
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring temperature” objective: Use negative numbers in context (temperature, finance, sea level); calculate intervals across zero.
subject: Mathematics

label: Numbers on a number line
statement: Demonstrate the “Numbers on a number line” objective: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from zero on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude in real-world contexts; distinguish absolute value comparisons from ordering statements.
subject: Mathematics

label: Sign Rules for Multiplication
statement: Demonstrate the “Sign Rules for Multiplication” objective: Multiply and divide with positive and negative integers and rational numbers, understanding the rules for the sign of the product or quotient.
subject: Mathematics

label: Real Entrepreneurs
statement: Demonstrate the “Real Entrepreneurs” objective: Stories of real entrepreneurs who started young: Mikaila Ulmer (Me & the Bees), Moziah Bridges (Mo's Bows), Cory Nieves (Mr. Cory's Cookies); what makes someone an entrepreneur.
subject: Life Skills

label: Multi-step problems: choosing operations
statement: Demonstrate the “Multi-step problems: choosing operations” objective: Solve problems involving addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, deciding which operations and methods to use and why; solve multi-step problems in contexts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Mild to Strong Emotions
statement: Demonstrate the “Mild to Strong Emotions” objective: Understand that emotions come in different intensities — from mild to strong — and that the same emotion can feel very different depending on how intense it is (e.g., annoyed → angry → furious, or nervous → anxious → panicked).
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Everyday Foods from Rainforests
statement: Demonstrate the “Everyday Foods from Rainforests” objective: Know that many everyday foods come from rainforests — chocolate is made from cacao beans, bananas grow in tropical forests, coffee berries ripen in forest shade, and Brazil nuts fall from giant trees — connecting our daily lives to faraway forests.
subject: Science

label: Expressing & Justifying Opinions
statement: Demonstrate the “Expressing & Justifying Opinions” objective: Articulate and justify answers, arguments, and opinions; participate in discussions, presentations, performances, role play, and debates.
subject: English

label: Standard English
statement: Demonstrate the “Standard English” objective: Know and understand the differences between spoken and written language — including differences in formality, register, grammar, and vocabulary — and between Standard English and other varieties of English, using Standard English confidently in writing and speech.
subject: English

label: Number bonds
statement: Demonstrate the “Number bonds” objective: Recall number bonds (addition and related subtraction facts) within 20.
subject: Mathematics

label: Supporting ideas with evidence
statement: Demonstrate the “Supporting ideas with evidence” objective: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which specific points.
subject: English

label: Persisting When It's Hard
statement: Demonstrate the “Persisting When It's Hard” objective: Keep trying when something feels hard — making mistakes and trying again is how learning happens.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Writing Techniques for Effect
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing Techniques for Effect” objective: Apply growing knowledge of vocabulary, grammar, and text structure to writing — drawing on literary and rhetorical devices from reading (e.g., rhetorical questions, tricolon, anaphora, contrast) to enhance impact.
subject: English

label: Correlative Conjunctions
statement: Demonstrate the “Correlative Conjunctions” objective: Use correlative conjunctions correctly in sentences, pairing words such as either/or, neither/nor, both/and, not only/but also, and whether/or.
subject: English

label: Different Lives and Experiences
statement: Demonstrate the “Different Lives and Experiences” objective: Understand that people's lives and experiences can be very different from their own — that some children face challenges like disability, poverty, family difficulties, or being new to a country — and develop compassion rather than judgement.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: What Is a Volcano
statement: Demonstrate the “What Is a Volcano” objective: Know what a volcano is: an opening in Earth's surface where hot melted rock (lava) comes out.
subject: Science

label: Using Weather Instruments
statement: Demonstrate the “Using Weather Instruments” objective: Use weather instruments to measure and record weather data: thermometers for temperature in °C, rain gauges for rainfall, wind vanes for direction, and anemometers for wind speed — and keep a weather diary over time.
subject: Science

label: Decimals to three places
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimals to three places” objective: Solve problems involving numbers with up to three decimal places.
subject: Mathematics

label: Living, Dead & Never Alive
statement: Demonstrate the “Living, Dead & Never Alive” objective: Explore and compare the differences between things that are living, dead, and things that have never been alive.
subject: Science

label: Using a Thesaurus to Choose Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Using a Thesaurus to Choose Words” objective: Use a thesaurus to find synonyms and extend vocabulary choices, selecting the most appropriate word based on context, connotation, and register.
subject: English

label: 2-D shapes (age 6+)
statement: Demonstrate the “2-D shapes (age 6+)” objective: Identify and describe properties of 2-D shapes including the number of sides and line symmetry in a vertical line.
subject: Mathematics

label: Buyers & Sellers
statement: Demonstrate the “Buyers & Sellers” objective: When someone makes or has something, they can sell it; when someone wants something, they can buy it; introduction to the concept of exchange and transactions.
subject: Life Skills

label: Decimals and fractions (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimals and fractions (age 11+)” objective: Work interchangeably with terminating decimals and their corresponding fractions (such as 3.5 and 7/2 or 0.375 and 3/8); convert fluently between the two forms.
subject: Mathematics

label: Metals vs Non-Metals
statement: Demonstrate the “Metals vs Non-Metals” objective: Compare the physical and chemical properties of metals and non-metals, explaining metallic properties (malleability, lustre, conductivity) and how position in the periodic table predicts reactivity.
subject: Science

label: Ice & States of Matter
statement: Demonstrate the “Ice & States of Matter” objective: Understand ice in different forms and states of matter — sea ice forms when ocean water freezes (it's salty and relatively thin), glacial ice forms from compacted snow over centuries (fresh water, very thick), and icebergs break off from glaciers and float in the sea; know that water exists as solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (water vapour), and that salt lowers the freezing point of water.
subject: Science

label: Reading for Meaning
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading for Meaning” objective: Understand that reading is about making meaning, not just saying words correctly — a text that can be decoded but not understood has not been read.
subject: English

label: Bones & Muscles
statement: Demonstrate the “Bones & Muscles” objective: Know that the body has a skeleton made of bones inside it that gives the body its shape and protects important organs like the brain (skull) and heart (ribcage), and that muscles attached to bones allow the body to move.
subject: Science

label: Literary Evidence in Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Literary Evidence in Writing” objective: Draw evidence from literary texts to support analysis, reflection, and research in writing, applying grade-level reading standards to literature.
subject: English

label: Nutrients in a Healthy Diet
statement: Demonstrate the “Nutrients in a Healthy Diet” objective: Identify the seven components of a healthy diet — carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, vitamins, minerals, dietary fibre, and water — and explain the role of each in the body.
subject: Science

label: Words for Big Feelings
statement: Demonstrate the “Words for Big Feelings” objective: Know and use the key words for managing big feelings — calm, strategy, cope, settle, patience, overwhelmed, and breathe — and understand that having words for these ideas is the first step to using them.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Wave Behaviour Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Wave Behaviour Vocabulary” objective: Use technical vocabulary for wave behaviour — refraction, absorption, reflection, scattering, amplitude, frequency, wavelength, echo, spectrum, angle of incidence, angle of reflection — and apply these when explaining how light and sound travel and interact with different materials.
subject: Science

label: Transformations on a grid
statement: Demonstrate the “Transformations on a grid” objective: Represent and carry out geometric transformations on squared paper or a coordinate grid: reflections (in horizontal, vertical, and diagonal mirror lines, including the axes), translations (described as a vector or as left/right/up/down moves), and rotations (90° or 180° about a stated centre point); describe each transformation precisely using the correct language; identify which transformation maps one shape onto its image by comparing position, orientation, and size.
subject: Mathematics

label: Types of Metamorphosis
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of Metamorphosis” objective: Complete vs incomplete metamorphosis. Complete: egg → larva → pupa → adult (butterflies, beetles, flies). Incomplete: egg → nymph → adult — the nymph looks like a small version of the adult and moults as it grows (grasshoppers, dragonflies, crickets). Why do some insects transform completely while others grow gradually?
subject: Science

label: Experimental probability
statement: Demonstrate the “Experimental probability” objective: Record, describe, and analyse the frequency of outcomes from probability experiments to develop an understanding of relative frequency as an estimate of probability.
subject: Mathematics

label: Spelling Word Lists (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Spelling Word Lists (age 9+)” objective: Spell words from the statutory word list for Years 5 and 6, including words with irregular or uncommon spelling patterns that must be learned individually.
subject: English

label: Measuring length
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring length” objective: Order three objects by length and compare the lengths of two objects indirectly using a third object.
subject: Mathematics

label: Main Ideas & Note-Taking
statement: Demonstrate the “Main Ideas & Note-Taking” objective: Identify main ideas drawn from more than one paragraph and summarise them; retrieve and record information from non-fiction texts using notes, tables or other methods.
subject: English

label: Multi-Step Problem Solving
statement: Demonstrate the “Multi-Step Problem Solving” objective: Make sense of multi-step problems involving four operations, fractions, and area/volume by identifying sub-steps, choosing a strategy, and monitoring progress.
subject: Mathematics

label: Plotting points in the first quadrant
statement: Demonstrate the “Plotting points in the first quadrant” objective: Plot and read ordered pairs in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane; represent real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points and interpreting coordinate values in context.
subject: Mathematics

label: Decimal place value
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimal place value” objective: Multiply one-digit numbers with up to two decimal places by whole numbers (e.g. 3.47 × 6).
subject: Mathematics

label: Measurement Conversions
statement: Demonstrate the “Measurement Conversions” objective: Solve problems involving the calculation and conversion of units of measure, using decimal notation and multi-step reasoning in real-world contexts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Ocean Depth Zones
statement: Demonstrate the “Ocean Depth Zones” objective: Understand that the ocean has different zones depending on depth and light: the sunlight zone near the surface where most life lives, the twilight zone where light fades, and the midnight zone of total darkness.
subject: Science

label: Ice & Snow
statement: Demonstrate the “Ice & Snow” objective: Know that water can be solid (ice and snow) or liquid, that snow is made of tiny frozen ice crystals, that icebergs are huge chunks of ice floating in the ocean with most of their bulk hidden underwater, and that ice floats because it is lighter than liquid water.
subject: Science

label: Adding and subtracting (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding and subtracting (age 7+)” objective: Add and subtract numbers with up to three digits using formal written methods of columnar addition and subtraction.
subject: Mathematics

label: Comparing fractions (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing fractions (age 7+)” objective: Solve problems involving counting in tenths, fractions of quantities, equivalence, fraction addition/subtraction, and fraction comparison.
subject: Mathematics

label: Characters, settings, and events
statement: Demonstrate the “Characters, settings, and events” objective: Identify characters, settings, and major events in stories; become familiar with key stories, fairy tales, and traditional tales and retell them with key details in sequence.
subject: English

label: What Money Is
statement: Demonstrate the “What Money Is” objective: What money is and why we use it; that money is exchanged for goods and services; brief history from barter to coins to digital payments.
subject: Life Skills

label: Literal vs Figurative Language
statement: Demonstrate the “Literal vs Figurative Language” objective: Distinguish literal from nonliteral (figurative) language in context and interpret common idioms and phrases.
subject: English

label: Mass vs Weight
statement: Demonstrate the “Mass vs Weight” objective: Distinguish between mass (amount of matter, measured in kg) and weight (gravitational force, measured in N), use the equation weight = mass × gravitational field strength, and explain why g differs on other planets and stars.
subject: Science

label: Comparing Books
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing Books” objective: Make comparisons within and across books, identifying similarities and differences in themes, characters, settings, and authorial choices across multiple texts.
subject: English

label: Circles: Circumference & Area
statement: Demonstrate the “Circles: Circumference & Area” objective: Calculate the circumference and area of circles using the formulae C = πd (or 2πr) and A = πr², and solve problems involving perimeters and areas of composite shapes that include circular parts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Grouping Materials
statement: Demonstrate the “Grouping Materials” objective: Compare and group everyday materials based on their simple physical properties.
subject: Science

label: Comparing fractions (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing fractions (age 9+)” objective: Compare and order fractions with different numerators and denominators by creating common denominators/numerators or comparing to a benchmark such as 1/2; justify conclusions with visual models.
subject: Mathematics

label: Engaging Listeners and Valuing Viewpoints
statement: Demonstrate the “Engaging Listeners and Valuing Viewpoints” objective: Gain, maintain and monitor the interest of listeners when speaking; consider and evaluate different viewpoints, attending to and building on others' contributions; begin to select appropriate language for different situations.
subject: English

label: One More Each Time
statement: Demonstrate the “One More Each Time” objective: Each successive counting number represents a quantity that is one larger than the previous number.
subject: Mathematics

label: Bees and pollination
statement: Demonstrate the “Bees and pollination” objective: Bees and pollination: how flowers and insects depend on each other. Bees visit flowers for nectar, pollen sticks to their bodies and transfers to the next flower. Without pollination many plants cannot make seeds or fruit. Why bees matter for the food we eat.
subject: Science

label: Vocabulary: ancient egypt
statement: Demonstrate the “Vocabulary: ancient egypt” objective: Know and use the key vocabulary of ancient Egypt — pharaoh, pyramid, tomb, mummy/mummification, hieroglyphs, papyrus, sarcophagus, canopic jar, natron, archaeologist, artefact, Nile, delta, irrigation, shaduf, scribe, vizier, obelisk, sphinx, cartouche — and apply these terms accurately when describing Egyptian society, religion, and material culture.
subject: History

label: Pronouns
statement: Demonstrate the “Pronouns” objective: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns correctly (e.g., I/me/my, they/them/their, anyone/everything), replacing nouns to avoid repetition.
subject: English

label: Text & Media Connections
statement: Demonstrate the “Text & Media Connections” objective: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of the text, identifying where each version reflects specific descriptions and directions from the text.
subject: English

label: The 0-to-1 Probability Scale
statement: Demonstrate the “The 0-to-1 Probability Scale” objective: Understand probability as a measure expressed as a number between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain); place events on the probability scale; express probabilities as fractions, decimals, and percentages.
subject: Mathematics

label: Reading Contractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading Contractions” objective: Read and understand contractions with apostrophes, knowing the apostrophe represents omitted letters.
subject: English

label: Prefixes (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Prefixes (age 7+)” objective: Spell words with a range of prefixes (dis-, mis-, un-, re-, pre-, anti-, auto-, super-) understanding how each prefix modifies the root word's meaning without changing its spelling.
subject: English

label: Grouping numbers to add
statement: Demonstrate the “Grouping numbers to add” objective: Understand and apply the associative property of addition: when adding three numbers, any two can be added first.
subject: Mathematics

label: Birds Evolved from Dinosaurs
statement: Demonstrate the “Birds Evolved from Dinosaurs” objective: Understand that modern birds evolved from a group of small feathered theropod dinosaurs, using evidence such as the fossil Archaeopteryx, feathered dinosaur fossils from China, and shared skeletal features.
subject: Science

label: Types of Sentences
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of Sentences” objective: Choose among and construct simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences to signal different relationships among ideas, varying sentence patterns deliberately for meaning, interest, and style.
subject: English

label: Angles in triangles (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Angles in triangles (age 11+)” objective: Derive and apply formulae for the area of triangles, parallelograms, and trapezia, and for the volume of cuboids and other prisms (including cylinders), connecting each formula to its geometric reasoning.
subject: Mathematics

label: Counting forwards and backwards (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Counting forwards and backwards (age 9+)” objective: Count forwards and backwards in steps of powers of 10 (10, 100, 1000, 10,000, 100,000) for any given number up to 1,000,000.
subject: Mathematics

label: Comparing durations
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing durations” objective: Use comparative language for time: quicker, slower, earlier, later.
subject: Mathematics

label: Learning from Mistakes
statement: Demonstrate the “Learning from Mistakes” objective: When you get something wrong, investigate why — what did you misunderstand or overlook? Analysing errors is one of the most powerful ways to learn.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Position, direction, and movement
statement: Demonstrate the “Position, direction, and movement” objective: Use mathematical vocabulary to describe position, direction, and movement, including straight lines and distinguishing rotation as a turn in terms of right angles (quarter, half, three-quarter turns, clockwise and anti-clockwise).
subject: Mathematics

label: Ocean Animal Migrations
statement: Demonstrate the “Ocean Animal Migrations” objective: Know that many ocean animals undertake remarkable migrations — humpback whales travel thousands of miles between feeding and breeding grounds, sea turtles return to the same beach where they hatched to lay eggs — and understand these journeys are linked to seasonal food supplies and reproduction.
subject: Science

label: Understanding angles (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding angles (age 11+)” objective: Apply the properties of angles at a point (360°), on a straight line (180°), and vertically opposite angles to find unknown angles in multi-step problems.
subject: Mathematics

label: Grammar words: letter, word, sentence
statement: Demonstrate the “Grammar words: letter, word, sentence” objective: Use basic grammatical terminology when discussing reading and writing: letter, capital letter, word, singular, plural, sentence, punctuation, full stop, question mark, exclamation mark.
subject: English

label: Multiplying fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiplying fractions” objective: Understand a/b as a multiple of 1/b; multiply proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers, supported by visual models (e.g. 3 × 2/5 = 6/5 = 1 1/5).
subject: Mathematics

label: Megafauna Extinction & De-Extinction
statement: Demonstrate the “Megafauna Extinction & De-Extinction” objective: Evaluate the debate over what drove Pleistocene megafauna to extinction — human overkill, climate change, or a combination — using evidence from fossil records, ancient DNA, and archaeological sites; connect to the present-day sixth mass extinction and consider the ethics and feasibility of de-extinction using ancient DNA.
subject: Science

label: The two digits of a two-digit number
statement: Demonstrate the “The two digits of a two-digit number” objective: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones.
subject: Mathematics

label: Discussing Texts as a Group
statement: Demonstrate the “Discussing Texts as a Group” objective: Participate in discussions about what is read, taking turns and listening to others; explain understanding clearly; actively engage in group reading activities.
subject: English

label: Writing Science Reports
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing Science Reports” objective: Communicate scientific findings in a structured report using appropriate scientific vocabulary, SI units, and standard notation; describe how peer review and replication contribute to the reliability of scientific knowledge.
subject: Science

label: Suffixes (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Suffixes (age 7+)” objective: Spell words using productive suffixes (-ation, -ly, -ous) and less common sound-spelling correspondences (/ɪ/ as y, /ʌ/ as ou, endings sounding like /ʒə/, /tʃə/, /ʒən/, /ʃən/) introduced in the Year 3-4 programme.
subject: English

label: Understanding drama and performance
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding drama and performance” objective: Understand how dramatists communicate meaning through performance — including staging, direction, set design, lighting, and actors' choices — and how different productions can interpret the same script differently.
subject: English

label: How Breathing Works
statement: Demonstrate the “How Breathing Works” objective: Know that we breathe air into our lungs through the nose and mouth, that our lungs take in oxygen from the air which our body needs to stay alive, and that we breathe out carbon dioxide as waste.
subject: Science

label: Adding numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding numbers” objective: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Anaerobic Respiration
statement: Demonstrate the “Anaerobic Respiration” objective: Explain anaerobic respiration in animals as the incomplete breakdown of glucose to lactic acid when oxygen is in short supply, causing muscle fatigue; contrast this with aerobic respiration in terms of energy yield and products.
subject: Science

label: Scale of the Solar System
statement: Demonstrate the “Scale of the Solar System” objective: Use scale models, diagrams, or calculations to represent the relative sizes and distances of objects in the solar system, understanding that the distances between planets are enormously larger than the planets themselves.
subject: Science

label: Rain & Puddles
statement: Demonstrate the “Rain & Puddles” objective: Know that rain falls from clouds in the sky, that puddles disappear because water goes back into the air, and that this is part of how water moves around — up into the sky and back down again.
subject: Science

label: Traits: inherited and environmental
statement: Demonstrate the “Traits: inherited and environmental” objective: Use evidence to support the explanation that traits can be influenced by the environment as well as inheritance.
subject: Science

label: Shadows
statement: Demonstrate the “Shadows” objective: Represent data in graphical displays to reveal patterns of daily changes in shadow length and direction, day and night cycles, and seasonal star patterns.
subject: Science

label: Precise Maths Communication
statement: Demonstrate the “Precise Maths Communication” objective: Communicate with mathematical precision: use correct vocabulary, specify units, and use symbols accurately.
subject: Mathematics

label: Climate Zones
statement: Demonstrate the “Climate Zones” objective: Understand that Earth has distinct climate zones — tropical (hot and wet near the equator), temperate (moderate, with four seasons), polar (freezing cold), arid/desert (very dry), and mountain (cold at high altitude) — and that each zone supports different ecosystems and ways of life.
subject: Science

label: Cohesion and Transitions Across Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Cohesion and Transitions Across Writing” objective: Use varied transitions, cohesive devices, and paragraph-linking strategies to create coherence across a whole piece of writing — including temporal transitions, causal connectives, and techniques for signalling shifts in argument, time, or setting.
subject: English

label: Roman numerals to 1000
statement: Demonstrate the “Roman numerals to 1000” objective: Read Roman numerals to 1000 (M) and recognise years written in Roman numerals.
subject: Mathematics

label: Unit Conversions
statement: Demonstrate the “Unit Conversions” objective: Convert freely between related standard units of measurement (time, length, area, volume/capacity, mass) using decimal notation to up to three decimal places where appropriate.
subject: Mathematics

label: Decimal equivalents of tenths and hundredths
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimal equivalents of tenths and hundredths” objective: Recognise and write decimal equivalents of any number of tenths or hundredths (e.g. 3/10 = 0.3, 27/100 = 0.27).
subject: Mathematics

label: Supply Chains
statement: Demonstrate the “Supply Chains” objective: Where products come from before they reach the customer; raw materials, making, transporting, and selling; the journey of a product from start to finish.
subject: Life Skills

label: Human Reproduction
statement: Demonstrate the “Human Reproduction” objective: Describe the structure and function of the male and female human reproductive systems, and explain the processes of fertilisation, gestation, and birth including the role of the placenta.
subject: Science

label: Heart Structure & Double Circulation
statement: Demonstrate the “Heart Structure & Double Circulation” objective: Describe the structure of the heart (four chambers, valves, coronary arteries) and explain how it pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs and oxygenated blood to the body in a double circulatory system.
subject: Science

label: Questioning Historical Sources
statement: Demonstrate the “Questioning Historical Sources” objective: Before trusting a historical source, ask: who made this, when, and why? — the answers shape how much weight the source should carry.
subject: History

label: Feelings Versus Actions
statement: Demonstrate the “Feelings Versus Actions” objective: Understand that feelings and actions are separate — you can feel something strongly without having to act on it straight away.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Themes Across Cultures and Traditions
statement: Demonstrate the “Themes Across Cultures and Traditions” objective: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes, topics, and story patterns (e.g., good vs evil, quest narratives, trickster tales) in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.
subject: English

label: Newton's First & Second Laws
statement: Demonstrate the “Newton's First & Second Laws” objective: State and apply Newton's First Law (an object stays at rest or constant velocity unless acted on by a resultant force) and Second Law (force = mass × acceleration), including the relationship between mass, force, and acceleration.
subject: Science

label: Deepfakes and AI-Generated Content
statement: Demonstrate the “Deepfakes and AI-Generated Content” objective: Deepfakes, AI-generated images and text; how to spot them and why they matter; the importance of checking sources; not everything online is real.
subject: Computing

label: Reviewing Own Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Reviewing Own Writing” objective: Evaluate whether your own writing achieves the effect you intended on a reader — go beyond checking for correctness to asking whether it actually works.
subject: English

label: Advanced Spelling Conventions
statement: Demonstrate the “Advanced Spelling Conventions” objective: Spell words using assorted Y5-6 conventions: doubling after -fer when the stress remains (referring but reference), using hyphens to join prefixes to root words (co-ordinate, re-enter), the /iː/ sound spelt ei after c (receive, ceiling), and the letter string ough representing different sounds (though, through, thought, thorough, plough).
subject: English

label: Separating Mixtures
statement: Demonstrate the “Separating Mixtures” objective: Select and carry out appropriate separation techniques for different types of mixtures: filtration (insoluble solids), distillation (liquids by boiling point), crystallisation (dissolved solids), and chromatography (coloured substances).
subject: Science

label: Dinosaur Sizes
statement: Demonstrate the “Dinosaur Sizes” objective: Compare dinosaur sizes to familiar things — some dinosaurs were as tall as a house, others were as small as a chicken — and understand that dinosaurs came in a huge range of sizes.
subject: Science

label: Comparing and ordering numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing and ordering numbers” objective: Compare and order two-digit numbers using the symbols >, =, and <, based on place value understanding.
subject: Mathematics

label: Four Types of Sentences
statement: Demonstrate the “Four Types of Sentences” objective: Understand and use the four sentence types — statement, question, exclamation, and command — recognising how grammatical patterns indicate sentence function.
subject: English

label: Parallel and perpendicular lines
statement: Demonstrate the “Parallel and perpendicular lines” objective: Identify horizontal and vertical lines and pairs of perpendicular and parallel lines.
subject: Mathematics

label: Homophones (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Homophones (age 9+)” objective: Distinguish and correctly spell homophones and commonly confused words at Y5-6 level (e.g., affect/effect, practice/practise, advice/advise, complement/compliment, aisle/isle, led/lead), including confused words such as to/too/two and there/their/they're.
subject: English

label: The Sun is a star
statement: Demonstrate the “The Sun is a star” objective: Know that the Sun is a star — the closest star to Earth — and that it is at the centre of our solar system, with all eight planets orbiting around it.
subject: Science

label: Multiplicative Comparison
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiplicative Comparison” objective: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison (e.g. 35 = 5 × 7 means 35 is 5 times as many as 7); represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as equations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Pictograms and tally charts (age 6+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Pictograms and tally charts (age 6+)” objective: Read, write, and use the vocabulary of data collection and display — data, tally, tally chart, frequency, frequency table, survey, pictogram, bar chart, axis/axes, scale, label, category, discrete data, continuous data, line graph, pie chart — and apply these terms when collecting, organising, and presenting data.
subject: Mathematics

label: Voice Assistants and How They Work
statement: Demonstrate the “Voice Assistants and How They Work” objective: What happens when you talk to Alexa, Siri, or Google Assistant; they listen, try to understand, look up answers; sometimes they get it wrong; they are tools, not alive.
subject: Computing

label: Subject-verb agreement
statement: Demonstrate the “Subject-verb agreement” objective: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in sentences, maintaining subject-verb agreement (e.g., 'He hops' vs 'We hop').
subject: English

label: Decimal place value (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimal place value (age 11+)” objective: Round numbers and measures to an appropriate degree of accuracy including to a specified number of decimal places or significant figures.
subject: Mathematics

label: Ordering Likelihoods
statement: Demonstrate the “Ordering Likelihoods” objective: Compare the likelihood of different events and order them from least to most likely — including situations with unequal outcomes such as a bag with more of one colour than another, or a spinner with sections of different sizes — and explain reasoning using informal language.
subject: Mathematics

label: How the Economy Works
statement: Demonstrate the “How the Economy Works” objective: What an economy is; producers and consumers; supply and demand; why prices change; the basics of how markets work.
subject: Life Skills

label: Fractions on a number line (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Fractions on a number line (age 11+)” objective: Order positive and negative integers, decimals, and fractions on a number line; use the symbols =, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥ to compare values including negative numbers and mixed representations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Root Words & Inflections
statement: Demonstrate the “Root Words & Inflections” objective: Identify frequently occurring root words and their inflectional forms (e.g., look/looks/looked/looking), using affixes as clues to word meaning and understanding how suffixes create nouns and adjectives.
subject: English

label: Factorising Expressions
statement: Demonstrate the “Factorising Expressions” objective: Factorise algebraic expressions by taking out common factors — identify the highest common factor of all terms and write the expression as a product, e.g., 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3).
subject: Mathematics

label: Spotting mathematical patterns
statement: Demonstrate the “Spotting mathematical patterns” objective: Notice simple patterns and structures: spot that changing order doesn't change the total, and recognise how numbers relate to each other.
subject: Mathematics

label: Learning from Mistakes
statement: Demonstrate the “Learning from Mistakes” objective: Understand that making mistakes is a normal part of learning and that everyone — including adults — makes mistakes, and begin to see mistakes as opportunities to learn rather than reasons to give up.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Actions and Their Consequences
