statement: Demonstrate the “Actions and Their Consequences” objective: Understand that actions have consequences — that what you choose to do affects both yourself and other people — and begin to think about what might happen before they act.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Comparing Lengths & Heights
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing Lengths & Heights” objective: Compare two objects directly by length or height and describe the difference using language such as long, short, tall, longer, shorter, taller, double, half.
subject: Mathematics

label: Finding Exoplanets
statement: Demonstrate the “Finding Exoplanets” objective: Describe how astronomers detect planets around other stars using transit photometry (dip in starlight as a planet crosses) and radial velocity (Doppler wobble of the star), explain the habitable zone concept, and discuss what atmospheric biosignatures — such as oxygen, methane, and water vapour detected together — would suggest about a planet.
subject: Science

label: Structural terminology
statement: Demonstrate the “Structural terminology” objective: Use structural terminology (chapter, scene, stanza) to refer to parts of literary texts and describe how each successive part builds on earlier sections.
subject: English

label: Inferring Characters' Feelings and Motives
statement: Demonstrate the “Inferring Characters' Feelings and Motives” objective: Draw inferences from independently-read texts, such as inferring characters' feelings, thoughts and motives from their actions, and justifying inferences with evidence from the text.
subject: English

label: Reversible Changes
statement: Demonstrate the “Reversible Changes” objective: Demonstrate that dissolving, mixing, and changes of state are reversible changes where no new materials are formed.
subject: Science

label: Capitals for Names, Days and I
statement: Demonstrate the “Capitals for Names, Days and I” objective: Use capital letters for proper nouns (names of people, places) the days of the week, and the personal pronoun 'I'.
subject: English

label: Towns & Trade
statement: Demonstrate the “Towns & Trade” objective: The growth of medieval towns: markets, guilds, the merchant class; how towns won charters of self-governance; the shift from purely rural to partly urban life.
subject: History

label: Telling time to the minute (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Telling time to the minute (age 8+)” objective: Tell and write time to the nearest minute using analogue and digital clocks.
subject: Mathematics

label: 2-D faces on 3-D shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “2-D faces on 3-D shapes” objective: Identify 2-D shapes on the surface of 3-D shapes (e.g. a circle on a cylinder, a triangle on a pyramid).
subject: Mathematics

label: Reactions That Release or Absorb Heat
statement: Demonstrate the “Reactions That Release or Absorb Heat” objective: Distinguish between exothermic reactions (release energy, temperature rises) and endothermic reactions (absorb energy, temperature falls), with everyday and industrial examples.
subject: Science

label: Expressing Time, Place and Cause
statement: Demonstrate the “Expressing Time, Place and Cause” objective: Use conjunctions (when, before, after, while, so, because), adverbs (then, next, soon, therefore) and prepositions (before, after, during, in, because of) to express time, place and cause within and across sentences.
subject: English

label: Asteroids, Comets & Dwarf Planets
statement: Demonstrate the “Asteroids, Comets & Dwarf Planets” objective: Identify other objects in the solar system beyond planets: asteroids (rocky bodies mostly between Mars and Jupiter), comets (icy bodies with tails when near the Sun), and meteoroids/meteors/meteorites (space rocks that enter Earth’s atmosphere).
subject: Science

label: Earning Money
statement: Demonstrate the “Earning Money” objective: Ways that children and adults earn money; the connection between work, skills and pay; that harder or more skilled work often pays more.
subject: Life Skills

label: Describing Movements
statement: Demonstrate the “Describing Movements” objective: Describe movements between positions as translations of a given unit to the left/right and up/down.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Mesozoic Era
statement: Demonstrate the “The Mesozoic Era” objective: Place the three periods of the Mesozoic Era — Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous — in order and understand that different dinosaurs lived in different periods, not all at the same time.
subject: Science

label: Adding two two-digit numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding two two-digit numbers” objective: Add and subtract two two-digit numbers using concrete objects, pictorial representations, and mental methods.
subject: Mathematics

label: Variation & Survival Advantage
statement: Demonstrate the “Variation & Survival Advantage” objective: Use evidence to explain how variations in characteristics among individuals of the same species may provide advantages in surviving, finding mates, and reproducing.
subject: Science

label: Weather Forecasting & Safety
statement: Demonstrate the “Weather Forecasting & Safety” objective: Ask questions to obtain information about the purpose of weather forecasting and how people prepare for and respond to severe weather.
subject: Science

label: Food Webs & Interdependence
statement: Demonstrate the “Food Webs & Interdependence” objective: Construct and interpret food webs showing the interdependence of organisms in an ecosystem, explaining how a change in one population affects others.
subject: Science

label: Banks & Saving
statement: Demonstrate the “Banks & Saving” objective: What banks do and why people use them; bank accounts as safe places for money; that savings in a bank can earn interest; children's savings accounts.
subject: Life Skills

label: Vocabulary: making decisions and keeping safe
statement: Demonstrate the “Vocabulary: making decisions and keeping safe” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of making decisions and keeping safe — choice, consequence, rule, safe, fair, honest, trusted adult, and right and wrong — and understand that naming these ideas clearly helps make better choices.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Rows & Columns in Rectangles
statement: Demonstrate the “Rows & Columns in Rectangles” objective: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.
subject: Mathematics

label: Earth Is Made of Rock
statement: Demonstrate the “Earth Is Made of Rock” objective: Understand that Earth is made of rock and other solid materials.
subject: Science

label: Women in the Middle Ages
statement: Demonstrate the “Women in the Middle Ages” objective: The lives of medieval women: noblewomen managing estates, peasant women's hard daily work, nuns and abbesses, notable figures like Eleanor of Aquitaine and Joan of Arc.
subject: History

label: Reading Food Web Diagrams
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading Food Web Diagrams” objective: Read and interpret food web diagrams — identify producers, primary and secondary consumers, and decomposers; trace energy flow along food chains within the web; predict the effect of removing or adding a species.
subject: Science

label: Linking paragraphs with adverbials
statement: Demonstrate the “Linking paragraphs with adverbials” objective: Link ideas across paragraphs using adverbials of time (later, meanwhile, after a while), place (nearby, far away, beyond the wall), and number (secondly, finally, in addition) to guide the reader through a multi-paragraph text.
subject: English

label: Syllables
statement: Demonstrate the “Syllables” objective: Count, blend, and segment syllables in spoken words; divide written words into syllables as an aid to reading and spelling.
subject: English

label: Colons and Semicolons in Lists
statement: Demonstrate the “Colons and Semicolons in Lists” objective: Use a colon to introduce a list and semi-colons to separate items within lists, particularly when list items contain internal commas or are complex phrases.
subject: English

label: Roman Law, Latin, and Christianity
statement: Demonstrate the “Roman Law, Latin, and Christianity” objective: Understand that Roman law became the basis for legal systems across Europe and beyond, that Latin is the root of French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, and Romanian and gave English hundreds of words (e.g. exit, video, annual, education), and that Christianity spread throughout the Roman Empire, eventually becoming its official religion under Emperor Constantine.
subject: History

label: Scribes and the Rosetta Stone
statement: Demonstrate the “Scribes and the Rosetta Stone” objective: Know that scribes were specially trained people who could read and write hieroglyphs, that the Rosetta Stone — a slab with the same text in three scripts — was the key to cracking the hieroglyphic code, and that Jean-François Champollion used it to decipher hieroglyphs in 1822 after centuries of mystery.
subject: History

label: Nocturnal Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Nocturnal Animals” objective: Know that some animals are nocturnal — active at night and sleeping during the day — and that nocturnal animals often have special features like big eyes (owls, tarsiers), large ears (bats, fennec foxes), or sensitive whiskers to help them find food in the dark.
subject: Science

label: Reading with Expression and Accuracy
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading with Expression and Accuracy” objective: Read aloud with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression (prosody), re-reading familiar texts to build fluency and confidence, and using context to self-correct.
subject: English

label: Types of Chemical Reaction
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of Chemical Reaction” objective: Identify and describe four types of chemical reaction: combustion (burning in oxygen), oxidation (gain of oxygen), thermal decomposition (breaking down by heat), and displacement (more reactive metal replaces less reactive one).
subject: Science

label: The Water Cycle
statement: Demonstrate the “The Water Cycle” objective: Describe the water cycle, tracing water through evaporation, condensation, precipitation, surface runoff, and transpiration in plants, explaining how the sun drives the cycle.
subject: Science

label: Story Lessons and Morals
statement: Demonstrate the “Story Lessons and Morals” objective: Determine the central message, lesson, or moral of a story, fable, or folktale, explaining what the story teaches the reader and supporting the interpretation with key details from the text.
subject: English

label: Animals Everywhere
statement: Demonstrate the “Animals Everywhere” objective: Know that animals live all over the world — on land, in water, and in the air — and that every continent, even icy Antarctica, is home to animals, each suited to the conditions where they live.
subject: Science

label: Choosing Form and Tone for Your Audience
statement: Demonstrate the “Choosing Form and Tone for Your Audience” objective: Identify the audience for and purpose of writing before beginning, selecting the appropriate form, tone, and register to match the intended reader and communicative goal.
subject: English

label: Reflecting After Learning
statement: Demonstrate the “Reflecting After Learning” objective: After completing a piece of learning, reflect on the process: what helped most, what was confusing, and what would you do differently next time?
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Fact vs opinion
statement: Demonstrate the “Fact vs opinion” objective: Distinguish between statements of fact and statements of opinion in texts, recognising how authors blend factual information with subjective viewpoints.
subject: English

label: Tropical Rainforest Climate
statement: Demonstrate the “Tropical Rainforest Climate” objective: Understand that rainforests have a tropical climate — consistently hot (25–30°C) with over 2000 mm of rainfall per year — and that this combination of heat and moisture creates ideal conditions for rapid plant growth and extraordinary biodiversity.
subject: Science

label: Gas Exchange & Breathing
statement: Demonstrate the “Gas Exchange & Breathing” objective: Describe the structure of the human gas exchange system (trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, alveoli) and explain how the mechanism of breathing — using pressure changes from rib and diaphragm movement — moves air in and out of the lungs.
subject: Science

label: Galaxies and the universe
statement: Demonstrate the “Galaxies and the universe” objective: Describe the scale of the universe, including the structure of galaxies, the position of the Sun in the Milky Way, and the use of light years as a unit of distance, and appreciate why space exploration requires enormous timescales.
subject: Science

label: Sympathy Versus Empathy
statement: Demonstrate the “Sympathy Versus Empathy” objective: Distinguish sympathy ('I feel sorry for you') from empathy ('I understand what you're experiencing'); develop active listening skills: reflecting, paraphrasing, asking open questions, resisting the urge to problem-solve too quickly; understand empathic curiosity as genuine interest in another person's inner world; practise being present for someone in distress without trying to fix or minimise their experience; understand vicarious trauma and compassion fatigue, and how empathetic people can protect their own wellbeing while staying present for others.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Erosion and weathering
statement: Demonstrate the “Erosion and weathering” objective: Make observations and measurements to provide evidence of the effects of weathering or the rate of erosion by water, ice, wind, or vegetation.
subject: Science

label: Narrative Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Narrative Writing” objective: Write narratives with developed settings, characters and plot, using dialogue and description to develop experiences and show character responses to situations.
subject: English

label: Early Word Problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Early Word Problems” objective: Solve one-step word problems involving addition and subtraction to 20, including missing-number problems.
subject: Mathematics

label: Vibrations & Sound
statement: Demonstrate the “Vibrations & Sound” objective: Understand that vibrating materials can make sound, and that sound can make materials vibrate.
subject: Science

label: Story Sequence and Central Message
statement: Demonstrate the “Story Sequence and Central Message” objective: Discuss the sequence of events in narrative texts and how items of information are related in non-fiction, retelling stories including key details and demonstrating understanding of central message or lesson.
subject: English

label: Cells Under the Microscope
statement: Demonstrate the “Cells Under the Microscope” objective: Understand that all living organisms are made of cells and use a light microscope to observe, interpret, and record cell structure.
subject: Science

label: Reading and writing numbers to 1000
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading and writing numbers to 1000” objective: Read and write numbers to 1000 in numerals, number names, and expanded form.
subject: Mathematics

label: More batteries, brighter bulb
statement: Demonstrate the “More batteries, brighter bulb” objective: Associate the brightness of a lamp or volume of a buzzer with the number and voltage of cells used in a series circuit.
subject: Science

label: Roman Republic and Empire
statement: Demonstrate the “Roman Republic and Empire” objective: Explain how Rome was first governed as a republic — with elected consuls, a powerful Senate, and a distinction between patricians and plebeians — before becoming an empire ruled by emperors like Augustus (who brought peace, the Pax Romana) and Nero, and compare republican government with Athenian direct democracy.
subject: History

label: Fraction Addition Concepts
statement: Demonstrate the “Fraction Addition Concepts” objective: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts; decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way.
subject: Mathematics

label: Picture & Bar Graphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Picture & Bar Graphs” objective: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories; solve put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph.
subject: Mathematics

label: Substituting into Formulae
statement: Demonstrate the “Substituting into Formulae” objective: Substitute numerical values into formulae and expressions including scientific formulae; evaluate expressions by replacing variables with given values and computing the result using correct order of operations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Decimals for Tenths & Hundredths
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimals for Tenths & Hundredths” objective: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100; read and write decimal numbers as fractions (e.g. 0.62 = 62/100, 0.71 = 71/100).
subject: Mathematics

label: Natural resources
statement: Demonstrate the “Natural resources” objective: Obtain and combine information to describe that energy and fuels are derived from natural resources and that their uses affect the environment.
subject: Science

label: Observing with simple equipment
statement: Demonstrate the “Observing with simple equipment” objective: Observe closely using simple equipment such as hand lenses, and use observations to describe, compare, and identify things.
subject: Science

label: 2-D shapes (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “2-D shapes (age 7+)” objective: Draw 2-D shapes and make 3-D shapes using modelling materials; recognise 3-D shapes in different orientations and describe them.
subject: Mathematics

label: Roman soldiers & builders
statement: Demonstrate the “Roman soldiers & builders” objective: Know that Roman soldiers marched across a huge empire building straight roads and strong walls, and that some Roman roads, walls, and buildings can still be seen today — showing that the Romans were powerful builders whose work has lasted thousands of years.
subject: History

label: Fraction Notation
statement: Demonstrate the “Fraction Notation” objective: Read, write, and use fraction notation correctly — fraction, numerator, denominator, unit fraction, non-unit fraction, proper fraction, improper fraction, mixed number, equivalent fraction, simplest form — and understand what each term describes, including the roles of the numerator and denominator in expressing parts of a whole.
subject: Mathematics

label: Multiplication as scaling
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiplication as scaling” objective: Interpret multiplication as scaling (resizing): compare the size of a product to a factor based on the size of the other factor without computing; explain the effect of multiplying by fractions greater than, equal to, or less than 1.
subject: Mathematics

label: Shades of Meaning
statement: Demonstrate the “Shades of Meaning” objective: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs describing similar actions and among adjectives differing in intensity; make real-life connections between words and their use.
subject: English

label: The Probability Scale
statement: Demonstrate the “The Probability Scale” objective: Understand probability as a measure on a scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain); use the language of probability including likely, unlikely, certain, and impossible.
subject: Mathematics

label: Commas to avoid ambiguity
statement: Demonstrate the “Commas to avoid ambiguity” objective: Use commas to clarify meaning and avoid ambiguity in sentences where the absence of a comma could cause misreading.
subject: English

label: Ratio (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Ratio (age 10+)” objective: Perform mental calculations including with mixed operations and large numbers, using strategies such as partitioning, compensation, and derived facts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Nets of 3-D Shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Nets of 3-D Shapes” objective: Identify, draw, and interpret nets of common 3-D shapes — cubes, cuboids, triangular prisms, and square-based pyramids — by predicting which 3-D shape a given flat arrangement of faces will fold into, checking whether a net will close completely, and sketching a net from a description or 3-D model; understand the relationship between the number of faces and the structure of the net.
subject: Mathematics

label: Gladiators & Pompeii
statement: Demonstrate the “Gladiators & Pompeii” objective: Know that Romans watched gladiators fight in huge arenas like the Colosseum in Rome, that gladiators were usually enslaved people or prisoners trained to fight, and that the city of Pompeii was buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79, preserving an extraordinary snapshot of Roman daily life.
subject: History

label: Who Is a Customer?
statement: Demonstrate the “Who Is a Customer?” objective: Understanding that a customer is someone who buys what you make or do; thinking about what customers want and need; the idea that businesses serve people.
subject: Life Skills

label: Multimedia Presentations
statement: Demonstrate the “Multimedia Presentations” objective: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.
subject: English

label: Moments, Pressure & Hooke's Law
statement: Demonstrate the “Moments, Pressure & Hooke's Law” objective: Calculate the turning effect (moment = force × perpendicular distance), explain how pressure is transmitted equally in liquids (Pascal's principle) and the concept of atmospheric pressure, and describe Hooke's Law (extension ∝ force up to the elastic limit).
subject: Science

label: Using inverse operations
statement: Demonstrate the “Using inverse operations” objective: Recognise and use relationships between operations including inverse operations; use these relationships to check answers and simplify calculations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Estimating by rounding
statement: Demonstrate the “Estimating by rounding” objective: Use approximation through rounding to estimate answers and calculate possible resulting errors expressed using inequality notation a < x ≤ b; understand upper and lower bounds of rounded values.
subject: Mathematics

label: Adjective Order in Sentences
statement: Demonstrate the “Adjective Order in Sentences” objective: Order adjectives within sentences according to conventional English patterns (opinion-size-age-shape-colour-origin-material-purpose) to produce natural-sounding descriptions.
subject: English

label: Vocabulary: historical thinking
statement: Demonstrate the “Vocabulary: historical thinking” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of historical thinking — source, evidence, primary source, secondary source, artefact, chronology, chronological order, BC/BCE, AD/CE, century, decade, era, period, timeline, excavation, archaeologist, interpretation, corroborate, bias, perspective — and apply these terms when discussing how we know about the past and how reliable our knowledge is.
subject: History

label: Negative Numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Negative Numbers” objective: Count backwards through zero to include negative numbers.
subject: Mathematics

label: Prepositions
statement: Demonstrate the “Prepositions” objective: Understand and use the most frequently occurring prepositions of location and direction (e.g. to, from, in, out, on, off, for, by, with).
subject: English

label: Gods & the Parthenon
statement: Demonstrate the “Gods & the Parthenon” objective: Name the major Greek gods and their roles — Zeus (king, thunder), Hera (queen, marriage), Athena (wisdom, warfare), Poseidon (sea), Apollo (sun, music), Artemis (hunting, moon), Ares (war), Aphrodite (love), Hermes (messengers), Hephaestus (fire, crafts), Hades (underworld) — and know that the Parthenon in Athens was a grand temple built to honour Athena.
subject: History

label: Decimal & Percent Notation
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimal & Percent Notation” objective: Read, write, and use decimal and percentage notation correctly — decimal, decimal point, tenths, hundredths, thousandths, percentage, per cent, % symbol, convert, terminating decimal — and understand the relationships between fractions, decimals, and percentages as three ways of expressing the same value.
subject: Mathematics

label: Renewable vs non-renewable energy
statement: Demonstrate the “Renewable vs non-renewable energy” objective: Distinguish between renewable energy resources (solar, wind, hydroelectric, tidal, geothermal, biomass) and non-renewable resources (coal, oil, gas, nuclear), comparing their advantages, disadvantages, and environmental impacts.
subject: Science

label: Rock Pool Habitats
statement: Demonstrate the “Rock Pool Habitats” objective: Explore rock pools (tide pools) as small ocean habitats where crabs, anemones, starfish, and small fish can be found, and understand that these creatures are adapted to survive crashing waves and changing water levels.
subject: Science

label: Earth's Spin & Orbit
statement: Demonstrate the “Earth's Spin & Orbit” objective: Understand that Earth moves in two ways: it rotates (spins) on its axis once every 24 hours causing day and night, and it orbits (travels around) the Sun once every 365 days, which is one year.
subject: Science

label: Eruption Types & Volcano Shape
statement: Demonstrate the “Eruption Types & Volcano Shape” objective: Understand that not all volcanic eruptions are the same: some flow gently (effusive) and some explode violently (explosive), depending on the properties of the magma, and that volcano shape is related to eruption type.
subject: Science

label: Roles in a Group
statement: Demonstrate the “Roles in a Group” objective: Understand different roles people play in groups — leader, supporter, mediator, idea-generator — and recognise that effective groups need a mix of roles, not everyone trying to be the leader.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Ocean Ecosystems
statement: Demonstrate the “Ocean Ecosystems” objective: Understand ocean ecosystems as interconnected systems where living things (producers, consumers, decomposers) and non-living factors (temperature, salinity, light, currents) all interact, and that changes to one part affect the whole system.
subject: Science

label: Connecting Ideas in Texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Connecting Ideas in Texts” objective: Describe connections between events, ideas, or concepts in informational text using time, sequence, cause-and-effect, and comparison language, and identify logical connections between sentences and paragraphs.
subject: English

label: Scams & Online Safety
statement: Demonstrate the “Scams & Online Safety” objective: Recognising financial scams and tricks; phishing emails and fake websites; protecting personal and financial information online; 'if it seems too good to be true, it probably is'.
subject: Life Skills

label: Waves & Different Materials
statement: Demonstrate the “Waves & Different Materials” objective: Explain how waves can be absorbed, transmitted, or reflected by different materials, and apply these interactions to explain colour perception, sight, communication technologies, and the effects of different surfaces on wave behaviour.
subject: Science

label: Patterns in Times Tables
statement: Demonstrate the “Patterns in Times Tables” objective: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table) and explain them using properties of operations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Ceramics, Polymers & Composites
statement: Demonstrate the “Ceramics, Polymers & Composites” objective: Describe the properties and uses of ceramics (hard, brittle, heat-resistant), polymers (flexible, lightweight, variable), and composites (combine properties of constituent materials), giving real-world examples of each.
subject: Science

label: Planet Features
statement: Demonstrate the “Planet Features” objective: Describe a key feature of each planet: Mercury is smallest and closest, Venus is the hottest, Mars is red with rust, Jupiter is the largest with a Great Red Spot, Saturn has rings, Uranus tilts on its side, Neptune is the farthest and very cold.
subject: Science

label: Simple tests and experiments
statement: Demonstrate the “Simple tests and experiments” objective: Perform simple tests and use observations and ideas to suggest answers to questions.
subject: Science

label: Decimals and fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Decimals and fractions” objective: Solve simple measure and money problems involving fractions and decimals to two decimal places.
subject: Mathematics

label: Linear Function Graphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Linear Function Graphs” objective: Recognise that a linear function produces a straight-line graph, understand the relationship between an equation of the form y = mx + c and its graphical representation, and interpret gradient and y-intercept in context.
subject: Mathematics

label: Sitting and holding a pencil
statement: Demonstrate the “Sitting and holding a pencil” objective: Sit correctly at a table holding a pencil comfortably and correctly; form lower-case letters in the correct direction starting and finishing in the right place.
subject: English

label: Right and Wrong Choices
statement: Demonstrate the “Right and Wrong Choices” objective: Know the difference between right and wrong in familiar everyday situations — understanding basic rules about honesty, not hurting others, respecting others' property, and being fair — and choose to do the right thing even when it's harder.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: One-to-one counting
statement: Demonstrate the “One-to-one counting” objective: One-to-one correspondence when counting objects: each object is paired with exactly one number name.
subject: Mathematics

label: Measuring Perimeters
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring Perimeters” objective: Measure the perimeter of simple 2-D shapes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Changing Shapes of Solids
statement: Demonstrate the “Changing Shapes of Solids” objective: Investigate how the shapes of solid objects can be changed by squashing, bending, twisting, and stretching.
subject: Science

label: The Periodic Table
statement: Demonstrate the “The Periodic Table” objective: Describe the organisation of the periodic table into periods and groups, explain the contribution of Mendeleev, and use the table to identify metals, non-metals, and predict patterns in reactivity.
subject: Science

label: 12-hour and 24-hour time
statement: Demonstrate the “12-hour and 24-hour time” objective: Read, write, and convert time between analogue and digital 12-hour and 24-hour clocks.
subject: Mathematics

label: Tracing Theme Across a Text
statement: Demonstrate the “Tracing Theme Across a Text” objective: Determine and analyse the theme or central idea of a text, trace how it develops across the text through key details and events, and provide an objective summary distinct from personal opinion.
subject: English

label: Multiplication as repeated addition (age 6+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiplication as repeated addition (age 6+)” objective: Solve problems involving multiplication and division using arrays, repeated addition, mental methods, and known facts.
subject: Mathematics

label: Animal Communication
statement: Demonstrate the “Animal Communication” objective: Understand that animals communicate in many different ways — birds sing to attract mates and defend territory, whales call across vast ocean distances, bees dance to show other bees where food is, wolves howl to keep the pack together, and fireflies flash light signals — and that communication is essential for survival.
subject: Science

label: Making Sense of Problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Making Sense of Problems” objective: Make sense of a problem by identifying what is being asked, choosing concrete objects or pictures to represent the situation, and explaining a pathway to the solution.
subject: Mathematics

label: Structured Opinion Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Structured Opinion Writing” objective: Compose opinion pieces that introduce a topic, state a clear point of view, provide organised reasons linked with connecting words, and include a concluding statement or section.
subject: English

label: Pollination & Seed Dispersal
statement: Demonstrate the “Pollination & Seed Dispersal” objective: Understand the life cycle of flowering plants including pollination, seed formation, and seed dispersal.
subject: Science

label: Multiplying and dividing (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiplying and dividing (age 10+)” objective: Multiply and divide numbers by 10, 100, and 1000 giving answers up to three decimal places, understanding that digits shift position in the place-value chart.
subject: Mathematics

label: Reading Dinosaur Trackways
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading Dinosaur Trackways” objective: Use dinosaur trackways (fossilised footprints) to make inferences about a dinosaur's size, speed, and behaviour — widely spaced prints suggest running, closely spaced suggest walking.
subject: Science

label: Subordinate clauses
statement: Demonstrate the “Subordinate clauses” objective: Use subordination (when, if, that, because) and co-ordination (or, and, but) to join clauses and create compound and complex sentences.
subject: English

label: Times tables (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Times tables (age 7+)” objective: Recall and use multiplication and division facts for the 3, 4, and 8 multiplication tables.
subject: Mathematics

label: Caterpillar to butterfly
statement: Demonstrate the “Caterpillar to butterfly” objective: Caterpillar to butterfly: the life cycle of a butterfly as an observable transformation. Egg → caterpillar → chrysalis → butterfly. The idea that one creature can change its whole form. Classroom butterfly kits, The Very Hungry Caterpillar.
subject: Science

label: Vocabulary: understanding others
statement: Demonstrate the “Vocabulary: understanding others” objective: Know and use the key vocabulary for understanding others — empathy, perspective, kind, fair, community, similar, different, and care — and understand that these words describe real habits of thinking and feeling.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Comparing Characters, Settings and Events
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing Characters, Settings and Events” objective: Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific details about how characters interact, settings influence action, or events connect.
subject: English

label: Smart Versus Not-Smart Devices
statement: Demonstrate the “Smart Versus Not-Smart Devices” objective: Sorting objects into 'smart' (can sense and respond) and 'not smart' (just sits there); a toaster vs a smart speaker; introduction to the idea that some machines can sense and respond to the world.
subject: Computing

label: Division with remainders (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Division with remainders (age 10+)” objective: Divide numbers up to 4 digits by a two-digit divisor using formal written long division, interpreting remainders as whole numbers, fractions, or by rounding as appropriate.
subject: Mathematics

label: Perimeters of polygons
statement: Demonstrate the “Perimeters of polygons” objective: Solve problems involving perimeters of polygons: find perimeter from side lengths, find an unknown side length, and explore rectangles with same perimeter but different areas (or vice versa).
subject: Mathematics

label: Types of angles (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Types of angles (age 11+)” objective: Use conventional geometric terms and notation to describe, sketch, and draw points, lines, parallel and perpendicular lines, right angles, regular polygons, and reflectively/rotationally symmetric polygons.
subject: Mathematics

label: Online Identity and Misinformation
statement: Demonstrate the “Online Identity and Misinformation” objective: Understand the ethics of online identity and the importance of consistency between who you are online and offline; explain how recommendation algorithms and filter bubbles narrow information exposure; evaluate the psychology of misinformation: why it spreads, why smart people believe it, and how to apply source evaluation (lateral reading, checking evidence, recognising emotional manipulation); understand digital consent around sharing images or personal information; explore the ethics of AI, surveillance, and data privacy as they affect everyday life; reflect on responsible content creation and online influence.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Tsunamis
statement: Demonstrate the “Tsunamis” objective: Know what a tsunami is: a very large, fast ocean wave caused by an earthquake or volcanic eruption under the sea, which can cause great damage when it reaches land.
subject: Science

label: 3-D shapes (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “3-D shapes (age 9+)” objective: Identify 3-D shapes, including cubes and other cuboids, from 2-D representations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Bullet Point Punctuation
statement: Demonstrate the “Bullet Point Punctuation” objective: Punctuate bullet points consistently to list information clearly, applying conventions for capitalisation, end punctuation, and parallel structure across items.
subject: English

label: Spotting Patterns
statement: Demonstrate the “Spotting Patterns” objective: Spot patterns and recurring structures — in numbers, words, nature, sounds, or events — and use them to make sense of new information.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Group discussions
statement: Demonstrate the “Group discussions” objective: Participate actively in collaborative conversations staying on topic; continue a conversation through multiple exchanges; maintain attention in discussions.
subject: English

label: Checking Sources Against Each Other
statement: Demonstrate the “Checking Sources Against Each Other” objective: Corroborate: check whether multiple sources agree on the same facts — and investigate why they might not.
subject: History

label: Pollination & Pollinator Decline
statement: Demonstrate the “Pollination & Pollinator Decline” objective: Explain the importance of insect pollination for plant reproduction and human food security, and discuss the consequences of pollinator decline.
subject: Science

label: Fluent multiplication and division facts
statement: Demonstrate the “Fluent multiplication and division facts” objective: Fluently multiply and divide within 100 using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division.
subject: Mathematics

label: Rainforest Plant Adaptations
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Plant Adaptations” objective: Know how rainforest plants are adapted to their environment — drip-tip leaves channel water off quickly to prevent rot, buttress roots spread wide to support tall trees in thin soil, epiphytes (like orchids and bromeliads) grow on tree branches to reach sunlight without needing soil, and lianas climb trunks to reach the canopy.
subject: Science

label: Patterns & Sequences
statement: Demonstrate the “Patterns & Sequences” objective: Order and arrange combinations of mathematical objects in patterns and sequences.
subject: Mathematics

label: Changing Environments
statement: Demonstrate the “Changing Environments” objective: Recognise that environments can change and that this can sometimes pose dangers and challenges to living things.
subject: Science

label: Mental and written addition and subtraction
statement: Demonstrate the “Mental and written addition and subtraction” objective: Solve addition and subtraction problems using mental and written methods, including problems involving numbers, quantities, and measures.
subject: Mathematics

label: Net Zero & Energy Transition
statement: Demonstrate the “Net Zero & Energy Transition” objective: Evaluate the energy transition required to reach net zero: renewable energy scaling, electrification of transport and heat, green hydrogen; describe carbon capture and storage (CCS) and direct air capture (DAC); introduce proposed solar radiation management techniques (stratospheric aerosol injection, marine cloud brightening) and their potential risks and governance challenges; critically evaluate the role of individual behaviour change versus systemic policy in reducing emissions.
subject: Science

label: Vocabulary Strategies
statement: Demonstrate the “Vocabulary Strategies” objective: Determine the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases using a flexible range of strategies — including context clues, Greek and Latin affixes and roots, reference materials, and verification of inferred meaning.
subject: English

label: Domain Vocabulary Across Subject Areas
statement: Demonstrate the “Domain Vocabulary Across Subject Areas” objective: Acquire and use accurately academic and domain-specific vocabulary relevant to grade-level topics, including words that signal precise meaning in informational texts across subject areas.
subject: English

label: Other People's Feelings and Thoughts
statement: Demonstrate the “Other People's Feelings and Thoughts” objective: Understand that other people have their own feelings and thoughts, and that these might be different from your own — a foundational awareness that not everyone sees or feels things the same way.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: How energy travels around
statement: Demonstrate the “How energy travels around” objective: Observe and provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat, and electric currents.
subject: Science

label: Greek and Latin Roots for Word Meaning
statement: Demonstrate the “Greek and Latin Roots for Word Meaning” objective: Use knowledge of Greek and Latin affixes (prefixes and suffixes) and roots as clues to determine the meaning of unfamiliar words, building a bank of common roots and their meanings.
subject: English

label: Correlation vs Causation
statement: Demonstrate the “Correlation vs Causation” objective: Two things happening together doesn't mean one caused the other — recognise the difference between correlation and causation before drawing conclusions.
subject: Science

label: Comparatives & Superlatives
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparatives & Superlatives” objective: Form and use comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs, choosing correctly between them.
subject: English

label: Narrative Perspective and Unreliable Narrators
statement: Demonstrate the “Narrative Perspective and Unreliable Narrators” objective: Analyse point of view and narrative perspective — including first person, third person limited and omniscient, and unreliable narrator — and how the author's or narrator's perspective shapes the reader's understanding and creates effects such as suspense, irony, or humour.
subject: English

label: The Arctic Tundra
statement: Demonstrate the “The Arctic Tundra” objective: Know what the Arctic tundra is — a vast, treeless landscape with permafrost (permanently frozen ground) just below the surface, a very short growing season in summer when mosses, lichens, and tough grasses burst into life, and home to caribou/reindeer, musk oxen, lemmings, and snowy owls.
subject: Science

label: Ratio (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Ratio (age 11+)” objective: Use conventional notation for the priority of operations including brackets, powers, roots, and reciprocals; apply BIDMAS/BODMAS consistently to evaluate complex numerical expressions.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Vikings
statement: Demonstrate the “The Vikings” objective: Who the Vikings were: seafaring warriors and traders from Scandinavia; longships; Viking raids on Britain; that Vikings also settled and farmed.
subject: History

label: Rainforest Plants
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Plants” objective: Know that rainforests contain an enormous variety of plants — towering kapok and Brazil nut trees, climbing vines called lianas, colourful orchids that grow on tree branches, giant water lilies, and huge leaves that funnel rainwater.
subject: Science

label: Friendships change over time
statement: Demonstrate the “Friendships change over time” objective: Understand that friendships change over time — that it's normal for friends to drift apart or for new friendships to form — and develop strategies for making new friends and handling friendship changes without feeling like something is wrong with them.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Reading and writing numbers to 100
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading and writing numbers to 100” objective: Read and write numerals from 0 to 100.
subject: Mathematics

label: Halves & Quarters of Shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Halves & Quarters of Shapes” objective: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares and describe them using the words halves, fourths, and quarters.
subject: Mathematics

label: One Quantity as a Fraction
statement: Demonstrate the “One Quantity as a Fraction” objective: Express one quantity as a fraction of another where the result may be less than 1 or greater than 1, and interpret the meaning in context.
subject: Mathematics

label: Who Really Built the Pyramids
statement: Demonstrate the “Who Really Built the Pyramids” objective: Analyse who built the pyramids and why, evaluating the evidence against the alien-builder myth and the slave-labour myth: archaeological evidence from worker villages at Giza shows a paid, skilled, well-fed workforce; discuss the social functions of monument building as a form of state organisation, religious duty, and employment; and assess the current controversy over newly discovered construction ramps and logistics.
subject: History

label: Computers in Everyday Life
statement: Demonstrate the “Computers in Everyday Life” objective: Identifying computers in everyday life — not just laptops but phones, tablets, smart speakers, traffic lights, washing machines; what makes something a computer.
subject: Computing

label: Rainforest Products in Daily Life
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Products in Daily Life” objective: Understand how rainforest products connect to everyday life through global supply chains — palm oil is in snacks, soap, and cosmetics; soy feeds livestock worldwide; cocoa becomes chocolate; rubber is in tyres and gloves; timber becomes furniture; and many medicines originate from rainforest plants — and that consumer choices can drive either destruction or sustainable practices.
subject: Science

label: Book Features and Author's Reasons
statement: Demonstrate the “Book Features and Author's Reasons” objective: Identify front cover, back cover, and title page of a book; identify the reasons an author gives to support points in informational text.
subject: English

label: Precise Maths Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Precise Maths Vocabulary” objective: Communicate with mathematical precision: use correct vocabulary for primes, factors, multiples, angle types, and polygon regularity; specify units including cm², m³, °; use notation for squares/cubes and percentages accurately.
subject: Mathematics

label: Complementary events
statement: Demonstrate the “Complementary events” objective: Understand and apply the rule that probabilities of all mutually exclusive outcomes sum to one; use this to find the probability of a complementary event (P(not A) = 1 − P(A)).
subject: Mathematics

label: Pompeii & Vesuvius
statement: Demonstrate the “Pompeii & Vesuvius” objective: Know the story of Pompeii: a Roman city buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD, preserved under volcanic ash, and rediscovered by archaeologists centuries later.
subject: Science

label: Factors, multiples, and primes (age 11+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Factors, multiples, and primes (age 11+)” objective: Use the concepts and vocabulary of prime numbers, factors, multiples, common factors, common multiples, highest common factor (HCF), lowest common multiple (LCM), and prime factorisation including product notation and the unique factorisation property.
subject: Mathematics

label: Asking scientific questions
statement: Demonstrate the “Asking scientific questions” objective: Ask simple scientific questions and recognise that they can be answered in different ways including observation, testing, and research.
subject: Science

label: Characters' Viewpoints and Responses
statement: Demonstrate the “Characters' Viewpoints and Responses” objective: Identify and compare characters' points of view, recognise who is narrating a story, describe how characters respond to events and challenges, and compare characters' experiences across different stories or versions of the same story.
subject: English

label: Combining Simple Shapes
statement: Demonstrate the “Combining Simple Shapes” objective: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes (e.g. two triangles make a rectangle).
subject: Mathematics

label: Silent Letters in Words
statement: Demonstrate the “Silent Letters in Words” objective: Spell words containing silent letters that are remnants of earlier pronunciation or etymology, recognising common silent-letter patterns and using word origins to remember them.
subject: English

label: Investigating Forces
statement: Demonstrate the “Investigating Forces” objective: Plan and carry out investigations into forces, including measuring force with a newton meter, investigating Hooke's Law, and collecting and interpreting motion data to test Newton's laws.
subject: Science

label: Rainforest Insects
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Insects” objective: Know that rainforests are home to millions of insects — leaf-cutter ants that farm fungus, giant beetles, jewel-coloured butterflies, enormous spiders, and stick insects — and that insects are the most numerous animals in the rainforest.
subject: Science

label: Long multiplication (age 10+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Long multiplication (age 10+)” objective: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers (up to 4 digits by 2 digits) using the formal written method of long multiplication.
subject: Mathematics

label: Our Solar System
statement: Demonstrate the “Our Solar System” objective: Know that there are other planets besides Earth and that our group of planets orbiting the Sun is called the solar system — and that space is the vast area beyond Earth's sky.
subject: Science

label: The teen numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “The teen numbers” objective: Understand that the teen numbers (11–19) are composed of ten ones and some further ones (early place value).
subject: Mathematics

label: Working with Large Numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Working with Large Numbers” objective: Solve number and practical problems involving reading, writing, ordering, comparing, and rounding whole numbers up to 1,000,000.
subject: Mathematics

label: Alexander the Great's Empire
statement: Demonstrate the “Alexander the Great's Empire” objective: Describe how Alexander the Great of Macedon conquered a vast empire stretching from Greece to Egypt to India, spreading Greek language, culture, and ideas across the ancient world — creating a period known as the Hellenistic Age where Greek and Eastern cultures blended.
subject: History

label: Numbers to Ten Million
statement: Demonstrate the “Numbers to Ten Million” objective: Solve number and practical problems involving reading, writing, ordering, comparing, rounding, and negative numbers up to 10,000,000.
subject: Mathematics

label: Summarising Non-Fiction Main Ideas
statement: Demonstrate the “Summarising Non-Fiction Main Ideas” objective: Determine two or more main ideas of an informational text and explain how they are supported by key details, then summarise the text without personal opinions.
subject: English

label: Splitting shapes into equal parts (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Splitting shapes into equal parts (age 7+)” objective: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares; describe shares as halves, thirds, and fourths; recognise that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.
subject: Mathematics

label: Sorting into categories
statement: Demonstrate the “Sorting into categories” objective: Classify objects into given categories, count the number in each category, and sort the categories by count.
subject: Mathematics

label: Mentally adding hundreds to 3-digit numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Mentally adding hundreds to 3-digit numbers” objective: Mentally add and subtract a three-digit number and hundreds.
subject: Mathematics

label: Parts of a circle
statement: Demonstrate the “Parts of a circle” objective: Illustrate and name parts of circles, including radius, diameter, and circumference; know that the diameter is twice the radius.
subject: Mathematics

label: Tectonic Plates
statement: Demonstrate the “Tectonic Plates” objective: Understand that Earth's crust is broken into large pieces called tectonic plates that float on hotter, softer rock beneath and move very slowly — a few centimetres per year.
subject: Science

label: Equally Likely Outcomes
statement: Demonstrate the “Equally Likely Outcomes” objective: Understand that 'equally likely' means every outcome has exactly the same chance of occurring; identify whether a given situation has equally likely outcomes (a fair coin, a fair die, a spinner with equal sections) or unequally likely outcomes (a bag with more of one colour, a spinner with unequal sections).
subject: Mathematics

label: Multimedia elements in texts
statement: Demonstrate the “Multimedia elements in texts” objective: Analyse how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a text such as graphic novels, multimedia presentations, or illustrated editions of fiction and poetry.
subject: English

label: The Electromagnetic Spectrum
statement: Demonstrate the “The Electromagnetic Spectrum” objective: Describe the full electromagnetic spectrum from radio waves to gamma rays, in order of increasing frequency and energy; explain that all EM waves travel at the same speed in a vacuum; and describe the uses and hazards of different regions.
subject: Science

label: Biodiversity & Resilience
statement: Demonstrate the “Biodiversity & Resilience” objective: Explain what biodiversity means, why high biodiversity makes ecosystems more resilient, and describe the ways human activity threatens biodiversity (habitat destruction, pollution, invasive species, climate change).
subject: Science

label: Comparing measurements
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing measurements” objective: Describe, interpret, and compare distributions of a single variable using appropriate measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and spread (range), including the effect of outliers.
subject: Mathematics

label: Understanding angles (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding angles (age 8+)” objective: Understand that shapes in different categories may share attributes defining a larger category; classify quadrilaterals (rhombuses, rectangles, squares) and draw examples of quadrilaterals not in those subcategories.
subject: Mathematics

label: Parts of a Plant
statement: Demonstrate the “Parts of a Plant” objective: Identify and describe the basic structure of common flowering plants (roots, stem, leaves, flowers) and trees (roots, trunk, branches, leaves).
subject: Science

label: Missing number problems (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Missing number problems (age 7+)” objective: Solve addition and subtraction problems including missing-number problems, using number facts, place value, and more complex methods.
subject: Mathematics

label: Reading and writing numbers to 120
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading and writing numbers to 120” objective: Count to 120 starting at any number less than 120; read and write numerals to 120.
subject: Mathematics

label: Rainforest Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Animals” objective: Name and recognise iconic rainforest animals — jaguars, toucans, sloths, poison dart frogs, howler monkeys, macaws, and butterflies — and know which layer of the rainforest each lives in.
subject: Science

label: Comparing lengths by measuring
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing lengths by measuring” objective: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit.
subject: Mathematics

label: Ratio Notation
statement: Demonstrate the “Ratio Notation” objective: Use ratio notation to describe the relationship between two or more quantities, simplify ratios to their simplest form, and convert between ratio and fraction representations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Rainforest Animal Survival Tricks
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Animal Survival Tricks” objective: Know how rainforest animals are adapted to their environment — camouflage helps leaf insects and tree frogs hide, bright warning colours (aposematism) signal that poison dart frogs are toxic, prehensile tails let monkeys grip branches, toucans' large beaks help reach distant fruit, and many animals are nocturnal to avoid daytime heat.
subject: Science

label: Punctuating Clauses
statement: Demonstrate the “Punctuating Clauses” objective: Use semi-colons, colons, and dashes to mark boundaries between independent clauses, choosing the appropriate punctuation based on the relationship between the clauses.
subject: English

label: Unknown in Multiplication & Division
statement: Demonstrate the “Unknown in Multiplication & Division” objective: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers (e.g. 8 × ? = 48, ? × 6 = 42).
subject: Mathematics

label: Coordinates (age 12+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Coordinates (age 12+)” objective: Understand similarity as a relationship where one shape is an enlargement of another; construct similar shapes by enlargement with a given scale factor and centre, with and without coordinate grids.
subject: Mathematics

label: Area (age 8+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Area (age 8+)” objective: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft).
subject: Mathematics

label: Prime numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Prime numbers” objective: Know and use the vocabulary of prime numbers, prime factors, and composite numbers; establish whether a number up to 100 is prime; recall prime numbers up to 19.
subject: Mathematics

label: Gravity Pulls Things Down
statement: Demonstrate the “Gravity Pulls Things Down” objective: Understand gravity as a force that pulls objects towards the centre of the Earth, that 'down' means towards Earth’s centre regardless of where you stand on the sphere, and that gravity keeps the Moon orbiting Earth and planets orbiting the Sun.
subject: Science

label: Understanding Why
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding Why” objective: Go beyond knowing *that* something is true — ask *why* it is true and *how* it works.
subject: Learning to Learn

label: Spellings from Greek, French and Latin
statement: Demonstrate the “Spellings from Greek, French and Latin” objective: Spell words with etymological letter patterns from Greek (ch = /k/), French (ch = /ʃ/, -gue, -que), and Latin (sc = /s/) origins.
subject: English

label: Air Resistance & Friction
statement: Demonstrate the “Air Resistance & Friction” objective: Identify the effects of air resistance, water resistance, and friction, and understand that these forces act between moving surfaces to oppose motion.
subject: Science

label: Turns & Directions
statement: Demonstrate the “Turns & Directions” objective: Describe movement and direction, including whole, half, quarter, and three-quarter turns.
subject: Mathematics

label: Human impact on environments
statement: Demonstrate the “Human impact on environments” objective: Use vocabulary for human impact on the environment — pollution, habitat destruction, deforestation, biodiversity, conservation, renewable energy, non-renewable energy, fossil fuel, carbon footprint, sustainability, endangered, extinct — and apply these when discussing environmental issues and human choices.
subject: Science

label: Basic Nouns & Verbs
statement: Demonstrate the “Basic Nouns & Verbs” objective: Use frequently occurring nouns (people, places, things) and verbs (action words) appropriately in speech and writing.
subject: English

label: Listening to Others
statement: Demonstrate the “Listening to Others” objective: Listen to others when they are speaking — looking at the speaker, waiting until they finish, and showing they have heard by responding to what was said rather than just talking about their own ideas.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Bystanders and Upstanders
statement: Demonstrate the “Bystanders and Upstanders” objective: Understand the bystander role — that when someone witnesses unkind or unfair behaviour, they have a choice: they can be a passive bystander (doing nothing), join in, or be an upstander (speaking up or getting help) — and develop the confidence to be an upstander.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Sound Travels Through Materials
statement: Demonstrate the “Sound Travels Through Materials” objective: Recognise that vibrations from sounds travel through a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to the ear.
subject: Science

label: Earthquake-Resistant Design
statement: Demonstrate the “Earthquake-Resistant Design” objective: Know that buildings can be designed to resist earthquakes, tsunami warning systems alert coastal communities, and communities prepare through evacuation plans and drills.
subject: Science

label: Joints, Tendons & Ligaments
statement: Demonstrate the “Joints, Tendons & Ligaments” objective: Explain biomechanics — the interaction between skeleton and muscles at joints, including the roles of tendons (attach muscle to bone) and ligaments (attach bone to bone).
subject: Science

label: Equations with Two Unknowns
statement: Demonstrate the “Equations with Two Unknowns” objective: Find pairs of numbers that satisfy an equation with two unknowns (e.g. find pairs (a, b) where a + b = 10 or 2a + b = 15).
subject: Mathematics

label: 3-D shapes (age 5+)
statement: Demonstrate the “3-D shapes (age 5+)” objective: Analyse and compare 2-D and 3-D shapes using informal language to describe sides, vertices, and other attributes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Rocks and soil
statement: Demonstrate the “Rocks and soil” objective: Recognise that soils are made from rocks and organic matter, and that different soils have different properties.
subject: Science

label: Themes and messages
statement: Demonstrate the “Themes and messages” objective: Identify recurring themes (good vs evil, friendship, bravery) and conventions (once upon a time, moral at the end, hero's journey) across a wide range of books including fairy stories, myths, legends and traditional tales.
subject: English

label: Tables, charts, and graphs
statement: Demonstrate the “Tables, charts, and graphs” objective: Construct data tables with correct headings and SI units, plot appropriate graph types (bar chart, line graph, scatter graph), draw a line of best fit, and calculate the gradient of a straight-line graph.
subject: Science

label: Addition and subtraction word problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Addition and subtraction word problems” objective: Solve addition and subtraction word problems within 10 using objects or drawings.
subject: Mathematics

label: Ratio Notation and Relationships
statement: Demonstrate the “Ratio Notation and Relationships” objective: Understand that a multiplicative relationship between two quantities can be expressed as a ratio; use ratio notation; simplify ratios.
subject: Mathematics

label: Reading High-Frequency Words by Sight
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading High-Frequency Words by Sight” objective: Read common high-frequency and exception words automatically by sight, including words with irregular spelling patterns.
subject: English

label: Performing Scripts & Poetry
statement: Demonstrate the “Performing Scripts & Poetry” objective: Improvise, rehearse, and perform play scripts and poetry — using role, intonation, tone, volume, mood, silence, stillness, and action to generate language, explore meaning, and add impact to performance.
subject: English

label: Matter Is Made of Particles
statement: Demonstrate the “Matter Is Made of Particles” objective: Develop a model to describe that matter is made of particles too small to be seen, and that this explains properties of solids, liquids, and gases.
subject: Science

label: Sorting Data into Categories
statement: Demonstrate the “Sorting Data into Categories” objective: Organise and represent data with up to three categories by counting objects in each category and sorting categories by quantity.
subject: Mathematics

label: Writing Poetry
statement: Demonstrate the “Writing Poetry” objective: Write poetry, exploring patterns of language, rhyme and rhythm, and learning poems by heart for recitation with appropriate intonation.
subject: English

label: Egyptian Tomb Paintings and Artefacts
statement: Demonstrate the “Egyptian Tomb Paintings and Artefacts” objective: Use tomb paintings, artefacts, and objects from ancient Egypt as evidence to find out about daily life: Nebamun's tomb paintings show hunting and feasting, jewellery and furniture reveal craftsmanship, and everyday objects like pots and tools tell us what ordinary people used — understanding that these sources are how we piece together information about a civilisation that ended thousands of years ago.
subject: History

label: Sexual Selection
statement: Demonstrate the “Sexual Selection” objective: Explain sexual selection as a form of natural selection: runaway selection for peacock tails, bird of paradise displays, and frog calls; explain kin selection and altruistic behaviour — why worker bees die to protect the hive, why meerkats stand guard at personal risk (Hamilton's rule, inclusive fitness); introduce game theory in animal behaviour using the hawk-dove model; define cognitive ethology and survey evidence for animal emotions, play, and culture.
subject: Science

label: Plant & Animal Reproduction
statement: Demonstrate the “Plant & Animal Reproduction” objective: Describe the life process of reproduction in some plants and animals, including sexual and asexual reproduction in plants.
subject: Science

label: Light & Sound Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Light & Sound Vocabulary” objective: Name and use vocabulary for how light and sound behave — light source, transparent, translucent, opaque, shadow, reflect, vibration, pitch, volume — and apply these terms correctly when describing observations about how light travels and how sounds are made and changed.
subject: Science

label: Relative Clauses
statement: Demonstrate the “Relative Clauses” objective: Form and use relative clauses beginning with relative pronouns (who, whose, whom, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why) to add detail, qualify nouns, and create complex sentences.
subject: English

label: Counting objects to 20
statement: Demonstrate the “Counting objects to 20” objective: Count a set of objects to answer 'how many?' for sets up to 20 (arranged in lines, arrays, circles, or scattered).
subject: Mathematics

label: Solids, Liquids & Gases
statement: Demonstrate the “Solids, Liquids & Gases” objective: Compare and group materials as solids, liquids, or gases based on their observable properties and behaviour.
subject: Science

label: Real-World Mathematical Modelling
statement: Demonstrate the “Real-World Mathematical Modelling” objective: Model real-world problems involving ratio, scale, volume, unit conversion, and proportional reasoning with appropriate tools, diagrams, or equations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Common minibeasts: naming and recognising
statement: Demonstrate the “Common minibeasts: naming and recognising” objective: Recognising and naming common minibeasts: ladybird, ant, bee, butterfly, spider, snail, worm, woodlouse, caterpillar, beetle. Building positive attitudes toward all minibeasts, not just the 'pretty' ones.
subject: Science

label: Formal Debates
statement: Demonstrate the “Formal Debates” objective: Participate in formal debates and structured discussions — presenting a position with supporting evidence, responding to others’ points, summarising and building on what has been said, and following rules of discussion.
subject: English

label: Preparing for and Explaining in Discussions
statement: Demonstrate the “Preparing for and Explaining in Discussions” objective: Come to discussions prepared, draw on preparation and known information, and explain ideas in light of the discussion.
subject: English

label: Dinosaur Hip Groups
statement: Demonstrate the “Dinosaur Hip Groups” objective: Classify dinosaurs into the two major groups based on hip structure: Saurischia (lizard-hipped, including theropods and sauropods) and Ornithischia (bird-hipped, including Triceratops and Stegosaurus).
subject: Science

label: Conduction, convection, and radiation
statement: Demonstrate the “Conduction, convection, and radiation” objective: Describe and compare the three mechanisms of heat transfer — conduction (particle vibration through solids), convection (fluid movement in liquids/gases), and radiation (infrared waves) — and explain that the rate of transfer depends on temperature difference.
subject: Science

label: Nutrient Transport in Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Nutrient Transport in Animals” objective: Describe how nutrients and water are transported within animals, including the role of the circulatory system in delivering nutrients from digestion.
subject: Science

label: How Emotions Feel in Your Body
statement: Demonstrate the “How Emotions Feel in Your Body” objective: Understand the connection between emotions and the body — recognising physical signals like butterflies in the stomach (nervous), clenched fists (angry), racing heart (scared or excited), and tight shoulders (stressed).
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Ocean Animal Variety
statement: Demonstrate the “Ocean Animal Variety” objective: Recognise that the ocean is home to an amazing variety of animals — from tiny seahorses and colourful clownfish to enormous whales and sharks — and that ocean animals come in many shapes and sizes.
subject: Science

label: Two-Step Word Problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Two-Step Word Problems” objective: Solve one- and two-step word problems within 100 using addition and subtraction, with unknowns in all positions.
subject: Mathematics

label: Estimating Angles
statement: Demonstrate the “Estimating Angles” objective: Estimate and compare acute, obtuse, and reflex angles in degrees; classify angles by type and order them by size.
subject: Mathematics

label: Toxins Building Up in Food Chains
statement: Demonstrate the “Toxins Building Up in Food Chains” objective: Explain how organisms affect and are affected by their environment, including the bioaccumulation of toxic materials (e.g. pesticides, heavy metals) through food chains.
subject: Science

label: Fluent addition and subtraction (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Fluent addition and subtraction (age 9+)” objective: Fluently add and subtract whole numbers with more than four digits using the standard columnar algorithm.
subject: Mathematics

label: Estimating answers (age 13+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Estimating answers (age 13+)” objective: Use graphs of linear and quadratic functions to estimate output values for given inputs, find approximate solutions to equations, and interpret graphical information in real-world contexts.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Ocean Floor
statement: Demonstrate the “The Ocean Floor” objective: Know that the ocean floor is not flat — it has mountains, valleys, and the deepest trenches on Earth — and that the deepest point is the Mariana Trench, deeper than Mount Everest is tall.
subject: Science

label: Generating Sequences
statement: Demonstrate the “Generating Sequences” objective: Generate terms of a sequence from a term-to-term rule (e.g., 'add 3 each time') or a position-to-term rule (e.g., '2n + 1'), and identify whether a sequence is arithmetic, geometric, or neither.
subject: Mathematics

label: Joining Words with 'And'
statement: Demonstrate the “Joining Words with 'And'” objective: Join words and clauses using the conjunction 'and' to create longer sentences.
subject: English

label: Savanna & Grassland Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Savanna & Grassland Animals” objective: Explore animals of the grasslands and savanna — lions, zebras, wildebeest, elephants, cheetahs in African savanna; bison and prairie dogs in American grasslands — understanding why large herds form on open grasslands and how predators and prey interact in these wide-open spaces.
subject: Science

label: Tenths
statement: Demonstrate the “Tenths” objective: Count up and down in tenths; recognise that tenths arise from dividing an object into 10 equal parts and from dividing one-digit numbers or quantities by 10.
subject: Mathematics

label: Atoms, Elements & Compounds
statement: Demonstrate the “Atoms, Elements & Compounds” objective: Explain the differences between atoms, elements, and compounds; describe the simple Bohr model of the atom (nucleus with protons and neutrons, electrons in shells); and write and interpret chemical symbols and simple formulae.
subject: Science

label: Speaking Formally and Giving Presentations
statement: Demonstrate the “Speaking Formally and Giving Presentations” objective: Use Standard English confidently in formal and informal spoken contexts — give short speeches and presentations expressing own ideas clearly, keeping to the point, and adapting register and vocabulary to the audience.
subject: English

label: Apostrophes for possession
statement: Demonstrate the “Apostrophes for possession” objective: Use the possessive apostrophe with singular nouns to show ownership (e.g., the girl's book, the dog's bone).
subject: English

label: Simple Design Problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Simple Design Problems” objective: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time, or cost.
subject: Science

label: Algebraic Transformations
statement: Demonstrate the “Algebraic Transformations” objective: Model situations or procedures by translating them into algebraic expressions or formulae and by using graphs; move between word problems, algebraic representations, tables, and graphical representations.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Rock Cycle
statement: Demonstrate the “The Rock Cycle” objective: Understand the rock cycle: rocks slowly change from one type to another over millions of years — igneous rock weathers into sediment, sediment becomes sedimentary rock, heat and pressure create metamorphic rock, and melting starts the cycle again.
subject: Science

label: Self-Reflection in Relationships
statement: Demonstrate the “Self-Reflection in Relationships” objective: Reflect on their own role and behaviour in relationships — recognising patterns in how they interact with others, understanding what they contribute to friendships, and identifying areas where they could improve as a friend or team member.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Comparing Arctic & Antarctic
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing Arctic & Antarctic” objective: Compare the Arctic and Antarctic in detail — the Arctic is an ocean covered by floating sea ice with surrounding land masses (Canada, Russia, Greenland, Scandinavia), while Antarctica is a continent larger than Europe buried under ice up to 4 km thick; polar bears, Arctic foxes, and walruses live only in the Arctic while penguins, leopard seals, and albatrosses are found only in the Antarctic.
subject: Science

label: Naming Everyday Materials
statement: Demonstrate the “Naming Everyday Materials” objective: Identify and name a variety of everyday materials including wood, plastic, glass, metal, water, and rock.
subject: Science

label: Cultural Allusions and Word Meaning
statement: Demonstrate the “Cultural Allusions and Word Meaning” objective: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as used in literary texts, including understanding references to mythology and cultural allusions (e.g., Herculean, Achilles' heel).
subject: English

label: Body Temperature Regulation
statement: Demonstrate the “Body Temperature Regulation” objective: Explain how the human body detects and responds to environmental changes including temperature, including the role of the skin in temperature regulation (sweating, shivering, vasodilation, vasoconstriction).
subject: Science

label: Reciting Poetry
statement: Demonstrate the “Reciting Poetry” objective: Learn poems by heart and recite with appropriate intonation, adding visual displays to descriptions when appropriate, and producing complete sentences in spoken presentations.
subject: English

label: The Prefix un-
statement: Demonstrate the “The Prefix un-” objective: Spell words using the prefix un- to change meaning; understand that un- creates opposites or reverses actions.
subject: English

label: Evaporation and condensation
statement: Demonstrate the “Evaporation and condensation” objective: Name and use vocabulary for the water cycle — evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection, transpiration, water vapour, runoff, groundwater — and describe each stage of the cycle using these terms in the correct sequence.
subject: Science

label: Developed Informational and Explanatory Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Developed Informational and Explanatory Writing” objective: Write informative and explanatory texts that examine a topic and convey ideas clearly — organising information logically with headings and formatting, developing the topic with relevant facts, definitions, details, and quotations, and using precise vocabulary.
subject: English

label: Measuring mass and weight
statement: Demonstrate the “Measuring mass and weight” objective: Measure and begin to record mass/weight using non-standard and standard units.
subject: Mathematics

label: Multiplication and Division Word Problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Multiplication and Division Word Problems” objective: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities.
subject: Mathematics

label: Living Things Vocabulary
statement: Demonstrate the “Living Things Vocabulary” objective: Name and use vocabulary for what makes something living — alive, dead, never been alive, movement, nutrition, growth, reproduction, sensitivity, excretion — and apply these terms when classifying objects and explaining why plants and animals count as living things.
subject: Science

label: Recording Data
statement: Demonstrate the “Recording Data” objective: Gather and record data using simple methods such as tables, tally charts, and drawings to help answer questions.
subject: Science

label: The multiples of 10
statement: Demonstrate the “The multiples of 10” objective: Understand that the multiples of 10 (10, 20, 30 … 90) represent one to nine tens and 0 ones.
