subject: Mathematics

label: Romulus & Remus
statement: Demonstrate the “Romulus & Remus” objective: Know the Roman founding myth of Romulus and Remus — twin brothers abandoned as babies, raised by a she-wolf, who grew up to found the city of Rome — and understand that this is a legend the Romans told about how their city began.
subject: History

label: Star Brightness & Distance
statement: Demonstrate the “Star Brightness & Distance” objective: Support an argument that the apparent brightness of the sun and stars is due to their relative distances from Earth, understanding the sun is a relatively close star.
subject: Science

label: Classifying Materials
statement: Demonstrate the “Classifying Materials” objective: Plan and conduct an investigation to classify different kinds of materials by their observable properties.
subject: Science

label: Non-Fiction Text Features
statement: Demonstrate the “Non-Fiction Text Features” objective: Recognise different non-fiction text structures and features (headings, contents, glossary, index), understanding how texts are organised to present information.
subject: English

label: Reading fluently
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading fluently” objective: Read aloud books matched to phonic ability accurately and with growing fluency; reread familiar texts to build confidence, speed, and expression.
subject: English

label: Minibeast Habitats
statement: Demonstrate the “Minibeast Habitats” objective: Where minibeasts live: micro-habitats. Different minibeasts prefer different conditions — under logs (damp, dark), in soil (underground), on leaves (sunny), in pond water (wet). The idea that you find different creatures in different places.
subject: Science

label: Basic digital citizenship
statement: Demonstrate the “Basic digital citizenship” objective: Understand basic digital citizenship — being kind online, protecting personal information, recognising that people behind screens are real people with real feelings, and knowing what to do if something online makes them uncomfortable.
subject: Personal & Social Development

label: Choosing Maths Tools
statement: Demonstrate the “Choosing Maths Tools” objective: Select and use tools and representations strategically: choose between mental methods, formal written methods, algebraic approaches, coordinate grids, and technology based on the demands of the problem.
subject: Mathematics

label: Rapid earth changes
statement: Demonstrate the “Rapid earth changes” objective: Use information from several sources to provide evidence that Earth events can occur quickly (earthquakes, volcanic eruptions) or slowly (erosion, mountain building).
subject: Science

label: Comparing Capacity
statement: Demonstrate the “Comparing Capacity” objective: Compare and describe capacity and volume using language such as full, empty, more than, less than, half full.
subject: Mathematics

label: Converting measurement units (age 9+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Converting measurement units (age 9+)” objective: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system (km/m/cm/mm, kg/g, l/ml, hr/min/sec); convert between different metric units and express measurements in terms of a smaller unit; record equivalents in conversion tables.
subject: Mathematics

label: Communication with Light & Sound
statement: Demonstrate the “Communication with Light & Sound” objective: Design and build a device that uses light or sound to solve the problem of communicating over a distance.
subject: Science

label: Addition and subtraction word problems
statement: Demonstrate the “Addition and subtraction word problems” objective: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with like denominators, using visual models and equations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Retelling Stories with Structure
statement: Demonstrate the “Retelling Stories with Structure” objective: Retell stories including key details in sequence, describe characters, settings, and major events using evidence from the text, and describe the overall structure of a story (beginning, middle, ending).
subject: English

label: Photosynthesis
statement: Demonstrate the “Photosynthesis” objective: Explain photosynthesis as the process by which plants use light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen, and describe how mineral nutrients are absorbed through roots.
subject: Science

label: Rainforest Futures & Trade-Offs
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Futures & Trade-Offs” objective: Understand that the future of rainforests depends on balancing competing needs — economic development for local communities, indigenous peoples' rights to their ancestral lands, global biodiversity conservation, and climate stability — and that there are no simple answers, requiring cooperation between governments, businesses, scientists, indigenous leaders, and consumers worldwide.
subject: Science

label: Understanding Percentages
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding Percentages” objective: Understand the per cent symbol (%); know that per cent means ‘number of parts per hundred’; write percentages as a fraction with denominator 100 and as a decimal.
subject: Mathematics

label: Numbers on a number line
statement: Demonstrate the “Numbers on a number line” objective: Select and use appropriate tools and representations (number lines, hundred squares, rulers, part-whole models) to support problem-solving.
subject: Mathematics

label: Varying Sentence Structure
statement: Demonstrate the “Varying Sentence Structure” objective: Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader interest, and style, using techniques such as embedding clauses, using appositives, and varying sentence length.
subject: English

label: Understanding fractions
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding fractions” objective: Solve problems involving scaling by simple fractions and problems involving simple rates.
subject: Mathematics

label: Reading ×, ÷, and = Symbols
statement: Demonstrate the “Reading ×, ÷, and = Symbols” objective: Read, write, and interpret the symbols ×, ÷, and = in multiplication and division number sentences.
subject: Mathematics

label: AI and the Environment
statement: Demonstrate the “AI and the Environment” objective: AI needs huge amounts of energy and water to train; data centres and their environmental cost; but AI can also help — predicting weather, monitoring deforestation, optimising energy; trade-offs.
subject: Computing

label: How the Lungs Work
statement: Demonstrate the “How the Lungs Work” objective: Explain how the respiratory system works in detail: air travels through the nose/mouth, down the trachea, into bronchi and bronchioles, reaching tiny air sacs (alveoli) in the lungs where oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out.
subject: Science

label: Saving Money
statement: Demonstrate the “Saving Money” objective: Why people save money; piggy banks and saving jars; setting a savings goal; the idea that not spending now means having more later.
subject: Life Skills

label: Monitoring Volcanoes
statement: Demonstrate the “Monitoring Volcanoes” objective: Understand how volcanologists monitor volcanoes by looking for warning signs — gas emissions, ground swelling, small earthquakes — and that prediction involves evidence and uncertainty, not certainty.
subject: Science

label: Understanding angles (age 12+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Understanding angles (age 12+)” objective: Use ruler and compasses to perform standard constructions: perpendicular bisector of a line segment, perpendicular to a line from or at a given point, and bisecting an angle.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Reactivity Series
statement: Demonstrate the “The Reactivity Series” objective: Order common metals in the reactivity series and explain how a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one; describe how carbon is used to extract metals from their oxides in industry.
subject: Science

label: Calculating Simple Probability
statement: Demonstrate the “Calculating Simple Probability” objective: Calculate the probability of a simple event with equally likely outcomes using the formula: probability = number of favourable outcomes ÷ total number of possible outcomes; express the result as a fraction in its simplest form; apply to rolling dice, drawing from bags, and other simple chance situations.
subject: Mathematics

label: Subtraction as taking away or separating
statement: Demonstrate the “Subtraction as taking away or separating” objective: Understand subtraction as taking away or separating from a group to find how many remain.
subject: Mathematics

label: Angles in triangles (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Angles in triangles (age 7+)” objective: Recognise and draw shapes having specified attributes (e.g. a given number of angles or equal faces); identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes.
subject: Mathematics

label: Naming Common Animals
statement: Demonstrate the “Naming Common Animals” objective: Identify and name common animals from major groups: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals.
subject: Science

label: Rainforest Water Cycle
statement: Demonstrate the “Rainforest Water Cycle” objective: Understand how the water cycle works in a rainforest — trees absorb water through their roots and release it through their leaves (transpiration), this moisture forms clouds above the canopy, and the clouds produce rain that falls back into the forest — creating a self-sustaining cycle that generates much of the rainforest's own rainfall.
subject: Science

label: Adding Three Small Numbers
statement: Demonstrate the “Adding Three Small Numbers” objective: Add three one-digit numbers using strategies including looking for pairs that make 10.
subject: Mathematics

label: Evidence-Based Writing
statement: Demonstrate the “Evidence-Based Writing” objective: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research in writing, applying grade-level reading standards to non-fiction.
subject: English

label: Addition and subtraction strategies (age 7+)
statement: Demonstrate the “Addition and subtraction strategies (age 7+)” objective: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.
subject: Mathematics

label: The Crusades
statement: Demonstrate the “The Crusades” objective: A simplified account of the Crusades: why Europeans travelled to the Holy Land, what they found there, the cultural exchange between Christian Europe and the Islamic world.
subject: History
